is a small, ported-from-mobile game that is nonetheless very interesting. You "swipe" left and right (more on that in a moment) to perform decisions which will affect your kingdom. The land is represented by three groups, the Church, the people, and the army, with the last factor being your treasury. From a pure gameplay perspective, the difficulty comes from trying to balance all four "meters", because both too little and too much focus put into any of them leads to a game over. This is hard at first but after a while, you simply remember what each card and each decision do, and learn to act on them instinctively.
You may actually be surprised that there is a story to this game — a kind of meta-storyline that occurs in between the lives of your many monarchs. I don't want to spoil anything here but the game maneuvers very deftly between a funny and light-hearted atmosphere and something more horror-like.
The atmosphere in the game, by the way, is overall really great. The soundtrack features something like a medieval monk choir, the illustrations are simple but fantastic, and even the flavor text, anachronistic as it is, somehow manages to reflect, in a humorous and irreverent way, the realities of the middle ages.
The game, unfortunately, has some flaws, mostly related to the interface. The controls were clearly designed for touchscreens and just don't make as much sense in a desktop environment. Whilst they're nice when you get used to them, for all their simplicity they were surprisingly hard for me to figure out initially. The game offers very little in the way of explanation (of anything, really), so that didn't help. Also, scrolling feels sort of laggy for me.
(There is also the obvious fact that the game, even with its hundreds of cards, is rather small when compared to many other, especially mainstream games. I've seen some people complain about that in other reviews. You really should be able to tell what you're getting by looking at the screenshots and the description, and the price is entirely appropriate. Also, if you aspire to find out all the secrets this game has, it will still take you many hours.)

I mean, I don't believe there are many "gamers" who could honestly say they never played any timewaster mobile game. But still, there is a big distinction between the kind of video games one part of the population tends to find enjoyable and the kind that the other part prefers.

in that I could see it being enjoyed both by a casual gamer looking to occupy themselves waiting in a queue and by a mainstream gamer wanting some unusual storytelling.

Background: Bought for pennies in the steam sale, never heard of it before.
The Good:
* Brilliant premise, locations and characters
* Decent tutorial (does miss out a few useful hints)
* Tons of ghosts to play with with fun interactions
* Varied scenarios are brilliantly Scooby Do fun to explore
* Trial and error hauntings are both good and challenging
* Good balance between creepy and fun
* Fun voice acting on the ghosts, Sims mumbling from the humans
* Most missions are sub 30mins for quick diversions
* 20 hour campaign, some replay value
The Bad:
* Graphics are dated.. looking Sims 2-esque
* NPC Characters get hooked on the scenery, other glitches in pathing
* The ghost/human menu is clunky and could give better feedback
* Golden Plasm too easy to waste while learning the ropes
* Replay and Upgrade-mansion interfaces are more awkward than seems necessary
* Some hints on releasing bonus ghosts very vague
* Cries out for more direct control and visually targeted attacks
* Some scenarios have triggers you have no control over make the game too easy
Impressions: Some games look great but are boring, others the reverse, this is the latter. It reminds me of the Commandos crossed with Hitman and The Sims 2 games..  looks dated but the game play shines. The game lovingly tiptoes around remaking famous setups from horror movies (the Evil Dead one is great) without getting so close they get sued.
Recommended for: Strategy fans who like replay value and Sims fans who like to drown their vassals in ladderless pools.
Conclusion.: 8/10. A game that triumphs in mechanics over visuals.

I'm not familiar with these types of games so it took me a bit to get used to the controls. Once I got rolling it was a very enjoyable adventure, and I absolutely loved the storyline. Really looking forward to the other games in this franchise.
P.S. Shotguns are fun.

Theme & Goals:
The game is set in a forest (Duh) in the middle of nowhere. The only thing that inhabits this forest are cute little bunnies, squirrels lizards and other animals, and quite a large population of cannibal natives that will hunt you down and murder you.
Your goal is quite simple, survive for as long as possible and try to locate your son that was taken by the natives at the opening cinematic.
There are also side objectives such as locating each and every passenger that was on your flight.
The game is scary and interesting alone and even more so with friends online.
Gameplay Mechanics:
The game sports a rather well made crafting and building system with quite realistic requirements for each craftable/buildable item.
The combat feels a tad stiff but very satisfying.
Hunger, thirst and fatigue mechanics have a major roll in the game but are not overwhelming or feel like a chore to maintain in good condition, something that a lot of survival games are guilty of.
Performance & Graphics:
The game runs on the Unity engine and when I first saw the screenshots I had a hard time believing that a game running on Unity could look so gorgeous.
Don't let the amazing graphics fool you, The developers have clearly put a lot of time and effort into making this beautiful game run smooth as butter on any system (considering you meet the minimum requirements).
On my system I managed to squeeze 130 - 144 frames per second on the highest possible settings (1920x1080) with motion blur turned off (cause I don't like it).

Totally sold on this game. I got really burned out on League of legends and how it pretty much turned into a job trying to keep up with how the game is played. Evolve has enough strategy to make it have a lot of replay value, but each match offers enough reward to make even bad games worth it.  I have enjoyed playing both as monster and as the hunters. Each side offers their own distinct experiences. I often play one side for several matches and then switch to the other to spice things up.  The asymmetrical gameplay makes it a, generally, interesting experience.  I am really enjoying the exploration of how to play the game and becoming proficient at each class and monster.  Some are more appealing than other, but overall I enjoy playing them all.
Of course there are balancing issues, but TRS shows us how balanced WLR's are for each monster, and hunter and give us a lot of other information to be transparant about who is winning and with what abilities. When you see Kraken's WLR
go from 70% to 51% or so you know that they have done good balancing.
I have been impressed with how TRS (Turtle Rock Studios) has dealt with the community (I relagate the DLC debacle on 2k and even then I don't really care, its my money I'll spend it how I want).  This is a large plus for the game. TRS is very open about how they are making the game and what they are making.  I am excited to see how the game changes and grows under their leadership.
I think my main issue with the game is that games can end up being just a long chase to end up being killed by a full health, full armor monster.  These games are really no fun at all, but this is mostly a learning curve issue and less a design issue.
I see a lot of similarities to MOBAs and feel right at home in Evolve. There is a high learning curve, but a lot of pay off to learning how to play.  People have their issues with paid DLC, but games like League of Legends has a very similar system.  Get a good group of friends and jump in its a blast.

It is unfortunate that I even need to say this, but: I am not interested, whatsoever, in becoming involved in the politics and lobbying of opinions that revolve around this game. I am just going to describe my experience with it and my opinion about it, and offer a suggestion of consideration to anyone who is interested.
So I stumbled across
in my backlog, and I will admit that there was an influence of brand recognition due to the circus that surrounds the game. Perhaps without which, I would still have yet to even try it. Regardless, I was curious about it so I checked it out and played it for a few hours one night.
It was a fun evening. The game isn’t some insanely life-changing experience, but it is entertaining and has a nice novelty about it. I hadn’t played anything quite like it. You can surely have a fun few hours playing it; I know I did.
It is extremely and purposefully simple, and there are very little controls or mechanics. This minimalist approach to the gameplay creates a scenario which allows the game to evoke a strong sense of helplessness and anxiety in the player. You really can’t do much, but that is the point. And even with the opening disclaimer about jump-scares, I got “got” a good 2-3 times by them as I played that night. I liked it.
Overall, there isn’t much to it. The game is short, the graphics are ugly, the mechanics are minimal, etc.
isn’t anything overtly special, but it also isn’t excessively terrible… it just is what it is. It’s like horror movies; they usually aren’t anyone’s all-time favorite, but they can be fun for a night.
So if we can put aside the trolling that surrounds this game for a moment, and speak logically: you will likely find
is an entertaining experience that will definitely appeal to horror buffs and casual gamers, but can also easily be enjoyed by a wide range of gamers. That said, if you are one of those people who believes only the most top-shelf, A-one, premium games “deserve” to be played, you should probably just stay clear. For everyone else: don’t expect the second coming of Jesus Christ, but also don’t expect some unbearably awful experience… just expect a few hours of cheap thrills and then to move on with your life. If that sounds cool with you, then consider checking this out.

This is one of very few creative works to have so drastically changed my feelings on a subject.  It is not easy to parse, nor enjoyable to play, and it left me feeling like I needed to rethink my whole life.  This game is certainly not for everyybody, but if you are the kind of person who believes they come to know an artist through their art, or are someone who sustains their own ego by collecting and showcasing the art of other people, maybe do yourself a painful favour and take a couple hours to play this 'game'.

Black Rose offers an experience that defies my expectations of steam's offerings in the horror genre.  Despite the limited resources of a single developer, he managed to put together a gruesomely intriguing storyline with a compelling atmosphere.  There are some fairly typical game design errors that even big studios make (continuity errors, overuse of tropes, empty deadend rooms, etc.  The graphics aren't very impressive either.  Regardless of these issues, the game as a whole is a purchase I highly reccomend.  Price and time in consideration, 8.5/10.

I am glad to see that my old favourite, Ghost Master has made it onto Steam.
Now, the best way to describe this game is "The Sims: Inverted". Instead of  having a bunch of Sims, you have to keep happy and well off, you have a cadre of Ghosts that only exist to keep your puny humans in a state of fear and madness.
Now, this game is far from perfect: Many Ghost skills lack a precise description, that explain their exact workings, some levels are overly puzzly and if you don't install a trainer, you can't revisit previous levels with unlocked ghosts.
Many reviews also complain about the fact that humans are eradic and difficult to herd.
Personally, I think that this is a rather realistic depiction of people, under the influence of ghosts.
Now, with all those factors: Is the game still fun?
Yes! A lot!
It is all about set up and delivery.
Calling a bunch of humans into the same room and then springing your best frightener on them is incredibly statisfying. Seeing them run around, driven insane by your phantasm is really funny and using different kinds of frighteners in different situations is really great.
There are a ton of small touches, like the descriptions of the humans, that are both funny and may inform you off their unique weaknesses or the desperate and endearing yells of your ghosts, if they ghet exorcised or captured.
If you are a person who enjoys to manipulate and overlook, but "The Sims" is just not malevolent enough for you, go and give this gem a try!

Iron Fisticle takes many retro elements and jams it into one fun-sized package. Perhaps a game you’d spend a few hours playing.
- Movement and shooting feels fluid and responsive.
- Decent variety of weapon and item drops. Makes killing enemies more dynamic.
- Collect food items to improve your score. You receive a multiplier bonus if you collect them in quick succession. I believe this adds to the replayability and compliments the retro point/leader board grading system.
- If you take too long to leave a room, very resilient enemies spawn to try to force you out. Not sure why this was included in the game, but I thought it was a clever touch.
- Fun bonus minigame. No real punishment for failing, but you get the opportunity to collect more gold. It’s a cute and refreshing break from all the twin shooting.
- Co-op option is nice. Very glad they included this feature.
- You can buy permanent upgrades during your playthroughs that will carry on when you start a new life. I am somewhat torn about this feature. On one hand, it gives you a feeling of progression although you start again after each death. On the other hand, once you are sufficiently powered up, the beginning of the dungeon becomes dull as it is too easy.
- The main difficulty in this game comes from fighting large numbers of enemies simultaneously. There is a decent number of different enemies, but not enough to keep this game entertaining for very long.
Overall, Iron Fisticle is a fun time waster. The game is not spectacular, but is well executed. The only reason I don’t recommend Iron Fisticle is because

, the sequel, is out for the same price. It is essentially an improved version of Iron Fisticle.

LIMBO is a 2D puzzle platformer. I haven't really paid much attention to the game and just got into it recently. It pays homage to games of old with it's simplistic style yet engaging content through it's simplicity.
Pros:
+ The controls are nice and feels intuitive. It's kinda fast paced but doesn't force you to do ridiculous jumps all the time like other platformers which make you rely solely on reaction time and memorizing routes though you might need to in order to finish the achievement of not dying more than 5 times in a single timed playthrough.
+ The soundtrack consists mostly of ambient noise and fragments of something that sounds like a song here and there. I enjoy it myself, being in this shadowy world that's completely in silence really helps to build up the atmosphere. Sometimes the music gets louder, sometimes it's in complete silence. Really takes you into an almost movie like setting.
+ Perhaps the thing I love the most about this game. The visuals; The whole world is black and white, with some kind of mist in the background. The characters are nothing but mere shadows, even the protagonist is a kid shrouded in shadows with just his eyes glowing. The world is gorgeous in a depressing way, after all, you're in Limbo. Forests, industrial areas, caves, lakes, even something that looks like a city. Rain pours down on you at some point, and it's nice and soothing. I really like the art style of this game. It's kinda gory too, your character can die in a wide array of painful deaths. Some are quite gory. Still, it's all in black and white, you'll see the shadows of your intestines.
+ The world itself. This might count towards the visuals, though. This game is quite somber, and really atmospheric. You're adventuring into the unknown, and you'll find all kinds of weird stuff along the way. You'll find corpses all around, some of them suicide victims. Even the living beings in Limbo are hostile towards you. It truly is a cold and unforgiving world.
Neutral:
+/- This game gets quite challenging later on. This might be a con for some, a pro for others. Personally, I enjoy it myself. You simply can't finish this game without dying quite a few times on the first run, because the game changes its rules at times, teases you, punishes you for taking the "easy" route. Sometimes, deaths are swift and gory, with less than a second to react. This game is a lot of trial and error, just like you'd expect from a game like this.
-/+ Another pro for some, con for others. This game is quite short. Puzzles are time consuming, and I dare to say, frustrating often, especially near the end of the game. You can easily finish this game in a couple of hours.
Cons:
- Lack of story. I won't tell you exactly what happens near the end, but you might not like it if you were expecting something amazing to happen. The journey was worth it for me, but the ending felt kinda weak.
TL;DR:
7.5/10
All in all, I would recommend picking this game up in a sale. If you are into puzzle/platformer games this is quite an interersting title, especially coming from an indie game. The visuals and ambience alone are worth it for me, and the game's short enough for me to avoid giving up in frustration before completing it.

Evolve had my eye from about a year from release date. My initial thoughts were that this looked like a unique take on the first person shooter genre and coop as well. As most games Evolve had the potential for one of two fates, be a total let-down or a complete success. Fast forward to February 10th 2015.
After one "Big-Alpha" event and another open beta event we now have the finished product. My opinion? Evolve is an outstanding game that delivers an experience that hasn't been dealt to the gaming community in quite some time. As said before, the game could have flopped. There were great potentials for horrible balance between hunters & monsters, bad optimization, and countless others. These issues however are not present. The balance is superb and every class plays a vital role in each match.
I commend Turtle Rock Studios for making a game that I personally will be playing for quite some time along with some other friends who enjoy Evolve as well. Limbo
Played on PC (Using an Xbox One controller)
Reviewed 02/09/2017
Purchased ($1.79 in a bundle)
Spoilers Warning
First thing is first.  Limbo is a side scrolling platformer with light puzzle elements.  You have no way of directly fighting anything and the game is all about surviving and making it to the next part.  There are no lives in Limbo and when you die you start back almost exactly where you just perished.  With persistence you will figure out what the game wants and progress along.
I very much enjoyed the visual aesthetics of Limbo.  The entire game is a silhouette with black and white defining most everything.  The effect is particularly effective in the main character.  A small boy who is completely silhouette in black except for his white eyes.  Because of the huge contrast between his body (pitch black) and his eyes (bright white) the eyes are remarkably expressive.  Even though he never says a thing, and we never learn anything about him or his horrible world I feel that I almost know his personality just from his blinking and his eye movements in general.  I consider that a pretty remarkable feat.  This light and dark effect also does a great job of setting the mood.  There is trepidation as you enter entirely dark caves and hope as the light welcomes you when you come out on the other side.  Darkness representing all the hazards you must overcome along the way, and light as you hope this little kid makes it through them all.  So in terms of art direction, and visual style I very much enjoyed Limbo.
The game doesn’t really have music.  Instead it has atmospheric sounds.  They work very well and really help set the mood.  This is the type of game where you do not want to play it while listening to your own music or with a tv in the background.  While playing definitely immerse yourself in the complete atmosphere the game gives you.

As stated above I really enjoyed the entire visual and audio direction Limbo went with.  Gameplay on the other hand is a different story.  The game is a history test and nothing more.  Cheap death following cheap death following cheap death.  You enter a new area, get killed until you figure out what the game wants you to do and then you do it.  None of the puzzles in the game are all that difficult, with the longest taking me maybe ten minutes.  Trying to figure the puzzles out is not an intellectual exercise.  More often than not it really is just keep dying till you do what the game wants.  That is complemented by a complete lack of a learning curve.  At no point during my four hour playthrough did I feel that I was getting better at the game.  At the beginning I was just dying till I figured out what the game wanted, and at the end I still just dying till I figured out what the game wanted.  I did die more at the end of the game then at first, but that is because the game is more mean spirited not because it was actually any harder.  Again, infinite lives and you respawn almost exactly where you died.
Limbo is normally $10, under no circumstances do I feel it is worth that price.  As stated above I got it during a steam sale and as part of a bundle.  Limbo itself was only $1.79 for me.  Honestly, I couldn’t imagine spending any more than $5 for it.
Visually I think Limbo is brilliant, but everything else just left me disappointed.
Score: Disappointing
How my scoring works: Most reviewers assign a numerical score to things.  This doesn’t really make sense to me.  If one game has an 8.5 and another has an 8 is one really better than the other?  Or is it just the mood of the reviewer at that time?  Are we talking about a meaningful differences?  Is a 8 really that much worse than an 9?  To me there is virtually no difference between these scores.  There are just too many dividing lines.  Now I get that In any review system you need tiers but to me you want as few tiers as possible.  I seriously considered just having “reccomend/Skip” as my system, but decided that that was to vague to be of much value to anyone.  That would combine outstanding games and just ok games under “reccomend”  So instead My scores are:
Amazing
Good
Disappointing
Terrible
Yes, if something is given a “good” score you could say I gave it a 3 out of 4 but that really what i’m going for.  Why convert a descriptive thing like good into something abstract like a number?

This is not a game for people who hate repetitive goals, but then again, the CoD franchise is successful.
First: The Game

The game is fun. It has three characters per role, including the monster. Each character has their own unique playstyle, which allows for around 24 unique combinations for matches.  There are also currently 12 maps, which increases the amount of unique games to 284 combinations for the basic Hunt mode.
Two gamemodes, Hunt and Evacuation. Hunt is simple, kill monster or kill hunters until time runs out or the generator is destroyed. Evacuation has Nest, Defend, Hunt, and Rescue game modes that players can choose from between a 5 game campaign. Each map gives a unique perk to the winner, and the losers get a handicap buff.
Second: Graphics    10/10, the game is beautiful. The maps look alike in color because they are all around an island-like region, just like a real continent or island would be.
Third: DLC  -  **COMPLETELY COSMETIC THUS FAR***
Yes, they are selling skins. Completely cosmetic. Do not effect gameplay. Hunter skins are $1.99 per skin, with $4.99 packs for 3 hunters of that class. Monster skins are $2.99, and have a $6.99 bundles for all 3 monsters for that skin category.
Fourth: Future DLC
Maps are free, and will always be free.  New hunters are $7.49 each, Monsters are $14.99 each. You don't need to buy these characters to play with or against them. They are also not necessary.
Fifth: Bugs/Server
New IP, hackers are getting into it, but the devs are working on fixing this situation. These hackers are rare, I haven't seen one my entire time playing since Alpha, Beta, Press release, and post-launch.  There are some bugs, but devs are also working on this. Every game has bugs. get over it.
Overall:  Fun game, worth the $60 for the PC Monster Race edition. It has it's flaws, but the core idea is fresh enough to keep me playing for a long time.

BioShock [PS3 - Steam - Xbox 360]: 7.3/10
Advertised as a "horror" shooter game, and I quote, "unlike any shooter you've ever played," (Steam) BioShock came out with immediate critical acclaim and praised as the holy messiah of shooters or at least 2007 shooters. No matter where you look it seems like this game gets 9/10's from IGN, Metacritic, etc. But since I'm not a tool I wasn't as utterly impressed as they were and I'm having trouble justifying some of the flaws for this game as they are so blatant. Of course, this game isn't bad, it's great in fact, but you have to wonder whose♥♥♥♥♥♥IGN and the lot were sucking: commissioned reviews or the "new IPs should be encouraged" spirit.
The game starts off with your character, a schizophrenic psychopath, fantasizing about his mommy and daddy as he rubs his thumb over their picture for half a second and then immediately looks at their present he plans to give to him. (In retrospect, considering the twist, I have to wonder why the present here even exists.) As fate would ♥♥♥♥ing have it, the plane crashes into the ocean immediately after. (Again in retrospect, considering the twist, why the ♥♥♥♥ would the plane crash of all the things you could've had happen. Seems a bit risky.) After swimming to the tower the plane crashed in front of, you enter. And for some stupid reason, you don't decide to try to find a phone or wait for a boat, you immediately descend the terrifying stairwell into God-knows-what. Enter Rapture: the steam-punk, 1940s obsessed, underwater hellhole where you'll be spending your next 11 hours.
So as you already know, the game is a shooter. Or rather, it's a shooter and a brawler, because the wrench is the weapon you'll probably be using the most. You will also gain super powers which you have to purchase by doing horrible things to little girls, or by doing nice things to little girls. According to the game, doing horrible things to little girls will reward you more, but it doesn't really. You pretty much get all you need by doing the nice thing and getting the "best" ending.
Protecting the little girls from your reign of terror/messiahness are the Big Daddies, which are essentially the poster child of the game's enemies. Apparently these things are supposed to be the most terrifying things here, as far as I can tell, but they're not really. They aren't really hard to kill and worst yet they don't attack you unless you attack them. I kind of like this aspect as much as it doesn't make sense because while I don't like getting my face drilled in I don't understand why these things wouldn't try to kill everything considering everything is trying to kill them.
The weapons in the game are quite good but are kind of messy. You will never hate reload time as much as you will in this game, let me tell you. You're going to be constantly barraged by ♥♥♥♥ing enemies or those goddamn machines so you'll want to use a specific weapon with a specific bullet type but you also want to be conservative and nothing frustrates me more. Other than your typical real weapons you have super powers, and I wish these things were more useful. Only a couple of these powers will actually kill enemies, but they usually only stun the ♥♥♥♥ing things or chip off some of their health.
Your powers require some neon juice that you inject into your arm without actually knowing what it is and no one tells you to do so (again, schizophrenic psycho), which means you're limited somewhat. But not really, because health drops and money are ♥♥♥♥ing littered across the place like a tornado passing through after destroying an American hospital. You will also need to replenish your health once you get low, but unlike your power gauge, you have to replenish it manually. Why wouldn't he just do it automatically? Throughout the game there are these chambers that you are revived in if you die, but I only relied on those because I didn't press the F button in time.
The hacking in the game is consistently easy as ♥♥♥♥. I think I only failed to do it 3 times. Well, genuinely anyway. Often times the ♥♥♥♥ing things will generate a hacking puzzle that literally could not be solved. ♥♥♥♥ing fair isn't it? Thankfully you can use automatic hacking machines so you don't have to do the puzzle as long as you have one.
Probably one of the most annoying things in the game are the ♥♥♥♥ing alarm systems. If you get caught by a security camera for more than a second you'll have to spend up to a minute fighting off an endless amount of flying turrets, and this happens so often. It doesn't add any real challenge to the game, it's just ♥♥♥♥ing annoying.
One of the best features is, in my opinion, the upgrades. When you save or kill little girls, you can buy upgrades to your powers and abilities. There are so many of them, some useless but most useful. I just don't understand why the hell they wait so long before allowing me to buy more slots for plasmids.
Suppose I should talk about the actual gameplay now that I talked about all the different things you do. The gameplay is pretty great, it's not that satisfying to kill things but it's still somewhat enjoyable. Moving around, at least when the game isn't ♥♥♥♥ing with you, is enjoyable and smooth, and switching between weapons and powers isn't that bad though needs some work.
The worst part about the game is how it drags on and on about 4 more hours than it should have. The latter portion of the game is stretched so paper thin that it grew tiresome and pathetic. After you form an allegiance with little girls you're forced to do various things I'd consider artificial game lengtheners, all the while dealing with the most annoying parts of the games like the turrets, cameras, and those ♥♥♥♥ing stupid electric trip wires. Before you can fight the boss, you have to do a fetch quest (which includes a stupid amount of backtracking, if you need me to get something why not tell me to get it before I'm five miles away?), another fetch quest (through what seems to be some ♥♥♥♥ing maze), and you have to protect a ♥♥♥♥ing little girl while she pointlessly leads you to 3 corpses so she can stab with a needle for no reason and eventually lead you to the boss.
The boss is so goddamn bland. He's just a big mutated brute who will enable you and toss you aside, and you just need to wait a second or two before you can attack him. He's a joke, especially if you saved your electric gel like I did.
The "best" ending was ♥♥♥♥ing dumb. All you get for your troubles is a 30 second cutscene about how the uncanny-valley little girls who've annoyed you throughout the game get to grow up and live happy lives. Good for them, but the escort mission gave me a negative stigma against them. So now I regret not ripping the adam out of them just for satisfaction.
I've never played such a good game with so many imperfections. You'd think that I'd give this game a score of at most a 6 considering all the complaints I have. But hear me out, the game is still a lot of fun and worth your time. It's a lot of fun going through the first 6 hours of the game, and I admire just how quickly the game lets you jump into it. No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, just get into the game and beat♥♥♥♥♥♥up with your wrench. The atmosphere is great, and I loved listening to all of the tapes you find (even though the game makes it a ♥♥♥♥ing challenge to listen to all of them). I just hate how the game didn't end when it should've, the last 5 hours were kind of horrible and filled with the worst parts of the game. Even those hours were fun enough to get through, but those hours are the most frustrationg parts.
It's a good game, good enough to be replayed in the future. I recommend it if you were a Nintendo baby and one of the few who never played it like I was.

Wow. I can't explain how this game had made me feel. Such an elaborate, yet concise way to look into one person's mind to understand what they go through and how we alone, are unable to help.  People are not problems to be solved, they are to be loved, valued, and understood.
What's remarkable about The Beginners Guide, is that it actually asks you to think: To look outside of what's in front of you and come to terms with the creator as well as the narrator. Whether $10 was worth it is debatable, but it's not ultimately my concern. We can't extract our entire value from some person. Our true value is not determined by them, and nor is their value determined by us. We are not enough. When we make comparisons or judgements, it reveals no long term benefits. I agree that it's a natural attitude that we can all have as humans who have the ability to choose their words and actions. But we can never choose the consequences of those decisions.
What does it mean to be human, a person who is valued, loved, cherished? What does it mean to know a person to whom your goal is to always help them choose what's best for them? And yet love them regardless of their decision?
Who can say that they can love people out of themselves so well, that regardless of their choices, they never change their mind about them?
There's only one person who will never stop loving all people, and I believe many of you may already know who that is. He lived on earth for 30+ yrs, understanding us from our level. He spent his last 3 yrs as a teacher, healer and miracle worker, always speaking the truth of His Father, from whom He came to show His love that can never be matched, by dying and then by rising again to prove who he is and to give a solution to human frailty. A relationship with Himself. The One who will always and forever knows what's best for you. All it takes is trust.
In conclusion, I definitely recommend this game for it's personal story and emotional theme to bring one's mind into another perpective.

When I first opened this game, I thought that I was ready for any role. I hop into a game as the Americans pushing up the beaches of Iwo Jima. A flamethrower is open, so I chose it, thinking that it'd be more fun than a rifleman. I rush up the first part, free of enemies, with my comrades rallying together on all sides of me. We get over the hill and a wall of bullets flies our way, whizzing past me as I serpentine to a nearby crater. I crouch for cover and check my surroundings to see that only 5 of the 20 people that was around me had made it with me to this crater. Three are patching themselves while another stumbles around and bleeds out slowly from a gutshot. The fourth clears the barbed wire in front of our crater with a satchel charge. The Japs are focused on other soldiers as we try to run up to their trench. The engineer was in front of me and body-blocked a rifle shot for me. Another friend takes out the guy who shot him while I wiped my friend's blood off of me. We all dive to the ground as a mounted MG starts firing on us and we spend the next two minutes crawling up to the trench. Once there, I sprayed the entire trench without looking and hopped over once the bullets stopped. First, I felt satisfied...until I saw their charred bodies still twisting and turning from my flames. I stood in shock in the trench as I realized just how much suffering I caused, as evident from their blood-curdling screams. My SL screams out "Sniper! Get Down!" just as I fall to the ground after seeing the sniper's scope glint. I fell down staring into the eyes of a charred Jap with embers still going on his peeling skin. I left the game and went to sleep. That night, I had nightmares of the event previously described. I woke up sweating and still haven't picked up that class since that night.
10/10 would get PTSD for a night again

I've only been playing for not even a day and yet I'm already enthralled in the game. Probably what sets this apart is the fact that it's fresh, clean, and crisp. It's not some cheap knock-off. The GUI and gameplay is very user friendly so you don't have to spend an hour and a half trying to figure out where the hell is what you're looking for. The beginning of the game is very flowing and doesn't suddenly drop a lot of concepts onto you rapidly like a lot of others do. It is a game that is simple enough for gamers who are new to the MMO to easily get into while still having enough to draw experianced players in. In short, these are the reasons to give it a shot.
- It's brand new. Join the fun early and play as new content develops instead of trying to catch up.
- It's for friggen free! Who doesn't love free?
- The graphics and art is of good quality and yet not too much where it causes lag. Even my ordinary laptop can run it smoothly at 17 FPS.
- Character customization. You can add/subtract height in body and legs which allows you to freely control your size as well as your face. Make it look like you if you want.
- It has a great GUI that's easy to grasp even for new MMO players.
- The community is great. I haven't seen any super "hard core" gamers that bash the newer casual players yet. If anything, they're a life saver. If someone of a signifigantly higher level tells you to do something, do it. You'll thank them later. Also because it's a new game, there are loads of new players that you can partner up with right at the beginning.
- Minx had recently done a playthrough with the game on Youtube to give you an idea of what it looks like.
-The skills have good synergy. They actually put in skills that compliment eachother if you play smart.
- Each class branches off into two sub-classes early in the game. A warrior for example can branch early in the game to be either a protector which is a defence-heavy class to tank for friends, or a beserker to go all out and chop enemies into two. Two players of the same class does not nessisarily mean they play in the same way.
Note that there are areas specifically designed for you to grind in, and as such is highly recommended. The goblin camp is the first place to grind in and you'll find that soon.
One thing I think the developers could've done was make a male and female avatar for each class. Currently, there are five classes; two of which are male and the other three are female. As a man, it was dissapointing to see my favorite playstyle (mage) be only usable with a female avatar. I am sure it is the same way for women who love playing as warriors or rouges. For men who would rather not play as women, we're stuck with either playing as a warrior or a rouge. I'd very much like to see a male and female for each class evenly. Another thing is gaving to set up an Aria account but you'll run into that in the launcher and it's fairly quick and easy. Other than that, it's a great game that's freash out of the gates and just waiting for new content.

After purchasing this game, I was unable to actually play it. Every time I tried to start it up, it went to a white screen and crashed. I became extremely confused and felt at a loss of 5 dollars, although it's not the money, it's the principle of the matter. Why sell a game that simply will not work? To my surprise, I was not the only one who had ran into this problem. Upon various hours of searching, and attempts to get the game to work, the only option (and very last) was to contact steam support about the problem and recieve a refund. I had then felt discouraged to do so after reading multiple comments from people complaining that steam will not contact them nor deal with the matter.
There are no words to describe the disappointment I felt at the time but I did not yet feel defeated, I wanted to know why.
the next day later, after reading more about what others have experienced and what they had done to fix the problem, I finally found the answer. There was nothing that needed to be done to the game but search in the folders and start the game from in the "Ghost data" folder, then starting the game by clicking "ghost". You must also have an internet connection and have steam open before starting the game. All along the problem was the game wasn't going to load unless it had a CD to run from. In order to play the game, you must manually dig thorugh your folder. This complaint is not towards the game as it works perfectly fine and is very entertaining and I do reccoment it. I am dissatisfied with steam for selling a game that is not in proper working order and for never dealing with the constant requests for help.

Two hours worth of content- if that- to be told "hey, get your friends to buy this game," an endless mode (that you've probably exhausted in twenty minutes trying to exert the illusion of choice on the final level), the ability to replay levels (prolly take you half the time to do this time around) and some challenge mode.
Don't get me wrong, the game is neat. The aesthetic is nice, gameplay handles well, replays look cool when done right. But every level is about the size of a small apartment unit, there's maybe only four ways to handle any conflict, the plot's kind of spastic (and a little abusive), and any sense of closure you get is actually, and I kid you not, literally telling you to tell your friends to buy the game.
I was perhaps a little harsh in my first assessment, though- Levels are fun enough to repeat a few times, there's a few secret this-and-thats to find and/or unlock, the extra widgets outside of the main game itself are marginally neat if you're not expecting anything, yadda yadda. You can milk the two hours of content pretty far if you're a completionist or achievement hunter.

SUPERHOT is a great game, don't get me wrong. But with the price at $25 and the very lacking amount of content I could not recommend this game for any more than $10. Lets discuss some of the topics.
GRAPHICS:
I think the graphics are nice. They are kind of a ripoff of mirror's edge but at least it gives you the information you need. It is very polygonal which can look pretty ugly in some people's eyes. The environment uses the exact same concrete looking white texture, even on vehicles. The bullets are tiny and colored black making them difficult to detect when they are coming at you straight on. It is annoying to be killed from behind. It is hard to tell how big your hitbox is. Your character is black, which is the exact same color for all of the weapons (and bullets). So, it is hard to distinguish your hands, from weapons, to bullets. If I were to be the director for the graphics design, I would make SUPERHOT a third person shooter. Your character is yellow, so are bullets. These simple changes could really make a difference.
STORY:
Or lack of, I should say. There is a story, but it is complete and utter garbage. It is not interesting. The game developers think it is clever to force you to try to exit to the main menu when you can't, force you to quit the game in order to play again, and say "You are out of control" or "We are watching".  I won't spoil anymore of it, but trust me, it is not good.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay is the main focus of this game. I think they did a good job. It is satisfying to dodge a dozen bullets and proceed to punch someone in the face.The game is fairly bug free. I think I've experienced 1 crash. The throwing physics can be inconsistant and throwing an object directly at a dude sometimes just deflects off of their manly chest, but other than that it is fine. I already adressed some of my issues with gameplay in my "GRAPHICS" topic, but there is still more I want to talk about.
CONTROL:
Unlike basically every first person shooter, SUPERHOT is best played with a gamepad of all things! You can walk more precisely instead of having to jump around like a lunatic or tap the movement keys over and over again, you are limited in how fast you can move your camera so you don't accidentally waste time, and it is more accessable to people who don't know how to game with a keyboard. But the main problem with using a controller is that you can't even change the controls!!!!!! Left trigger is jump for some strange reason and B is throw. Jumping wasn't even a mechanic in the original! Why have it on left trigger? To throw something you have to take your hand off the anologue stick. Also, slightly tilting the anologue stick allows you to make time move slowly but still allow you to move at full speed. If only the developers made it so that moving the anologue stick less or more changes your speed proportional to time so there is still some tension and encouragement to move at full speed.
CONTENT:
I have already said this before, and I'll say it again. SUPERHOT is VERY lacking in content. The gameplay is simplistic, which is intentional, but the problem is it ruins replay value. You just shoot, then throw your gun and punch a dude. Another problem is the fact that I can count every weapon in the game with ONE HAND!!! There are only THREE guns, a few melee weapons that are identical other then asthetic, a katana, and a bunch of throwing weapons that are identical in every way other than size. (I have twelve fingers) The campaign can be completed in 2 hours counting all of the unskippable "story" segments. Once you complete the campaign you can play it again but with different mutators like katana only or fists only or throwing items only.... Yeah like as if the gameplay wasn't simple enough. There is also an endless mode where you replay levels from the campaign but there are infinitely spawning bad guys. This can become VERY tiring and you can tell the game wasn't intended for this kind of gameplay. Some of the levels from endless mode suck too. The gameplay barely varies even with the mutators. If I were a gameplay director, I would add more then 3 god damn guns. In a first person SHOOTER there aren't many ways to shoot a guy. Even if the weapons don't vary too much, at least it gives you something else to look at and a slight variation on gameplay. I would also add more environments because many people agree there aren't enough.
CONCLUSION:
All in all, it is a good game and worth a buy so long as you buy it at around 10$. Hey, I enjoyed playing SUPERHOT. How could I not enjoy it if I played it for 20 hours total? Even though some of that time was watching unskippable cutscenes, looking at the fake chat room, letting my friend play (yes, I have friends), and having the game open while I was doing something else. I probably played this game for much longer than most people. And also, thank you for reading this review! I hope it helped or will help you make a decision on weither you will purchase this game or not. Hey maybe you get enough enjoyment in watching others play. It is a pretty similar experience to be honest....

Limbo
Played on PC (Using an Xbox One controller)
Reviewed 02/09/2017
Purchased ($1.79 in a bundle)
Spoilers Warning
First thing is first.  Limbo is a side scrolling platformer with light puzzle elements.  You have no way of directly fighting anything and the game is all about surviving and making it to the next part.  There are no lives in Limbo and when you die you start back almost exactly where you just perished.  With persistence you will figure out what the game wants and progress along.
I very much enjoyed the visual aesthetics of Limbo.  The entire game is a silhouette with black and white defining most everything.  The effect is particularly effective in the main character.  A small boy who is completely silhouette in black except for his white eyes.  Because of the huge contrast between his body (pitch black) and his eyes (bright white) the eyes are remarkably expressive.  Even though he never says a thing, and we never learn anything about him or his horrible world I feel that I almost know his personality just from his blinking and his eye movements in general.  I consider that a pretty remarkable feat.  This light and dark effect also does a great job of setting the mood.  There is trepidation as you enter entirely dark caves and hope as the light welcomes you when you come out on the other side.  Darkness representing all the hazards you must overcome along the way, and light as you hope this little kid makes it through them all.  So in terms of art direction, and visual style I very much enjoyed Limbo.
The game doesn’t really have music.  Instead it has atmospheric sounds.  They work very well and really help set the mood.  This is the type of game where you do not want to play it while listening to your own music or with a tv in the background.  While playing definitely immerse yourself in the complete atmosphere the game gives you.

As stated above I really enjoyed the entire visual and audio direction Limbo went with.  Gameplay on the other hand is a different story.  The game is a history test and nothing more.  Cheap death following cheap death following cheap death.  You enter a new area, get killed until you figure out what the game wants you to do and then you do it.  None of the puzzles in the game are all that difficult, with the longest taking me maybe ten minutes.  Trying to figure the puzzles out is not an intellectual exercise.  More often than not it really is just keep dying till you do what the game wants.  That is complemented by a complete lack of a learning curve.  At no point during my four hour playthrough did I feel that I was getting better at the game.  At the beginning I was just dying till I figured out what the game wanted, and at the end I still just dying till I figured out what the game wanted.  I did die more at the end of the game then at first, but that is because the game is more mean spirited not because it was actually any harder.  Again, infinite lives and you respawn almost exactly where you died.
Limbo is normally $10, under no circumstances do I feel it is worth that price.  As stated above I got it during a steam sale and as part of a bundle.  Limbo itself was only $1.79 for me.  Honestly, I couldn’t imagine spending any more than $5 for it.
Visually I think Limbo is brilliant, but everything else just left me disappointed.
Score: Disappointing
How my scoring works: Most reviewers assign a numerical score to things.  This doesn’t really make sense to me.  If one game has an 8.5 and another has an 8 is one really better than the other?  Or is it just the mood of the reviewer at that time?  Are we talking about a meaningful differences?  Is a 8 really that much worse than an 9?  To me there is virtually no difference between these scores.  There are just too many dividing lines.  Now I get that In any review system you need tiers but to me you want as few tiers as possible.  I seriously considered just having “reccomend/Skip” as my system, but decided that that was to vague to be of much value to anyone.  That would combine outstanding games and just ok games under “reccomend”  So instead My scores are:
Amazing
Good
Disappointing
Terrible
Yes, if something is given a “good” score you could say I gave it a 3 out of 4 but that really what i’m going for.  Why convert a descriptive thing like good into something abstract like a number?

This game reminds me a lot of the classic game Smash TV and sort of reminds me of an Amstrad CPC game, Mikie, and is very enjoyable to play.
A twin-stick shooter, players level up and can upgrade their character's abilities, via random drops and also by collecting gold, to use to purchase items, such as health upgrades also, in the store.  The player starts of with a fairly sparse health bar, although, this as well as damage, attack speed and weapon pickup effectiveness duration, can be upgraded permanantly, up to a limit, specified by difficulty level, so that the player will eventually find it easier to advance from the beginning.
I think this game is really excellent.  Very retro graphics with real nice bright fruit and other item pickups.  The inclusion of steam leaderboards is a great incentive to replay the game after completion, and players will find that they may have to consider their route to the boss room, on each floor, to increase the probability of achieving a high score.
Connecting some of the rooms on each floor, players will find either a shop or bonus level.  The bonus level is a fairly challenging platformer, which is excellent in itself.  Players collect gold along the route and are awarded with a special item at the end.
The soundtrack is fairly retro dark electronic sounding, which is good, although possibly noticeably repetitive at the start.  Provides a fairly dark atmosphere, lightened by real nice pick ups and weapon effects.  The game is really worth completing just to hear the track on completion of the 'final' floor.  Excellent music.
Works great with xbox controller.  Local co-op is available.  Would love to see a sequel.  Highly recommended, especially considering the low price. 10/10.

No tanks in this DLC ,which i prefer  , and since there is so much cover you can get away with more of a run and gun  gameplay , but there are choke points where you have to have good Squad leaders and a team leader that use smoke effectively and set good artillery spots , to clear  out pesky  defenders.  Accurate period historic weapons make this game a bit unbalanced for the Japenese , but a good Jap team can woop the Americans no problem , the worst most one sided map is Maggot Hill ,  and is terrible map design ,but can be defended with good tactics and communication.  Overall a Great game for patient  tactical players.

Wow. I can't explain how this game had made me feel. Such an elaborate, yet concise way to look into one person's mind to understand what they go through and how we alone, are unable to help.  People are not problems to be solved, they are to be loved, valued, and understood.
What's remarkable about The Beginners Guide, is that it actually asks you to think: To look outside of what's in front of you and come to terms with the creator as well as the narrator. Whether $10 was worth it is debatable, but it's not ultimately my concern. We can't extract our entire value from some person. Our true value is not determined by them, and nor is their value determined by us. We are not enough. When we make comparisons or judgements, it reveals no long term benefits. I agree that it's a natural attitude that we can all have as humans who have the ability to choose their words and actions. But we can never choose the consequences of those decisions.
What does it mean to be human, a person who is valued, loved, cherished? What does it mean to know a person to whom your goal is to always help them choose what's best for them? And yet love them regardless of their decision?
Who can say that they can love people out of themselves so well, that regardless of their choices, they never change their mind about them?
There's only one person who will never stop loving all people, and I believe many of you may already know who that is. He lived on earth for 30+ yrs, understanding us from our level. He spent his last 3 yrs as a teacher, healer and miracle worker, always speaking the truth of His Father, from whom He came to show His love that can never be matched, by dying and then by rising again to prove who he is and to give a solution to human frailty. A relationship with Himself. The One who will always and forever knows what's best for you. All it takes is trust.
In conclusion, I definitely recommend this game for it's personal story and emotional theme to bring one's mind into another perpective.

While I only have a small amount of time put into this game so far, I can say that I am very, very happy with my purchase. RO2/RS has to be one of the most fun games I've played in a very long time.
This game can be rage inducing...
This game can be unfair at times...
...but, it never seems that I didn't have a chance to do better.
For instance, I was playing as the Russians on a snow map where we had to push uphill to capture 12 german points in a manner similar to Rush from the battlefield series. I popped my head out, and got sniped. If I thought my plan through, I could've made my way to a hill with more trees on it that would provide cover, but I wasn't thinking as smartly as I could have been.
Another thing that I like about this game that I find lacking in other games is teamwork. I don't just mean talking to your teammates and maybe executing team strategies (like in CSGO), but an unspoken teamwork. I never used my microphone, and nor did most of the other players that I played with, but we moved as a group, attacked as a group, and died as a group. Whenever someone pushed up, there were other players that instantly assisted in the push, instantly covered those pushing, and, in my case, take a bullet for a teammate (accidently, but still saved someone in a videogame. ARE YOU PROUD OF ME YET MOTHER!?).
The only cons I can think of about this game are the learning curve, team-killing (which is apart of the learning curve in some way), and the optimization. This game can be brutally unforgiving. If you are looking for an arcade game that doesn't really take any skill to dominate, go play one of the recent CODs. This game has a damage model that is basically 1 bullet, 1 kill (in most everycase), but if you somehow survive being shot, you have to find cover and use one of the 2 bandages that you spawn in with everytime. Team killing plays into the learning curve because you have to be able to distinguish who is a friend and who is a foe, which can be difficult in some of the maps where both teams have similar clothing. The game also has some fps drops now and then, but that could just be my system, so take that con with a pinch of salt.
Overall, I would have to say that if you are looking for an experience in between Battlefield and ArmA (like Insurgency, but a little bit more so), then this is the game that you probably are looking for. If you do get it, I recommend getting the bundle, because then you will be able to play both Red Orchestra 2 (Eastern Front | Germans and Russians) and Rising Storm (Pacific Campaign | American and Japanese) within the same game.
This game is a must have for any FPS player, but take what I said (or typed) with a pinch of salt considering I have just under 3 hours played. I do not believe that my score will go down, but I have a feeling that as I play, the score may increase a bit.
Oh, and this game has the best flamethrower that I've ever seen in a video game.

Really awesome simulation of a harsh world in the time of a zombie-apocalypse. Despite it´s crude graphics this game is able to build a strong immersion, where your character will suffer hunger, thirst, loneliness, boredom, depression and disease and every dumb move can be your last. Fights with Zombies are not your only problem, as your only chance of survival will depend on your abilities to build or secure a savehouse, loot food, weapons and tools and, later on, build your own farm with rain collectors and much more. There is a huge skillsystem and an interesting character creation, that is different to other games. If your character dies, that´s it, because there is no saving and permadeath is an important feature of the game. There is a large, constantly increasing map with many points of interest. The buildings will slowly crumble as time goes on and nature will reconquer the land. When you start your game, electricity and water are still available, but trust me this will change...
In my opinion this game is one of the best early access-games right now because the developers are kind, ambitious and hear, what the fans have to say. The content right now is already really amazing and will keep you entertained for many hours. Some people in the comments said, that updates are kind of slow, but I don´t think so. There is a frequently updated beta-branch available, if people accept the consequences of a less stable build and I didn´t had much problems with it so far. Also there is a weekly update-blog, which informs everyone about new features and ongoing development.
Right now some things in the game are still missing. Especially vehicles and NPCs. It might take some time until these are implemented, but I am pretty sure, that once they are in, they will rock. At the moment the late-game content is a little bit thin, because once you got your savehouse with walls, a successful farm and enough watersupplies it´s not necessary to leave your stronghold, but the developers are working on more ways of zombie movement and hordebuilding and making your life harder. Also NPCs, once they are in, will make the endgame more interesting.
The endgame is my only real problem with this game yet and I played quite a lot so it is still entertaining. Also replay value is amazing, since the start of the game with no weapons in a world full of zombies is always different and you will face different problems every time. There are also many settings for new games like, behaviour and strength of zombies, loot-frequency, month of start, number of zombies, weather and even the time, that has passed since the apocalypse.
One important notice: There is a demo available and I would normally say: "Go play it to see if it´s for you", but this demo is really outdated, many features missing and, in my opinion, not much fun, because you will only see about one ingame day on a pretty deserted location of the otherwise huge and interesting map. I would advise to only play it to see, if your PC can handle it and if the controls are okay for you.

It's a shame that many people aren't aware of Ghost Master because it's a great game. If you were one of those people who enjoyed tormenting sims in The Sims, then this game is for you. If you're a person who likes paranormal or ghost themed video games, then this game is for you. If you enjoy light strategy and puzzle solving, then this game is for you.
The game cost me less than a dollar and I've put 25 enjoyable hours into it. There are dozens of ghosts to experiment with and each can be upgraded, adding a degree of personalization to the way you tackle missions. The game is over a decade old, but while the visuals aren't anything to write home about the stylistically cartoonish art direction means that it hasn't aged poorly.
I'm sure initial perceptions of the game are that it is a casual shovelware title, but it's to your detriment if you write it off thinking so. Give it a try the next time you have a dollar from selling trading cards during the next sale.

When all's said and done, it's the art style and atmosphere that made this game a success. The puzzles are generally above average for games of this type, although they mostly use rather vanilla mechanics that have been seen before in countless other games (push blocks around, swing on ropes, pull levers to change states of machinery etc. etc.) It's an amazing game at first: artistic, eerie atmosphere; an intriguing story; and a variety of clever mini-puzzles.
Sadly, at about the halfway point it stops being about puzzles and starts being about running as fast as you can and perfect-timing every jump. The puzzle design becomes far too reliant on precision timing, and frustration tends to dominate. What I found was that you fairly quickly work out *what* you are supposed to do, but the act of *actually* executing the sequence is bogged down with endless trial-and-error as you have to constantly micro-adjust the positions of things, and re-adjust your timing until you hit that split-second and pixel-perfect "sweet spot" that allows progression to actually occur. When it takes 30secs to figure out the solution, but 10 minutes of repeating the same sequence over and over until you hit that jump just right (for example), then there is something obviously wrong with the design. Best way of summing it up - it's a bit like how Braid would have played if you were allowed to rewind time. Ouch.
Just as it was introducing some interesting mechanics, the game ended. Add to that the ending is a huge disappointment story wise (no real spoilers, but suffice to say: it ends like an Arthouse movie, not at all like a fantastic mystery).
Thoroughly disappointing beyond the first half.

This is one of those games that truly has a unique experience awaiting the player. This is basically the Sims turned on it's head where instead of building up a virtual family or a house, your building up an ability to scare the pants off of the local Sims population.
Complete with a multitude of nods to various movies and fictions, this game is packed with a tool set for the player to create his or her own brand of mayhem, and an almost unparalleled ability to cause spontaneous bursts of maniacal laughter. There really is something brilliant about having engineered circumstances just right so that a house full of Sims having a party is turned into complete chaos with all the party guests running and screaming around the map.
There are some downsides. For instance, I still find the initial scenario and learning curve a bit clunky, and the interface is a bit micro management-ish, until you get used to it and get comfortable with the alternatives and shortcuts. There are also some minor bugs and occasionally you may find it difficult to advance a scenario as there is often no clear indication of what to do. (This is actually something I greatly appreciate as it is left to the player to figure out what he or she would like to do, but could be something others dislike).
Overall, this is a genuinely magnificent game, full of character, humor, and a robust set of play mechanics. Right now there is an absurd sale for this title, and there has never been a better reason to give it a go. One of my all time favorites, I highly and wholeheartedly recommend this game.

I approached this game with caution. It sure looked like a variant of the original gauntlet (one of my favorite games of old) and I didn't want to be disappointed (as I was with the recent Gauntlet remake).
At a first glance the pixel graphics, resemble the original much more than its name sake, however the similarities don't end there as in many ways it does resemble it. Is it a worthy successor ? well I am not sure about that, its a nice try and I must say that with a little bit more work it could have been  truly great. Don't get me wrong, it is a wonderful game and one that offers lots and lots of fun, but unfortunately it is a bit shallow. Each battle takes place in a single room stage, so there is no exploring with a horde of monsters on your heels and the variation of weapons and specials is a bit limited, especially after a few runs.
Boss fights are generally easy and you get the hang of each (of the few bosses - I think its four or five of them only) pretty easily.
There is a leveling system, accompanied by a skill set, which (especially in the beginning) is a nice novelty, but you go through it pretty quickly and actually will forget about it (for the most part) as you play more and more. You keep your level (along with certain skills you have bought) from one game to another, but there are also temp skills you acquire for each play-through only.
One very nice touch, is the global (score) ranking, so you can try to climb that ladder. Be warned though, to get to the upper levels of the rankings you will need to spend quite a bit of time and (for me at least) the game seems more geared towards casual and occasional play-throughs.
The control scheme is a bit complicated and i would not recommend it without a controller (twin stick is the best way to play it in my opinion). The game is generally undemanding in terms of specs and it run perfectly on my crappy laptop (even when I had forgotten to clean its vents causing it to overheat on almost every other game).
There is local coop also, but truth be told I did not get to try it, still it sounds like fun.
Would I recommend it ? Yes, absolutely, its great fun, just don't expect something more than what it really is. I will be keeping it installed on my pc for sure as it is a great go to for some casual fun.

Evolve is an outstanding game that delivers an experience that hasn't been dealt to the gaming community in quite some time. As said before, the game could have flopped. There were great potentials for horrible balance between hunters & monsters, bad optimization, and countless others. These issues however are not present. A very decent Co-Op twin stick shooter. But its just that : decent. It doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it doesn't improve on it either.
You shoot the same zombies over and over and over. Mages appear a little later that shoot bullets, but it gets so crowded that you might not survive to where there is more enemy variety. I picked it up to play some casual co-op with a friend, so I didn't intend to practice to get far. So we didn't.
The game lacks a certain punch to it. Know that sound and feel when you get a hit in Super Smash Bros, esp. on the N64? Yeah, there isn't that here. You just, somehow, throw AXES at a machine-gun pace and it does a barely-audible *tick*. Game feel is very important.
There is a lack of classes - there is only one. A thing I really enjoyed in the new Gauntlet remake was that one player could use the Valkyrie and shield your archer or mage teammate. Then the mage can slow enemies down so that they can be easier to handle melee. We would call when we'd prepare a move before the enemies spawned. That was really cool teamwork dynamic. None of that here.
Items are for the most part useless. You get a staggering amount of drops from enemies, which then gets annoying since it does nothing but give you points. This is 2016, I'm playing in my living room not in an arcade gallery. Nobody is gonna look over and say OMG YOU GOT SO MANY POINTS!
I know that it tries to recreate that style of arcady old-school game, but even then points never got in the way of the gameplay. You would kill enemies and get points automatically. But in this game you get drops that seem useful (to level up, for instance?), but only serve to distract from the enemies and give no gameplay benefit.
Oh! Is that a book? Awesome! I must get some kind of cool spell ability! *grabs book* 100 POINTS! *gets killed by projectile while distracted*
In terms of aesthetics, it is also okay but nothing to write home about. Cute pixel-art. Music is forgettable (see Shovel Knight). Sound lacks punch. Level design is square and bare. Average.
IN CONCLUSION : a game that falls short of expections and becomes quickly boring despite the potential and attractiveness of the trailer.
Score : 6.5/10
RECOMMENDATION : Get on sale if you have a buddy that likes mob swarm twin-stick shooters to play Co-Op. Challenge yourselves to work as a team and crank up the sound to make things a bit more interesting.

This is not a game for people who hate repetitive goals, but then again, the CoD franchise is successful.
First: The Game

The game is fun. It has three characters per role, including the monster. Each character has their own unique playstyle, which allows for around 24 unique combinations for matches.  There are also currently 12 maps, which increases the amount of unique games to 284 combinations for the basic Hunt mode.
Two gamemodes, Hunt and Evacuation. Hunt is simple, kill monster or kill hunters until time runs out or the generator is destroyed. Evacuation has Nest, Defend, Hunt, and Rescue game modes that players can choose from between a 5 game campaign. Each map gives a unique perk to the winner, and the losers get a handicap buff.
Second: Graphics    10/10, the game is beautiful. The maps look alike in color because they are all around an island-like region, just like a real continent or island would be.
Third: DLC  -  **COMPLETELY COSMETIC THUS FAR***
Yes, they are selling skins. Completely cosmetic. Do not effect gameplay. Hunter skins are $1.99 per skin, with $4.99 packs for 3 hunters of that class. Monster skins are $2.99, and have a $6.99 bundles for all 3 monsters for that skin category.
Fourth: Future DLC
Maps are free, and will always be free.  New hunters are $7.49 each, Monsters are $14.99 each. You don't need to buy these characters to play with or against them. They are also not necessary.
Fifth: Bugs/Server
New IP, hackers are getting into it, but the devs are working on fixing this situation. These hackers are rare, I haven't seen one my entire time playing since Alpha, Beta, Press release, and post-launch.  There are some bugs, but devs are also working on this. Every game has bugs. get over it.
Overall:  Fun game, worth the $60 for the PC Monster Race edition. It has it's flaws, but the core idea is fresh enough to keep me playing for a long time.

Let's start with the “Meh”: the game's singleplayer mode is the biggest, if not only, weakness of this title. They try to make a story around it, but it feels and plays identical to the Multiplayer. In that respect, the SP part feels more like "training with bots" than anything else. But that's because it is.
The real meat and bones of this juicy, juicy bean stew is in the multiplayer and I dare say that RO2 is the only title that has been able to display accurately the feel and struggle of the Second World War. Besides the maps and weapons and guts flying in all directions when a grenade lands, and all the bolt-action weapons, RO2 capture the essence of World War II by genuinely not giving a flying f*ck about the player.
No, really. Everything in this game is created with the precise reason of making your life hard and it works on so many levels.
The movement is rough, with any sprint taking from your stamina bar, making it harder to aim. Entering or exiting crouch or prone will make you lose control of your weapon for a few seconds. Gone are the days of the Battlefield 3+ super soldier who could run, jump, sprint and crouch quicker than you can say “I wish they didn’t close the BF2142 servers”.
Nearby artillery or enemy gunfire will also make your stamina deplete faster. When it gets to zero, your screen turns black and white and you can no longer zoom in while aiming; making shooting a more difficult endeavour.
And a difficult one it is nonetheless; aiming is done in the usual modern manner, but with an extra twist. You can do a slight zoom while aiming down the sight, vital for the large fields that fill the RO2 maps (players of Operation Flashpoint 1 / Arma will know this feature). Trust me, you will need this slight zoom. On many maps, discerning a distant player from friend or foe is a challenge within itself and at first you will find yourself shooting friendlies in this game (remember to say “sorry”), but that is part of war, for war is gruesome.
But perhaps the most authentic feature that strives to the game’s reality is it’s class system. In RO2, classes are restricted. Each map has x snipers, y gunners, z heavy gunners and so forth. These numbers are always small (less than 5), with the bulk of the players filling the most used class, Rifleman. This means that most players in a server will be using bolt-action rifles, while the more complex ones will have access to better weapons or tools/traits. This also highlights one of the game’s weaker points, since, without a pretty strong machine and gaming rig, your map will load slowly, lessening your chances of choosing the desired class.
Even so, I cannot recommend RO2 enough. It is a gem among 64-player FPS games and should be experienced by anyone who is interested in massive multiplayer shooters. The core game, along side with the Rising Storm expansion and the free maps created by the community give you a game that is still played thoroughly, for good reason.

Ok, so my time in this game was VERY short lived. I have played MMO's since before WoW was an idea. I may throw some more time into this game, but I highly doubt it.
First off, all classes are genderlocked. So no, you can not choose your gender. Honestly, not a big issue with me as I'm more about the gameplay and content. It was just a drawback from the standpoint I love customization and variety in my appearance, which once again, this game does practically does not have.
Second, story seems pretty generic. World is in trouble, gods need you, yadada. No biggy, it's hard to find an original premise for stories these days. But the world itself is pretty cool. GFX aren't the best of 2015, but it's a F2P....no complaints for not having billion dollar budget GFX.
The controls and camera are what cut my time short in this game honestly. I can deal with lack of variety, a medoicre story, crappy graphics...but holy crap...Q and E do not strafe and the camera has to be manually turned. Your A and D keys to not turn your character, but strafe instead. All turning requires the mouse and often times you turn the camera but your character will keep running in the direction you were originally running (AKA character doesn't turn with the camera). I spent more time trying to move and target enemies than actually fighting...I think the only other MMO I've played that had that kind of control/camera system MIGHT have been Lineage II, but even it wasn' this bad.
Combat, pretty generic point-and-click spam your rotation MMO. I personally like those kinda of combat system, but the camera issues really throw a wrench into this game...
All-in-all, I haven't dont anything outside of the little noob area (hell, didn't even finish that) but based on my experience here....this game is far from being any big award winners. Not the best, no the worst...but definitely not worth the time if you're looking for a good consistent MMO.
I may re-do this review later, but I feel like I will probably never devote enough time to do the game a fully unbiased review.

One of the more intense zed survival games I've ever played.  Creep around scavenging supplies all the while trying to avoid detection from roving hoards of zombies.  Noises constantly shift and sway the hoard around town, keeping you on your toes constantly.  Shoot, slice, and smack enemies as you scavenge, but remember that ANY encounter could be your last.  All it takes is a simple scratch to infect you, leading to a slow death.  Your character will slowly become more proficient with different skills as you play through the game, but it takes effort and planning to truly master various skills.  If you plan on living a long time, you'll need to learn how to catch/grow your own food/water, and build dependable structures.  Chances are very good that you will die in this game, but trying not to is a delightful challenge regardless.
This is one of the better Early Access games that I am excited to see finished!  In the meanwhile, its back to scavenging for nails for my ever expanding fort.
