Here's a list of bullet points about the game in no particular order!
-No Day 1 DLC that isn't cosmetic, yes they're just weapon/monster reskins.
-Yes, there is a lot of planned DLC, and some of it is free. Yes, monsters are likely going to be overpriced.
-Not having DLC will not prevent you from playing with those who do have DLC, keeping the community more or less together
-It's well balanced and fun for the most part.
-Both monster and hunters are fun to play as and offer numerous play styles.
-There are two game modes, Hunt which is the core game and Evacuation which is actually a 5 round long mini story which players vote on different game modes to play. I don't know why the other game modes (Nest, Rescue, etc) aren't offered on lists, but it's likely to keep populations focused. These modes are available in custom games though.
-There are bots which are not terrible most of the time, it is possible to do hunter/monster progression through solo to unlock more hunters/monsters/elite skins.
-You very likely will be forced to play the monster at some point. Even if it is your 5th choice the game is like a pushy used car salesman "YOU WANNA PLAY THE MONSTER NOW RIGHT? YEAH RIGHT?" Even though I've been in games with 3 people who have Monster as their No. 1 pick. Not quite sure what the deal with that is.
-Unlockable hunters are no better (and in some cases worse) than the starter hunters. They may accel vs. different monsters or mesh better with other hunters but are not better or worse.
-Actually getting into games can be a pain in the butt. Sometimes you'll join a fresh game and the lobby will disconnect, other times you'll join in an already started game and you're about to lose and then you get disconnected for no reason.
-There are a few minor bugs actually in game that are gamebreaking, but they aren't very exploitable and are mostly just chance. These are likely to be patched ASAP so here's hoping.
-I'm really just writing this to help a badge progress YAY.

Iron Fisticle, got this game for insanely cheap via coupons and has blown me away. Skeptical of cheap games I expected the game to be filled with bugs, more crashes than a stock car race and really bad game play. I was genuinely surprised at how well thought out this game is.
Iron Fisticle is a Dungeon crawling shooter game where you battle through 4 Levels (which aren't easy). This game has a level of difficulty to it and provides a nice leveling up system with permanent and temporary character upgrades. One of they games where you can actually notice an improvement in your character, and player skill - which is very rewarding.
However, my cons are is that once you become an highly ranked character is that the game could become easy as there is only 4 levels (which is the ultimate outcome if you grind games). There is another mode, which at the current time I haven't dived into. The mode is basically the same as the normal mode, but you do not gain permanent upgrades - so Binding of Isaac.
Conclusion: for how cheap the game is, it's perfect. I believe all the other reviews are positive. If I was the developer of a relatively (review based) successful game I would be pushing as much content out the door as possible! This game exceeds the warrant to release DLC or sequel.

Strictly speaking from my own perspective;
This is one of the most unique experiences in gaming.
I know there were similar games in the past, encompassing both asymmetrical and abnormal game mechanics, but for the majority of games available these days, this stands out.
I think the DLC controversy is both unwarranted and irrelevant.
Yes, it is irritating to have "Day 1 DLC".
Yes, it is pathetic to launch a game with so much DLC available.
Yes, it is shameful to have such a small amount of content for a full-price (60$ USD) title.
Yes, it is reasonable to say that this title lacks value.
However.
I think people are judging the game too harshly, and here's why:
Firstly, ALL (100%) of the DLC is strictly vanity/cosmetic. There is no way to overstate how important that fact is.
This game fills a niche that, effectively, most gamers are not aware exists;
There are a number of MLG titles out there; CS, LoL, DoTA, etc... but all of them fall by the wayside as soon as you enter the competitive scene. Why? It's because the community is all about maximum performance. This means that you would never choose X item over Y item for Z role. For me, and a good number of other people, this is nonsensical. Why bother adding X item at all? Games like LoL have to constantly evolve (heh-heh) their characters and playstyles with paatches and updates, just to keep things balanced and viable. While it's great that developers see a problem and attempt to fix it, it would be a far superior strategy to simply bypass the problems entirely.
Having never met a dev from Evolve, I can only assume they are either geniuses or incidentally lucky that they have ENTIRELY skipped the second biggest problem facing MLG; Proper Balance.
At this point you may be confused as to why I could consider Proper Balance to be a bad thing, so to speak.
The reason is simple; Sometimes you need variance. Sometimes there needs to be an element of chance. Sometimes encountering impossible odds leads to motivation to outplay your opponent. Sometimes not.
Personally, I LOVE Evolve for the same reason I love Hearthstone; RNG.
It's entirely possible to play a match and never encounter an Albino (rare enemy with a buff reward) and still wreck your opponent(s).
It's entirely possible to play a match where your opponent(s) encounter and slay multiple Albinos, leaving you significantly under-powered.
It's entirely possible to play a match where you collect tons of buffs and still get rekt.
I love the variance. I think it provides much more exciting gameplay than people give it credit for.
I really can't speak highly enough of the game, and I encourage you to try it out.
That having been said, there ARE reasonable flaws/complaints to be made.
One such complaint has really caught my attention; If you follow a guide posted here on Steam forums (and likely found elsewhere too) to remove cutscenes, your game install file becomes roughly 12.5GB.
That's not all, though; Steam lists the system requirements as 50GB. This is, for lack of a better word, laughable.
I find it reasonable to recommend more than the necessary amount, in case of later-available content, sure.
But if you consider the "core game" (maps, engine, default characters, game modes, menus) is likely about 10GB by itself, that means roughly 2.5GB can be attributed to the playable characters (audio files, models, ability code, interaction etc).
Assuming this estimate is roughly accurate, that means they have plans to release roughly 25GB worth of content over the course of the game's lifetime.
Assuming this estimate is roughly accurate, we could expect to see a huge number of playable characters, maps and game modes in the future.
THIS would have been well-worth the 60$ title.
However, we know that extra characters, maps, modes will be charged for, thusly making this title one of the least value purchases you could make, from my perspective.
Why, then, did I myself purchase it?
It's fun as ♥♥♥♥, that's why. Sometimes value isn't everything.

First things first, hear some nagatives about this game:
1. RO2 could be a nightmare for beginers because of absence of a good tutorial. This game already has a tutorial but its not good at all. So many classes are left unexplained and also many game mechanics are left to be found by players. So you should be very patient at your early hours in this game.
2. There are so many bugs and glitches and issues in RO2. Collisions and invisible walls bugs, animations glitches, sound effects issues, servers connection and matchmaking problems and even more. So now you know you are going to face  not a very clean game.
3. There is no single player experience waiting for you in this game. As you know, this game is all about multiplayer, and not about those tiny multiplayer servers with about 5 or 6 people in them. If you want to achieve the real feeling of RO2, you should take part in massive battles with more than 40 or 50 people in them. Finding these servers are not always easy and it would take some time.
RO2 is a realistic shooter with a WWII theme which can satisfy players who enjoy playing titles like Insurgency, Squad, Arma, Flashpoint and etc. If you have no problem with those negative points that I mentioned and also love realistic shooters, congrates, this game is for you.

At first i thought this was just gonna be another free cheesy horror game, with a little exploration and a few jumpscares, nothing much else...
well....... this is the part where i say, it proved me wrong and infact far excedeed my expectations.
Now take note that as a disclamer here i have not infact played that many horror games, and i am not a big horror game connoisseur. However, this game turned out to have so much more to it than i initially thought, and without trying to praise it too much here, i really have say that for such a free little horror game it really did it's job at scaring the everliving crap out of me. It kept me feeling uncomfortable and on edge thoughout the entire experience, just wanting to get out and get to the end, yet only to keep finding that there was more to do..
Sir Bedlam Productions really knew what he was doing when he made this game, and i think he did a great job on it.
Now the game itself is fairly short, with about maybe 4 hours or so of playtime, more or less depending on how many times you  die, and how quickly your able to figure things out.
the story that is there is short and simple, but its easy to get into and does the job nonetheless, and It doesnt take long for the game to pick up before you imediately start to feel uncomfortable and filled with an unyeilding sense of Dread and panic.
As you progress through the game you'll discover more and more of the story and the places history, all the while things get increasingly more creepy, terrifying, and intense as you anxiously try to figure out what to do and where to go next..
now.. yes this is a free indie horror game, made by a single developer, and i know that there are probably plenty of them in existance already, don't get me wrong, if your a horror veteran or just somebody who likes really good horror, i'm not trying to set you up with super high expectations here, because this is another Free Indie Horror game, but...for everything that it is and everything that the dev put into it, i'd say that its probably one of the better ones that are out there, it gave me a few good scares, and it was able to keep the tension up throught the whole thing, never  letting me feel safe, i'd say that for the few hours of playtime that it is worth, it did a pretty decent job as a horror game, especially for a free one, which more than i can probably say for alot of others. So for everything that this game is i'll give it an 8.5/10 and maybe thats a bit genrous but  i think it's pretty good and I'd highly recommend it if your a horror enthusiast.
P.S: I really liked that creepy poetry bit in that one scene, it was a real nice touch, just the way it was spoken and delivered, super unsettling. Sends chills down my spine every time i think of it, and also that Finale was Probably the most stress inducing thing i ever tried to play through in a game.
TL:DR Stop being so damn Lazy and actually Read things. oh and yeah for a free game it's actually pretty scary/creepy.

The video game market is flush with post-apocalypse undead survival games, and at a casual first look Project Zomboid does little to stand apart from the horde. But examine a little closer and you will find that Project Zomboid is a true gem in it's genre, despite being in its early access stages. Project Zomboid is at its heart -IMO- a survival game with hardcore RPG elements that should appeal to the storyteller in almost every gamer. You'll have to manage aspects of your character (hunger and thirst, boredom and happiness) while scavenging for food and supplies in an isometric post-apocalypse world
Firstly Project Zomboid is still in its developement, and as such you can expect to find bugs, glitches, and other programing issues. The PZ Devs seem like a fairly hardworking group, release updates frequently, and I have read from other players that tthey are top notch at working with indivuals within the community with getting their games to work and ironing out all the bugs. All that being said I have yet to encounter any major bugs, but buyers beware with early access.
In my opinion the graphics are a little cutsie and old fashioned, having the appearance of an older 90's game; your fancy graphics card will not be worked out running this game. And because of the graphics the user interface is occasionally rather clunky, and it can be difficult sometimes to tell the exact direction your character is facing, which is moderately important when trying to bash in some zombies skull with a fireaxe...or golfclub....or frying pan. The Devs have made massive strides in this area, but is going to be frustrating to get srcatched or bitten because of an interface issue.
The community behind this game is rather vibrant and supporting, and the Devs seem commited to producing their vision as quickly as they can. Since I have bought the game it has expanded and been updated more times than I can count, and the devs are constantly turinging out new content. But if they are not working fast enough for you their is an excellent community of modders expanding the game in other direction with new items, actions, maps, etc.
I expected this game to be finished by now, and it is not. Indie Stone (the group behind PZ) appears to me to be a pretty small group of people, and perhaps had they more reasources the game would be a finished product at this time.
This is honestly one of the most immersive and seemingly realistic survival horror RPG games I have come across. Their are as many strategies of playing the game as their are players. You can build a base, scaveenge for food and supplies, farm for food, fish, wield an axe, break said axe and repair it, cook your food,play on multiplayer servers, or play in a sandbox mode where you can set all aspects of the games conditions (zombie count, weather, starting date, supply rate, etc). The game is HUGE in what you can do, limited only by the players ability to be creative and immagine new possibilities for themselves, and promises to get even bigger with each new patch.
[b[Whats Still Missing?:[/b] As of this build Project Zomboid is still missing some -IMO- crucial portions of the game. While Multiplayer has been instituted, NPC's do not exist as of this build, nor is there any kind of story mode, and there are no cars, vehicles, or game world events (as opposed to "meta noises and events" which only serve to move the hordes around). All of these things are planned for the game, but have not yet been implamented, leaving long term players or long term servivors with less options than the finished game will likely have.
Project Zomboid is meant for fans of the survival horror genre, but should also appeal to hardcore RPG fans, or anyone that loves to build and explore game worlds. If you have ever wondered if you or your friends could survive a zombie apocalypse then this game if for you. If you have ever thought about surviving in the Walking Dead universe or teeling their story your way then this game is for you.
This game has no ending or endgame, and is about the story of how your character died, so if you are the type of video game player that like clear direction in your games and paths to advance then you may wish to stay away from PZ. the goals in PZ are all set by the player, and you may generally attempt to do anything you think might help you survive.
Project Zomboid is also a hard and difficult game, even on easier settings. You will die, and you will loose characters to foolish mistakes or risks, and if you are like me then you'll bask in the depression of every hard-grown characters death. May they RIP.

Superhot is a quirky new take on the fps genre with a time bending ability mixed in, the story breaks the fourth wall with you (the player) being in the game and playing Superhot through a dos like system, basically the mission is to eliminate all foes in each room using any weapon or object. You can steal objects from enemies by punching them, the art style is simple yet perfect. The gameplay is the strongest link in Superhot & the feeling of gratification when completing a level is never lost. While it offers a unique gameplay experience the story is lacking & very short hence why I would recommend this game if it is on sale as the retail price is quite high but don't let that deter you as this still is a great game.
Superhot is a FPS puzzle shooter with a time bending ability. The basic premise of the game is to eliminate all the red figures in a room using weapons or objects. You are always outnumbered so running and gunning isn't an option or you will be killed instantly however enemies can only move if you are moving or doing an action like picking up an object ,This means that you can shoot three enemies at once if you are standing still , which evens out the odds considerable but it isn't as easy as you think because enemies are positioned all around ,they can also  be behind cover or behind you! in addition to this enemies bullets still go somewhat fast when you are standing still so dodging them is a must and this where the "fun" is found to dodge incoming bullets while stealing enemy weapons and killing them with-it, while the game progresses the techniques in which you can eliminate an enemy is increased.
As you can probably see from the store page pictures, the game looks rather simple however don't let that deceive unlike some other indie games the simplicity is well developed, it's sharp & could be compared to Mirror's edge catalyst. The main colours you will see in game are Red, White & Black even though there is a low use of the colour spectrum it still feels lifelike and vibrant (When you shoot an enemy the red shards fly out of the body oh so beautifully). After completing the level, you can watch a short replay of you completing the level in real time these are short and sweet.
If you read my introductory paragraph you would know that Superhot is a game based on eliminating overpowered enemies with your control of time being your advantage. It is off course a unique idea that has been used in games rarely, one thing that comes up to my mind is Dishonoured's Bend time ability where you can slow time (A little more overpowered). Even though the level can be completed in 10secs but it will take you much longer because you will need to stop time to be able to eliminate the red figures. One annoying thing is that red figures can respawn behind you and you have only a very short amount of time to kill them or you will be killed, this is especially true on harder levels however as you progress through the game you unlock new weapons like the katana but this are pretty redundant because they don't offer any real variation to killing the enemy however I love the ability to weaken any enemy by punching them and stealing their weapon and then murdering them with their own weapon that truly never gets old. Besides the fact that you are controlling time & feeling like an action hero when you see yourself in the replay clips in real time. Cons are if you want to have creative flexibility most of the levels have a set path to success and offer very limited or no alternate paths so memorization of where the enemy is needed which might suck if you’re not into that kind of suck it’s kind of a big CON .
You are a hacker who received  a crack of SUPERHOT from your friend and you begin to play it & slowly get addicted, after a little while the system gets irrated and tries to get you to leave, there is more but that is the basic premise that is all I can say, after that it is probably considered spoiler territory. The story is matrix like & is presented through a dos like system which can be very annoying, the sound in-between levels can be very irritating, It sounds like a untuned television (Not very pleasant). It is as if the developer tried too hard with the story to make it some psychological thriller however it is a break from the action which might be a good thing or a bad thing, the story is feels very short, indeed it only took me around 2 1/2 hours for me to complete and that is including the numerous deaths I have had. The story is defiantly the weakest point of the game however because the gameplay is the main factor in SUPERHOT it isn't as much of a problem as it would be in other games.

This game is amazing. It's that simple.
Your objective is to usually spook humans out of a house, which you do using the ghosts at your disposal. Different ghosts are 'bound' to different point of focus, the "fetters". So taking several ghosts tagged Corpse into the fraternity level is unadvisable, because they won't have anywhere to be bound to the material world.
There's a good amount of custom choices, with increased unlockable powers for all the ghosts based on how much ectoplasm (scary juice!) you earn. The levels always give a recommended lineup, but if you know what you're doing you can pick your own ghosts - to great success, or miserable failure: knowing the level helps!
Their powers can be combined in sometimes unpredictable power combos. As in, this is not mentioned anywhere in the game! But in a sense it rewards experimenting. The music really brings out the goofy, let's-scare-the-pants-off-some-mortals atmosphere. The pickup in tempo once you REALLY get your ghosts going, combined with the screams of the terrified victims, is just hugely entertaining.
Some of the levels with extra objectives require creative thinking, and some can be downright "how the ♥♥♥♥ do I do this" moments.  Nonetheless, the game is absolutely worth its low price tag, is very entertaining, and has good replayability if you liked it the first time around. I loved this game when I was younger and I still love it now.

Sir, You Are Being Hunted is a british robot adventure, that can make you at times jump out of your skin. So what has it got going for itself?
Sir, You Are Being Hunted is an Action Stealth game being created by Big Robot Ltd. In the past, they have created a game under the name of AVSEQ. To say the least, it was a mixed opinion. Now this has come out, and to say the least, AVSEQ can't even compare towards SYABH. In the game, you are stuck on a total of five islands. You require to collect some artifacts, bring them to the central location on the map, and use them to save progress. The game is beat, when all the artifacts are located, and used. To keep you from completing your target, a good number of robots will try to hunt you down, and shoot ten shotgun shells into your skull. Charming to say the least. While avoiding them, you must also find food to stay alive. These three concepts mix together to create the enviroment you will be in, and it works amazingly. You have to keep so much on your mind while you explore this world. Where is that robot? How hungry am I? What caused those crows to fly away? It really keeps you on your toes. At the moment, enemy mixture is decent, but not all content at the moment is final, considering its early access.
Gameplay. A big part to say the least. The game is mostly stealth, so you will be crouched most of the time. Noise and visibilty is view by a eye and noise icon at the bottom of the screen. Stealth works nicely at the moment. You feel any action COULD have its problems. Anything noisey will cause the robots to invesigate, which could be your death, OR your key to survival. Distractions become a big part of the game when the robots just wont cooperate to move away from a location or something along those lines. A well placed alarm clock or even a toy train will divert their attention just long enough so you can complete your task. However, keeping in mind, I said this was a ACTION game. At some instances during your looting of buildings, guns or ammunition will be found among the skulls and mouldy bread. Your options now open up a bit more. A problem could be controlled, a divertion could be caused, or you could simply run and gun. The last option is NOT recommended. On a personal note, at times i have played this game in the pitch dark. A few encounters have made me spoil my boxers to say the least. My point is, under the right conditions, you can turn it a bit into a horror.
As a sum up, this game is great. More than that really. Exploring these vast wastelands while worrying about all the issues has never felt so good. Even a few times, this game has made me chuckly due to the slight humor. (Robots taking a tea break to say the least is one of them.) I really recommend getting this game, and as time goes on, more content will be added. As of writing this, i have not even tried the January Patch yet! There is nothing more to say that this really:
GO.    BUY.     THIS.      GAME!             8.5/10

Strictly speaking from my own perspective;
This is one of the most unique experiences in gaming.
I know there were similar games in the past, encompassing both asymmetrical and abnormal game mechanics, but for the majority of games available these days, this stands out.
I think the DLC controversy is both unwarranted and irrelevant.
Yes, it is irritating to have "Day 1 DLC".
Yes, it is pathetic to launch a game with so much DLC available.
Yes, it is shameful to have such a small amount of content for a full-price (60$ USD) title.
Yes, it is reasonable to say that this title lacks value.
However.
I think people are judging the game too harshly, and here's why:
Firstly, ALL (100%) of the DLC is strictly vanity/cosmetic. There is no way to overstate how important that fact is.
This game fills a niche that, effectively, most gamers are not aware exists;
There are a number of MLG titles out there; CS, LoL, DoTA, etc... but all of them fall by the wayside as soon as you enter the competitive scene. Why? It's because the community is all about maximum performance. This means that you would never choose X item over Y item for Z role. For me, and a good number of other people, this is nonsensical. Why bother adding X item at all? Games like LoL have to constantly evolve (heh-heh) their characters and playstyles with paatches and updates, just to keep things balanced and viable. While it's great that developers see a problem and attempt to fix it, it would be a far superior strategy to simply bypass the problems entirely.
Having never met a dev from Evolve, I can only assume they are either geniuses or incidentally lucky that they have ENTIRELY skipped the second biggest problem facing MLG; Proper Balance.
At this point you may be confused as to why I could consider Proper Balance to be a bad thing, so to speak.
The reason is simple; Sometimes you need variance. Sometimes there needs to be an element of chance. Sometimes encountering impossible odds leads to motivation to outplay your opponent. Sometimes not.
Personally, I LOVE Evolve for the same reason I love Hearthstone; RNG.
It's entirely possible to play a match and never encounter an Albino (rare enemy with a buff reward) and still wreck your opponent(s).
It's entirely possible to play a match where your opponent(s) encounter and slay multiple Albinos, leaving you significantly under-powered.
It's entirely possible to play a match where you collect tons of buffs and still get rekt.
I love the variance. I think it provides much more exciting gameplay than people give it credit for.
I really can't speak highly enough of the game, and I encourage you to try it out.
That having been said, there ARE reasonable flaws/complaints to be made.
One such complaint has really caught my attention; If you follow a guide posted here on Steam forums (and likely found elsewhere too) to remove cutscenes, your game install file becomes roughly 12.5GB.
That's not all, though; Steam lists the system requirements as 50GB. This is, for lack of a better word, laughable.
I find it reasonable to recommend more than the necessary amount, in case of later-available content, sure.
But if you consider the "core game" (maps, engine, default characters, game modes, menus) is likely about 10GB by itself, that means roughly 2.5GB can be attributed to the playable characters (audio files, models, ability code, interaction etc).
Assuming this estimate is roughly accurate, that means they have plans to release roughly 25GB worth of content over the course of the game's lifetime.
Assuming this estimate is roughly accurate, we could expect to see a huge number of playable characters, maps and game modes in the future.
THIS would have been well-worth the 60$ title.
However, we know that extra characters, maps, modes will be charged for, thusly making this title one of the least value purchases you could make, from my perspective.
Why, then, did I myself purchase it?
It's fun as ♥♥♥♥, that's why. Sometimes value isn't everything.

Equal parts silly and scary, this game is loads of fun even if it is a bit unpolished. As the description says it is you, on a small set of islands, being carefully hunted by a never ending supply of well armed (and dapper) robots of all shapes and sizes. You scavenge for food, lay traps, and learn to dread any and all electronic noises as you search the islands for a number of stones to make your escape. Despite its somewhat goofy premise this is very much a survival horror game with enemies that are both fiercely intelligent and almost omnipresent. There will rarely be a time in which firing your gun won't leave you with a sense of dread, knowing that it's going to bring every hunter within a halfmile jogging towards your position. I'd almost call it remniscient of DayZ, only with a brutal AI instead of other players. If the concept sounds at all interesting to you I highly recommend it.

I'm sitting here trying to think of how to review Uriel's Chasm, and it is extremely difficult. Let me start by first saying that I don't think Uriel's Chasm should be given a normal game review, as it is not a normal game, I would even hesitate to call it a game. It is both more and less than a game, it is an experience. It is most definitely not for everyone, it's not even for most people I would surmise; However if you are reading this review you contain that spark of interest, and in which case I recommend that you buy it (it's not very expensive) and try it for yourself.
The game contains 4 levels, the last was added in an update. The gameplay is simplistic, and excepting the last level not very challenging. The game is very short as well, probably about 30 minutes to beat, less once you know what you're doing.  Do not buy this for the gameplay, that is not where the appeal lies. I know that sounds counter-intuitive, but I am a firm believer of games as art; they can be for more than entertainment! I like gameplay just as much as the next gamer, and more than some, but sometimes I want more than empty entertainment. And art is exactly what this game is, make no mistake. The game literally calls itself rubbish, so I feel that people that complain about the gameplay are missing the point entirely.
The graphics are excellent, though primitive, and contain some very memorable images ( the hidden face especially ) that combine with the superb music to create an extremely surreal, trippy, oftentimes quite disturbing aesthetic. I cannot comment on the story other than to say it is 'out there' for sure. It is very obtuse and to me didn't make much sense. I am not the type of person to really read a bunch of stuff into something, I'm not very good at that. I can't deny though that it did conjure up some very powerful emotions, something very few games do.
I could go on and still not be able to describe this game as it is something that needs to be experienced. If you have any interest I urge you to try it, form your own opinion. I feel sad that me and like 5 other ♥♥♥♥ing people like the game.

Buy this game if you know your watching a meta narrative about gaming and are into high brow, high art games. This is not funny like the stanley parable, so if you came here after that looking for more it's not this game.

NOTE : RailSlaveGames does not make mass consumption games. Just check out
for a frame of reference before judging this.
That being said, this game is more of an enigma which is placed within a long lost ZX Spectrum cartridge that is then presented to you through a Sega CD game than anything else. It is a user experience rather than a game, one that you should
and let it sink in. RailSlaveGames has created a world where every little detail is part of an intentionally obscure story which is up to the user to put it together. Nothing is just handed to you, and that’s the way it should be. More like a journey, Uriel’s Chasm is a trip. The gameplay is something you’re doing while you’re checking out the details and investigating the madness.
Let me try to explain....
In the game portion, you play as Sister Tabitha who has travelled to the edge of space to find out what happened to the Orbital Monastery “Enoch’s Hope”, which seems to be in grasps of “Garden”... some kind of otherworldly beast. The first stage is you bolstering your faith (and your sanity) to encounter “Garden” and hopefully find survivors. The second stage is you making the journey and the third stage has you locating the survivors.
This is only half the story. The other half is the story of those playing this game.
See, you’re not the player… nor Sister Tabitha. You’re only an observer.
What you’re watching is more akin to The Ring or The Blair Witch Project than any game you’ve played thusfar. The characters in the video sequences (including the trailer) have found some kind of lost or buried NES or ZX Spectrum cartridge. They’re confused and angry at the game. The developer himself calls the game “rubbish” during one of these sequences as it has no options screen and is confusing, just like the game you’re “playing”. However, they’re almost supernaturally compelled to continue to play the game. It keeps calling to them. By the end… well… that’s up to your interpretation.
What’s nice is that the developer is also very open about this title and already has been addressing issues players have been having with it’s presentation and length. Much like //N.P.P.D Rush//, he’s going to continue to add, refine and deepen the experience. Check
occasionally, you’ll be glad you did.
...and the music is FANTASTIC. It’s gritty and edgy at parts, while completely environmental and entrancing at others. The vocal tracks can best be described as “UK style Grunge-Goth & PostPunk”.
Uriel’s Chasm defies conventional logic, as any mindscrew should. Let the dark cartridge take you over. Give your soul to that which should have remained lost (or buried).

I definitely recommend this game!
As a ex-hardcore wow player, I would like to share my thoughts on this game as well.
I played this game as a rogue through CBT and the OBT!
Let me give you an honest feedback about this game
1. Creating a character is a little bit weird since you have  gender locked  classes.
Beside that: The options to customize your character are really nice! I'm very happy with the way my char looks!
2. Graphics: The game will not deliver the best graphics in history but its decent for a f2p. Not everybody can afford to have a BiS computer. It can reach a wider audience and attracts more players.
3. First Steps: The game basically supports you in every possible way.  Quests to introduce the dungeon browser, pvp browser and so on.
4. Questing: Of course its the usual Search X and deliver it to Y, Kill X amount of Y but there are other quests as well. I'm not positively surprised but also not disappointed.
5. PvP: You can clearly feel, that the game is made for Characters who reached level 60. You can join the pvp battle as soon as you hit level 10 (with an outstanding matchmaking system) and you most likely get owned by people who have a higher level than you. You resistance and HP are pumped up to level 60 standard but you can obviously not compete with your level 10 gear and skillset. Nevertheless, I was able to get the mvp (best player in the team) a lot of times when i was between level 10 and 40. The PvP is not necessarily innovative but it gives a ton of xp, and is really fun. Even though you are a melee and not level 60.
I also dont get why people complain about (always the same). They took the best content of other games and implemented it here. Its a nice combination of my favourite MMOS.
6. PvE: I really really like the Single Dungeon System and the grouping is amazing as well. You can match groups or go alone. One criticism: The leader can just kick people for whatever reason. If you dont have the super awesome gear, you get kicked in most of the times. On the other hand: It helps a lot to not wipe infinitely and if you dont have good gear, get some. There are tons of ways to farm good stuff in the game and i dont speak about cashing in.
7. p2w?: Yes and No! Of course, this is a f2p title and some paid features give you some kind of advantage. I think, Aeria wants to make things different here and when I compare this Launch to Aura Kingdom back in the days, I can clearly say, that this here is totally different.
I never had the feeling that I have to spend money. Questing was always flawless, never an artificial blocker which annoyed me or forced me to buy an xp boost. There are tons of free events which give me some nice goodies.
Im pretty okay with the fact that people who spend money get some benefits since they are keeping the service alive!
Summary:
There are pros and cons but eventually the game is a lot of fun to play, even without paying!
The game is not really "free". Paying users get some benefits but they dont have an impact on the fairness in game. You can achieve everything without paying in a reasonable time. Its just like a p2p mmo but paying users get a small advantage. Pretty fair imo.

Uriel’s Chasm is a game that many people will not love and will not enjoy. It’s a different sort of game and it doesn’t happen very often that I play a game this weird. Naturally, the word ‘weird’ can be interpreted both ways here, but I mean it in a negative sense, I’m afraid.
The game is approximately 30 minutes long and it’s unclear, unfocused, amateuristic  and, above all, pretentious.
It’s supposedly about religion and faith. That’s what the ‘story’ led me to believe anyway. But this story mostly consists of (seemingly random) Bible verses, sometimes spoken by a person that clearly has no passion doing this.
The FMVs are also uninteresting and, in my opinion, hardly add anything to the entire game.
Gameplay-wise the game consists of several genres; you start the game in a ship shown for a top-down perspective and it’s your goal to collect more faith than what’s in the garden. This can be done by shooting meteorites while also avoiding them and one, large, rotating monster (I think ?).
Meteorites will sometimes drop bible verses, which you can then collect to increase your faith meter. You have to take into account that moving will decrease your fuel meter and hitting enemies will decrease your faith meter. Shooting your guns will also deplete your ammo meter. If any meter completely depletes it is game over.
If you’ve collected enough faith the game will continue to the next part which is a side-scrolling shooter. The goal there is shoot your enemies or to just avoid their gunfire and kill the boss at the end of the level. Looks simple, but the collision detection is poor and as a result is sometimes fairly frustrating.
The last part is a platformer. You just jump around finding trees/crosses that show you verses from the Bible. There are no enemies and you can’t die here. But the level does rotate so it might be a bit confusing and disorienting to some. This should be simple enough for most of us.
Like I said, all of this takes approximately 30 minutes or 1 hour max if maybe you don’t play many games.
The graphics are retro and in 2D, which look ok. Some of the graphics are a bit hideous but overall it all looks decent enough.
And despite what you would think the music is pretty good. But that’s about the only real thing I enjoyed I guess.
The user interface is obtrusive and way out of proportion and clutters the screen. This is completely unnecessary. The text is also annoying to read, because it changes colors every second and, yes, this is also too big for the screen.
So, if you still haven’t got the impression that I didn’t enjoy this game then this review is probably worthless to you. But if it did make sense to you then I suggest you stay away from this game. Even if it goes on sale (which shouldn’t take that long if I had to take a guess).

How to begin with Echo of Soul...
I suppose to begin, I'm gong to give my rating on this game:  8/10 (reserving judgment due to the status of the game being Open Beta) => RECOMMENDED
I've had a bit of a love-hate relationship with Aeria Games since I first became a member in 2008.  Echo of Soul is the third of their published games which I've played for more than 2 days.  In fact, I've been playing this game since their Open Beta launch on June 1st.  But this isn't about my history with others of Aeria's games, this review is about this one in particular.  Let's begin, shall we?
=====CHARACTER CREATION=====
The first thing you'll notice about Echo of Soul is that there are a total of five classes (thus far) to choose from.  These classes are gender-locked, and each class has two spec mastery paths.  The gender lock is there to follow with the game's storyline.  The classes you can choose from are as follows:
1.  Male Warrior
2.  Male Rogue
3.  Female Guardian (Lancer, for those familiar with Tera)
4.  Female Mage
5.  Female Archer
As you will begin to notice, there is no dedicated healing class.  More on this later.
Each class has different customization options available to further make your character unique in physical appearance.  You then start off with a default costume (I can assume this to be random from a small pool, as I've created different characters of the same class, and ended up with differing clothing looks from the get-go.)
=====LEVELING=====
Leveling in Echo of Soul is very much geared toward the casual player.  For the hardcore speedlevelers, it's possible to make it from levels 1 to 60 (current cap, at time of review) in a matter of 1-3 days through the game's PvP Battlegrounds (accessible starting at level 10.)  For the more casual player, you can still make it to 60 relatively quickly or you can take your time with it.  Moderate-speed casual players can make it inside of a week.  Slow casuals can make it to cap in abotu 2 weeks of gameplay time.
Both PvP and PvE Questing offer a very generous amount of EXP, so reaching cap is entirely on how you want to do it.  You can go solely as a Battlegrounds resident, through the PvE story, or mix it up a bit.  For the best leveling experience, I would recommend doing either PvP or PvE (depending on which one you want to stick to primarily) just to try it out.
Grinding mobs in the overworld will provide very little in the way of EXP.  Grinding overworld mobs is an easy option to obtain enhancement jewels, crafting ingredients, or even some crafting recipes.  If you wish to do PvE grind for EXP, then your best bet would be to do so in the dungeons.  Though, grinding out the dungeons might not be a bad idea, as the sub and main bosses can provide your character with class-specific equipment sets to further enhance your stats and abilities.  There is also the option to take repeatables in maps called Infinite Hunting Grounds which also reward a fair amount of EXP per turn-in.
=====ECONOMY=====
There are a couple of things which new players will find out relatively quickly:
1.  Mobs do not drop money.
2.  Items from NPC vendors are really cheap.
This means it will be relatively difficult to make solid gold before your 50-60 level bracket.  I would assume it to be a tactic by the developers to maintain a relatively strong pre-endgame economy.  With that being said, there is no restrictions on the amount of in-game gold you can carry in difference to those at level cap.  If you wish to make some quick major gold for your earlier levels, your best bet would be to utilize the cash shop and in-game auction board.
As I have not hit level cap, as of yet (I'm a -very- slow player, and have taken more time to get to know the forum community due to my work/sleep schedules) I will not post a comment on endgame economy.
=====QUESTING=====
PvE questing is quite linear, and very story-based.  While you do get a vast amount of miscellaneous quests (both overworld and dungeon) the magic of PvE questing truly shines with the story-based quests.  As with most typical MMORPGs, you get EXP, money, and the occasional piece of gear to upgrade your set.  However, it's also relatively easy to outlevel some of these quests, but the EXP you gain from some of the lower-level quests is still quite generous.
=====Player-versus-Player=====
Echo of Soul offers two types of PvP:  Battlegrounds and Open-World Guild vs Guild.  Let's expand, shall we?
Currently, there are two Battlegrounds maps (both accessible starting at level 10.)  Both are points-based Capture the Flag-esque types.  One requires teams to capture resources spawned on the map, and the other requires teams to capture and hold towers for as long as possible.  The actual player-kill aspect of these battlegrounds can be quite hectic and fast-paced.  There are also two tiers of Battlegrounds- one for Levels 10-59, and one exclusively for Level 60.
Open-World GvG takes place between guilds which have declared themselves to be hostile.  Players in hostile guilds are fair game to be PK'd at any time, anywhere by other hostile guilds' members.  Guildless and Peaceful-alligned guild players do not have to worry about being randomly PK'd while running around the overworld maps.
There is also a PvP event (run at least daily) called Valhalla.  Since I have yet to participate in this event, I cannot write a review about it.
=====CRAFTING=====
Like the rest of the game, crafting is geared toward the more casual player.  Relatively cheap and brainless, it's fairly easy to level both a profession and the two hobby crafting skills available in a short amount of time.  Certain tiers of crafting require certain character levels to be obtained.  Beginner-level crafters can gain most of their supplies directly from their crafting vendor.  However, there does come a time where some mob grinding is required to get higher level base materials.
=====UNIQUE FEATURES=====
1.  Echo of Soul has a hunger system.  This is determined by two values:  Energy and Satiety.  The higher your current energy level is to your max, certain buffs are applied to your character.  You increase energy by eating foods which are crafted or obtained as quest rewards.  Satiety is how much food you can eat.  With a max value of 1,000 and each piece of food taking up 200 Satiety, this leaves you with a maximum of 5 food waten at a time.  Satiety can be decreased over time, or with the use of a Digestant item.  Energy is depleted through the use of skills.
2.  The Soul System:  Through daily rewards or killing of mobs, you can obtain what's called "Chaos Souls."  When purified (either near a purification point, or cooperatively with another player) these souls can grant you charges for temporary buffs.
3.  The Cash Shop:  While most free-to-play MMOs out there have a cash shop which is mostly geared to be pay-to-win, Echo of Souls isn't geared that way.  Mostly asthetics or RNG fun, there is literally nothing on the cash shop which you are required to get to advance in the game, or gain a significant advantage.  The things on the shop which seem that way are literally a pay-to-be-lazy mechanic.
4.  No Dedicated Healer Class:  The entire party works as a team to heal!
=====THE BADS=====
1.  There is no general server chat channel.  Primary communication is done at either close-range, through the use of the Loudspeaker items, or on the map-specific Shout channel.  Unless you get yourself into an active guild, or are part of a different chat system (i.e. Teamspeak) prepare to be playing mostly in blisful chat silence towards you.
2.  Your other Typicals:  Elitists, gold spammers, and general complaining doomsday naysayers.
=====TL;DR=====
If you're a casual gamer looking for a casual game which you can level relatively easily without getting too far behind the curve, then Echo of Soul is a good pick for you!

You start in one room and you have to kill everything that spawns in there, then you move on to the next room, which will be a bit more difficult. Little 2D Jump N Run sequences allow you to collect even more coins.

At the moment the game is on sale for 1,79 EUR. This is a mere steal for such a great arcade shooter. You might not play it for hours and hours, but it is really one of those I just like to play for three, four rounds in between of other games.

I've always been fascinated by the idea of an assymetric PvP Game, and
has been on my radar since reading about it in Game Infomer in January of 2014.
And i have got to say, Turtle Rock has delivered, the game is an absolute
to play.
In the premier "Hunt" Game mode it's 4 v 1 -- 4 hunters ranging in classes from support to damage, and your goal is to hunt down the monster and destroy it. If you're the monster, your job is to either wipe out the hunters or destroy the com relay.
I really enjoy the game, like a ton, and I am glad i ended up picking it up after waffling around following "DLC-gate" (more on that in a bit.). To be quite frank, the game gives me an adrenaline rush, particularly when i play with a competent team against a good monster(or vice versa but i'm a terrible monster). The classes are fun, and the way the leveling system is set up really forces you to understand the role before you can unlock the more advanced variations of said role. It sort of reminds me of the way Battlefield 3 did unlocks in terms of functionality, but it just doesn't feel as grindy. Also, the game looks spectacular, though i guess thats subjective.
So far i have always ended up with balanced teams (I play on PC) when i play with randoms, and for me at least, I've almost always been paired with some pretty fun folks when they had coms active. The gameplay itself also, has largely felt balanced-- though vs wraith is frustrating, but apparently there is a nerf coming.
I have found that the game has a pretty steep learning curve. Yeah sure, you can get the basics of each class/monster down in a couple of games, but if you approach Evolve as a generic cookie cutter CoD Shooter,
. Everything from sounds to carcasses to broken tree branches can point you in the direction of the monster. A good team can split in two and drive the monster into your own ambush-- where you place your arena matters just as much as placing it(Don't do it in a cavern!), and understanding when to engage and when to flee is incredibly important, And those are just a couple of examples. Really, Turtle Rock did a great job of delivering the feeling of an FPS with the strategic depth of a solid moba... and if you don't play moba's, they tend to have insane amount of depth.
This however, brings me to my next point.
It's possible to have great games with randoms, i've had a couple-- but if you really want a consistently fun experience, and really amp up your strategic depth, get your friends to buy the game or find a group on reddit or Gridom. That having been said, so far i still usually play solo and i still quite enjoy the experience.
like the rest of most, i was initially really turned off when this came out, but i have since made peace with it. The game in my opinion, carries tons of merit on it's own, and if you look at the majority of the negative reviews on steam they will all echo this sentiment, before launching into complaints about the DLC. These are some of the top negative reviews:
“Great Game, Solid all round in gameplay, competitive and a lot of replayability with different strats/compesitions...” - Mr. Farenheit
“Let me be perfectly honest, I absolutely had a blast playing this game in Alpha and Beta..” - Giddy Wraith
“So far I'm really liking this game...” - N8
The reason why i changed my mind is largely... well, honestly, it's several things. A major reason is because i later read somewhere that the reason why it was made so (DLC) compatible is so that they have the funding available to continually expand the game, rather than go on a bi-annual release like CoD or BF do (to name the two most prominent examples). And i can get behind that. I understand tyhat the cost of development has gone up, and that eventually intial sales of the game will taper off, so if devs want to continue expanding on the game they need to generate new revenue somehow through DLC-- or abandon the game and begin developing a brand new title (Evolve: Black ops the presequel anyone?!). The second, and perhaps this is a leap of faith on my part, but i sincerely believe that turtlerock studios really really cares about this game, just judging from how amped they are when i saw them speak on their twitch stream or whatever, how much emphasis they keep putting on wanting feedback from the community for balancing purposes... and i just don't think there is a deliberate attempt to fleece us by the devs-- hell, if anyone was watching the launch day stream yesterday, they are ultimately just a bunch of nerds that really ♥♥♥♥ing love video games.
I also want to point out that all DLC currently available, contrary to popular belief, is cosmetic. So what? I mean if the fact that you have to pay 5$ extra to plau 'wendigo' goliath (or whatever it is) detracts THAT much from your gaming experience, then you should reevaluate your priorities. And even beyond
I think turtle rock created a really fun and original multiplayer game, with tons of strategic depth, and is a game i think most of you would actually enjoy if you'd give it a chance. DLC isn't inherently a bad thing.
So if the premise of the game interests you, check out some videos on youtube, and if it interests you enough to buy it, please do so!

There's too many overly proportioned arguments being cried about this game that are either inflated or completely false, here's few biggest ones:
Argument #1: The game is uneven / monster this or that is OP
WRONG. The game is not symmetric, it is even. When you team 4 players against 1 you can't have symmetric game, it wouldn't work. The monsters are more powerful by default, but they are alone against many. No matter how much you would try to balance the opposing factions, you would always have certain disparity due to the way the game is made, AND IT IS A GOOD THING! A skillful player can employ the strenghts of a monster to his/her victory or a trained team of hunters can score a kill through good communication and teamwork.
Mayby the biggest cries of inexperienced players are projected towards Wraith. Wraith is not overpowered, check the in-game scoreboards, the statistics in top 15 rankings between the 3 current monsters in the game do not deviate from each other.
Here's a good example of how to take down a skillful Wraith:
Argument #2: The game is broken/glitchy/buggy.
WRONG. The game had an exceptionally good release especially when compared to other multiplayer games recently. You could jump in and start playing on the release day without too long queues or game breaking bugs!
Many people like to cling on the mouse cursor bug which is a real thing but not nearly big enough deal to not make you buy the game and will surely be fixed in an upcoming patch.
Argument #3:  The business model for the game is a money grab.
OVERINFLATED. This side of this publication has grown so out of proportion in game reviews around here. Many comments focus on the subjective opinion of how much one should pay for their entertainment and the whole issue has very little bearing on how one experiences the game itself. I've got over 50 hours gameplay behind me now, that's ~1€ per hour so far and going down because I'm nowhere near of getting bored of the game. To me that is money well spent!

Rewrote the review, and changed the rating.
First off, this game makes...not always sense.
For example, make an egg in this game, all you need is seasoning (which magically turns into an egg apparently)
To make a hamburger, all you need is bread. You know what my favourite kind of hamburger is? The one without any kind of meat, or lettuce, or sauce, JUST bread. Yummy.
Not to mention you can make three kinds of burgers (BBQ, Bacon ...) and they all need only one ingredient - bread.
As a person who loves crafting this is bad. You know what else is bad? Get this:
There are three professions in this game, of which you can only learn one, and two hobbies of which you can learn both.
Two of the professions need resources you can gather in the wild. Guess what the third profession is. Yep, its Resource gathering.
So either you become a resource gatherer and can make nothing out of it but sell things, or you become an alchemist or jeweler and can make nothing because you can't gather resources. If they want to create an active, living market, this is NOT the way to do it, and it somewhat cancels out a certain type of freedom, too, if you want to gather and make your own stuff out of it.
However, after playing a bit I have to say that, otherwise, the game is quite solid. The fighting is fun, the graphics are slightly above average but are used well, the game feels fluid despite using the good old tab targeting fighting system, and it constantly rewards you and keeps you engaged. It is still somewhat generic, but I rate games based on how fun they are, and...well, I am having fun.
How long that will motivate me? I don't know, but for now, I am motivated to play until the first dungeon (apparently Lvl. 35) and, for an MMO these days, that says a lot for me. Will update this as I go along.
Edit 1, 23th June 2015: PVP seems pretty well done. I have seen people saying that melee has an extreme disadvantage, but after playing a few matches, I have seen none of that. Of course, I am nowhere near experienced to really say for certain but it seems pretty fair to me for both melee and ranged, and PVP is kinda fun.
Edit 2, 29th June 2015: I played the game more, and rolled a new character. They all feel distinctively different which is certainly a good thing. I still recommend this game.
Edit 3, 07th July 2015: I think my final verdict on it is that it is certainly a good and fun way to pass time if you don't look for anything deep. Everyone else should stay away, because its very same-y.

I was actually a bit upset when I finally got around to playing this game. Everything I heard about it was positive. The controls were new and inventive, it was humorous, the level design was great. But the more I played it, the more stuff I found that I really did not like at all.
The controls are awful. You use WSAD to move and jump, and the spacebar makes you dance, because I suppose the devs thought the 2 second dance from the beginning of the game was hilarious enough to throw into the control scheme. Dancing is like a taunt in fighting games. It doesnt do anything. You then use the mouse to guide the giant laser that you shoot. Only your cursor also moves with your character. Not with the screen, your character. If you move left, the cursor moves left. WHO THOUGHT THAT WOULD BE A GOOD IDEA? It makes the physics-based puzzles so much harder than they actually are. But aside from the controls, there were a lot of other things I started questioning.
-Why is the game locked to 720p? It just makes it look dated and confined.
-Why are the alternate weapons just used as gimmicks for specific puzzles?
-If the devs opted to include voice acting, why dont their mouths move?
-Why do I have infinite lives for the entire game, but only 3 for boss fights?
-Why are the boss fights the only actual enemies in the game?
-Why doesnt the level selection have any info on the level you are playing? I cant even tell which one I left off on when I go back to play the game.
Then there is the game's "humor" if I can even call it that. This game has 2 jokes throughout the entire game. The first is the rampant screaming you hear your future self yell in the first few levels, which jus gets annoying when you realize the devs only recorded about 12 phrases that just get looped over and over again. The second joke comes directly from the title, and what I mean by that is they dont explain anything and just expect you to find it humorous and accept it, which I dont. WHY IS a giant crab trying to kill me? WHY IS there a random UFO? WHY IS there a giant groundhog with a drill in its mouth as a boss? If you didnt want to explain anything, why make so much stuff that needs explaining? Random does not equal funny.
On a final note, the game is not terrible, but it has enough problems to a point where it feels like a beta. I expected more from a "remastered" game. That being said, the game's strong point is the levels. Playing through them was fun, and if it was just that it would be an awesome arcade-style game. But with the immense number of bad things I found in the game, I can not recommend it.

EOS is a new cutesy anime style MMORPG with the classic MMO elements but a slight difference. You can relate it to WoW in terms of combat(for some part), nothing is seemingly new for such a new MMO, I will say its very well done for what it is. My long review, I hope this helps any one on edge about playing or not. Also consider it a mini basic things to know of the game.
Cash shop?
Yes. P2W? I wouldn't say yes or no it this. Everything in game can be purchased with gold through the market from other players, some cash shop items through the "magic egg system", and others from events. Basically anything from the cash shop can be gotten with gold,  and at a much, much slower and less probable rate via Magic Lamps(purchased with eggs)
PvP?
Yes Battlegrounds, Arena,  and its well done to a point. A player over level 10 may join the BG's and its a great way to level. Gems can be used on Equipment to improve your stats as well. Anything over +5 means you will need a Safeguard(use magic eggs, cash shop, Lamps(random), market, to get) to ensure that your gems do not break when you upgrade them, but no guarentee they will upgrade. This system can greatly unbalance PvP but as long as you do your share of the work you will be rewarded, win or lose. I cannot say for that you are guarenteed rewards in arena with a lose though as I have yet to do that. Its a lot of fun but you may also find yourself wanting to bash your head off the wall at some of the players.
Guild Battles?
Yes! Open world guild pvp makes it a bit harder if you are lower level and new to the game. However avoiding a hostile guild is best until you are familiar and comfortable with the game and your class.
Guilds can compete in Valhalaa, where guilds will compete to kill a daily spawn boss for amazing rewards that will benefit your guild.
Dungeons?
Yes! My favourite part of this game is the level 60 dungeons. The game does start you small, giving you regular and heroic soloable dungeons to do starting from level 10 until 60! This is a great way to learn boss fights and mechanics until you can get to level 60 and begin heroic party dungeons. The game holds your hand though in the fights and will tell you what to do and when to do it, so long as you can read! Epic PvE armor will drop at random during each level 60 party dungeon. There is a weekly limit cap on how many of each specific dungeon you can do, starting at 4. You can increase this with dungeon tickets x 2(bought from market, magic eggs, found in lamps) or reset one of your uses with 1 ticket. You will get 30 gold per dungeon I believe. 10gish per boss. Its great for earning gold and then you can afford to upgrade gems or buy cool things this way!
Raids?
Coming Soon~
Profesions?
Yes, you will be able to choose 2 hobbies and 1 profession. The 2 hobbies are Cooking and Soul Processing. Both are important and should always be learned right away. The 3 Professions are Resource Collector, Jeweler, Alchemist. Unfortunately there is no armor, weapon or bag crafting but those come easy enough. I would have loved to see FISHING Q.Q
Cooking: Energy and Satiety play a big role in buffing your attack and HP. Energy is used when you use any skill! Satiety fades slowly with time and will determine your hunger level. If you are full you cannot eat any more food to increase your energy, energy is what specifically increases your attack and HP. You can either use a Digestant(Cash shop item, market item, lamps.) to lower your satiety, or wait it out. Digestants can also be obtained from questing in the highest level questing zone.
I feel like I should shut up at some point so maybe now. Overall its a newer game in a old school MMORPG style, great for killing time and probably getting really in to. You will find nothing new here but if you love Anime and MMO's then this just might be your game. At least until Blade & Soul or Black Desert. . .

In this game, you are presented with "cards" that each represent a choice that you must make as the king of your country. I can't say I've played a game quite like this before.

After the year 1200 (about an hour and a half of playing), I quickly began to grow bored of the same swipe-left-swipe-right mechanic that the game is based upon. Although the game is fun initially, you'll likely grow bored of it over a couple hours. Nonetheless, the characters and the humor is what makes the game what it is. This game can be seen as a mixture of three games, namely "Bubble Bobble", "Garrison" and "North and South". Why is that? Take the music, the food, the items as well as the "BONUS" achievement and compare them to Bubble Bobble: The music is similar by the choice of tune, and the food is basically the same, as one finds apples and cake and so on. Speaking of the identity of the items, one may find a crown or a cross for example, and last but not least, the "BONUS" achievement is comparable to the "EXTEND" achievement (as one is supposed to pick up the corresponding letters that appaer occasionally).
The comparison with Garrison is obvious from the identity of the game goals, i.e. running around throwing axes, arrows or swords to crush the enemy.
Furthermore, the bonus level design is based on the Fortress Capture challenges of North and South (i.e. running from left to right avoiding getting caught by the left border of the screen).
All in all it's a well made composition of games of the past to enjoy.

I've always been fascinated by the idea of an assymetric PvP Game, and
has been on my radar since reading about it in Game Infomer in January of 2014.
And i have got to say, Turtle Rock has delivered, the game is an absolute
to play.
In the premier "Hunt" Game mode it's 4 v 1 -- 4 hunters ranging in classes from support to damage, and your goal is to hunt down the monster and destroy it. If you're the monster, your job is to either wipe out the hunters or destroy the com relay.
I really enjoy the game, like a ton, and I am glad i ended up picking it up after waffling around following "DLC-gate" (more on that in a bit.). To be quite frank, the game gives me an adrenaline rush, particularly when i play with a competent team against a good monster(or vice versa but i'm a terrible monster). The classes are fun, and the way the leveling system is set up really forces you to understand the role before you can unlock the more advanced variations of said role. It sort of reminds me of the way Battlefield 3 did unlocks in terms of functionality, but it just doesn't feel as grindy. Also, the game looks spectacular, though i guess thats subjective.
So far i have always ended up with balanced teams (I play on PC) when i play with randoms, and for me at least, I've almost always been paired with some pretty fun folks when they had coms active. The gameplay itself also, has largely felt balanced-- though vs wraith is frustrating, but apparently there is a nerf coming.
I have found that the game has a pretty steep learning curve. Yeah sure, you can get the basics of each class/monster down in a couple of games, but if you approach Evolve as a generic cookie cutter CoD Shooter,
. Everything from sounds to carcasses to broken tree branches can point you in the direction of the monster. A good team can split in two and drive the monster into your own ambush-- where you place your arena matters just as much as placing it(Don't do it in a cavern!), and understanding when to engage and when to flee is incredibly important, And those are just a couple of examples. Really, Turtle Rock did a great job of delivering the feeling of an FPS with the strategic depth of a solid moba... and if you don't play moba's, they tend to have insane amount of depth.
This however, brings me to my next point.
It's possible to have great games with randoms, i've had a couple-- but if you really want a consistently fun experience, and really amp up your strategic depth, get your friends to buy the game or find a group on reddit or Gridom. That having been said, so far i still usually play solo and i still quite enjoy the experience.
like the rest of most, i was initially really turned off when this came out, but i have since made peace with it. The game in my opinion, carries tons of merit on it's own, and if you look at the majority of the negative reviews on steam they will all echo this sentiment, before launching into complaints about the DLC. These are some of the top negative reviews:
“Great Game, Solid all round in gameplay, competitive and a lot of replayability with different strats/compesitions...” - Mr. Farenheit
“Let me be perfectly honest, I absolutely had a blast playing this game in Alpha and Beta..” - Giddy Wraith
“So far I'm really liking this game...” - N8
The reason why i changed my mind is largely... well, honestly, it's several things. A major reason is because i later read somewhere that the reason why it was made so (DLC) compatible is so that they have the funding available to continually expand the game, rather than go on a bi-annual release like CoD or BF do (to name the two most prominent examples). And i can get behind that. I understand tyhat the cost of development has gone up, and that eventually intial sales of the game will taper off, so if devs want to continue expanding on the game they need to generate new revenue somehow through DLC-- or abandon the game and begin developing a brand new title (Evolve: Black ops the presequel anyone?!). The second, and perhaps this is a leap of faith on my part, but i sincerely believe that turtlerock studios really really cares about this game, just judging from how amped they are when i saw them speak on their twitch stream or whatever, how much emphasis they keep putting on wanting feedback from the community for balancing purposes... and i just don't think there is a deliberate attempt to fleece us by the devs-- hell, if anyone was watching the launch day stream yesterday, they are ultimately just a bunch of nerds that really ♥♥♥♥ing love video games.
I also want to point out that all DLC currently available, contrary to popular belief, is cosmetic. So what? I mean if the fact that you have to pay 5$ extra to plau 'wendigo' goliath (or whatever it is) detracts THAT much from your gaming experience, then you should reevaluate your priorities. And even beyond
I think turtle rock created a really fun and original multiplayer game, with tons of strategic depth, and is a game i think most of you would actually enjoy if you'd give it a chance. DLC isn't inherently a bad thing.
So if the premise of the game interests you, check out some videos on youtube, and if it interests you enough to buy it, please do so!

This a fun little filler of game that takes place in dungeon with connecting rooms.  Your job is simply to kill all the mobs in the room and then grab the key to exit to another room.  You keep doing this until you reach the boss, which, after beating, will grant you access to the next floor.  There are four floors in this game, and runs can take you anywhere from a few minutes to a half hour, so it's great to pick up and play when you want something quick and light.
There are bonus levels and shops along the way to upgrade your stats such as speed, damage, rate of fire, health, and other goodies.  If you save your money, you can buy permanent stats that will help you with future runs, which is nice since you lose everything when you die.  The neat thing is you find yourself progressing fast enough, so you don't feel like it's a long grind.
Overall this is a simple game with decent replayability and just enough depth to make it enjoyable.  It's perfect for me because I like to play a few quick rounds and then come back later.  I certainly recommended this game.

Empire at War is probably the Star Wars' most serious foray into the strategy genre, and I hate to say it's mixed at best. While the battlescapes make for some really impressive visuals, the game falls flat on its face on the tactical map.
It's one of the worst I've ever seen in a strategy game. It's real time with a pause, which wouldn't be an issue execpt the game refuses to let you make any meaningful orders while paused. It will only be an hour or so before you started getting bombarded with battle prompts (which you can autoresolve) back-to-back, and it just becomes completely unmanagable as your attention is constantly divided. It seriously plays like a turn-based system that was retooled to realtime at the very last second, and its shows. I cannot understate how frustrating it is to deal with.
And while the battlescape is fun to play on, it also has issues. Pathfinding for you or the AI is atrocious, and you'll often have to bear ships taking a full minute to turn around when they could have just moved forward. On top of some pretty awful unit balance, battles are always completely lopsided and predictable.
Do not get this on anything but the cheapest of sales. The cool battles might draw you in, but the game turns into a slog very, very quickly.

Having just finished the game no more than an hour ago, I felt it appropriate that I write an honest review. "Sir (or Madam), You Are Being Hunted" is a 'procedurally-generated' first person shooter, set in a hilariously extreme British world, where robot gentlemen hunt humans for sport.
The game does a lot of things right. The setting is unique, as is the plot. Your job, as the human, is to survive against the robotic apocalypse and track down fragments of a teleportation device that will get you safely out of this 'tweedpunk' nightmare. There are 25 fragments, scattered across five islands. If and when you are caught, the robots will not hesitate to shoot. Should you lose all your health and fall to the ground, you'll be sent back to the place where you last saved.
An impressive array of weapons awaits you, however, should you pick and choose your battles wisely. There are weapons ranging from the close-encounter woodcutter's axe to the fine hunting rifle, along with a pistol, shotgun, and blunderbuss. Ammo is scarce, and should be conserved.
Along with ammo and weaponry, there are foodstuffs and bandages. If you've ever played Minecraft, you understand that eating food doesn't refill your health. It refills your hunger, which when close to 100%, heals your health. Sir, You Are Being Hunted is very similar. As you traverse the British countryside, your vitality will drop. Eating food will raise that, which will in turn raise your health, should you be recovering from an encounter.
tl;dr, This game is great. You'll laugh, you'll jump, and you'll have a heck of a lot of fun. I totally recommend this game, to anyone who enjoys stealthy shoot and loot type games.

Iron Fisticle is a poorly conceived cocktail recipe. Mix 2 shots twinstick arena shooter with a one shot rogue-lite, add a dash of RPG and thoroughly muddle until murky and mediocre.
It’s passable at everything it does, but it does it all with a resounding lack of flair. Yes, the screen is awash with enemies, but the enemies are dull and uninspired, and often don’t present any interesting problem - simply kiting around the edge of the screen and firing inwards will get you through most rooms. Deaths are often the result  of sloppiness borne out of boredom, rather than the game throwing you a curveball.
Then there’s the RPG elements. These should make the game more fun, but in fact, make it less fun. You can purchase permanent power-ups for all subsequent runs, and the upshot of this is that it makes a game of Iron Fisticle (a) last longer and (b) be even more tedious for the first level, as you’re now overpowered for it. That’s right, upgrades make the game *less enjoyable*.
That said, there’s a spot in everyone’s game library for something like Iron Fisticle, that game to play when you’re too tired and/or drunk to be bothered to play anything enjoyable, challenging or rewarding, and you just want something to do with your thumbs while you turn your brain off.

The purpose of puzzle games is to offer a simple concept, sometimes adding a few twists, slowly increasing the difficulty over time and providing a sense of satisfaction to the player when the puzzle is resolved.
LYNE offers the simple concept - join one end of a connector to another, hitting all the correct points along the way. It fails in executing any of the other things well.
The game seems to become very difficult very quickly, especially for those who are not good with spacial awareness. The twist added is a special block that can take more than one line passing through it. It can take two three or four connections to satisfy the game's criteria of every point must be connected. This leads to the biggest problem with the game - you can see the solution, you just seem to end up at the same point no matter which way you to try to rearrange the lines.
The end result is that instead of a sense of accomplishment or satisfaction at solving the puzzle, you are almost always bashing your head in with frustration, or looking at the level indicator at the top of the screen and hoping that you reach the end of the course of 25 rounds quickly.
The game becomes tedious and boring very quickly, and the music has a tendency of exacerbating those feelings. I tend to play with the in-game music muted and playing my own music in the background.
Do not buy this game, even if you are a spacially aware gamer - the game will tire you out quickly, and there are much better puzzle games available on Steam that cost less.
