I hesitated a lot before buying this game. Being not much of a crafter guy I had misgivings. Furthermore, being in early access and all, I had some bad experiences before. Last, I feared that it would not be that much interesting or challenging. No real ennemies and all that. Boy, I was WRONG!
I thought I knew about survival, I thought those zombie games had prepared me. Not in the least, they hadn't.
First try, I found a gun, went all rambo after I missed a wolf and decided to track it down. I got lost, got surrounded by wolves and got killed. Ok I learnt to respect them. There were some ennemies after all. New game, I thought I knew what to expect but no, I still hadn't met the most fearsome foe of all: the cold.
After I found a very comfy cabine beside a frozen lake I decided to go to one of the small fishing huts. It was 500 meters away, tops. So I decided to dump most of the clutter in my backpack (you know, silly useless things such as spare clothes,wood, soda cans, food in general). So here I go in the bright morning to do some fishing. I did fish, but when I looked up from my fishing hole an end of the world blizzard was bellowing outside. Complete whiteout, I started to get very cold. So I looked through my pack, found some wood and (I was lucky there was a heating apparatus in that hut) started warming up while cooking the fish. Two hours later, visibility still a big fat zero.
So started the most adrenaline filled, terrifying moment I've had with a video game in a long time. I decided to hoof it back to the cabine through the wind and the snow.
Five meters toward the shore. Ten. Can't see the hut behind me, cant see the shore either, I'm hoping I'm not getting lost. At last I see some trunks. I take a right to get back to the cabine. I"m getting colder, I start shaking then growing numb. Rocks, trees, snow, still no cabine.
AT LAST over there I think I can see the roof... No. Just another boulder. At that point I was completely exhausted, badly dehydrated and almost frozen to death. It felt like I'd been going for hours. I kept telling myself "nah, its just 500 meters, that's not much, you must be real close!". And when I could barely walk anymore, my bag seemingly weighting a ton, then I saw it. THE CABINE only 10 PACES AHEAD! I made it. It was really useful to try and memorize how I could use the  shore as a rail to go back but still... I was shaking with relief as my character collapsed in a bed to get ten hours of shuteye.
Last thing, I thought I'd never say that but it's the first game to make me go "OMG YES, A FROZEN HALF ROTTEN DEAR! T'IS MY LUCKY DAY!". For a game in early access it has a great feel to it. It already beats a lot of AAA titles, the replayability looks great from where I stand. Buy without hesitation, support the devs!

For people who don’t care for a long, detailed review: I rate this game a 4/5 for fun gameplay with a few personal irritations.
For people who ARE interested in my more in-depth opinion, read on (There are absolutely no spoilers for plot in this review):
So I spotted this game as a featured title on sale, and as it was only about four dollars, I bought it. I'm a fan of indie games, and it was cheap, so why not? Not a bad decision, in my opinion—though I’m not very far, yet.
I think that to call it a Legend-of-Zelda-esque game is a bit misleading. It seems, to me, to be more of a mix of Final Fantasy and Zelda. The combat is very reminiscent of Zelda games (same attacking style, get money and items for killing monsters, can definitely get messed up if you go too far too fast, very little guidance for your quest, etc.), but I feel that other aspects of the game (the menu, the equips, the graphics, and the adventure itself) are far closer to the older, handheld Final Fantasy games, like FFIII for the GBA (Or FFVII for the SNES for people who follow Japanese release titles). It makes for a very fun combination when playing.
Regardless of which well-known titles it is like, it is a fun play, and engaging enough that I’ll definitely be heading back to play some more before too long, and I definitely recommend it for people who read this review. I'll be nudging my my family members to buy and download this game. The music is catchy and fits the areas you’re in, the game play is fun, and it’s always satisfying to smack things until you get that sweet, sweet level up sound/animation! The characters are very simple, but that simply adds to the reminiscent charm of older games, and it’s nice to see some attitude from the NPCs.
With that said, there are a few quirks I’d like to point out. As I mentioned earlier, there is very little guidance within the game. For people like me, who’ve been gamming their entire lives and have a certain level of scorn for manuals (born from being an impatient child who wanted to smack things sooner, rather than later), this wasn’t a problem: I just hit buttons until I found what I wanted, and carried on (who needs a booklet’s help to be am RPG hero?). That method of gaming might not work for some, however. There is no in-game tutorial on how to use your weapon, shield, or items aside from being directed to a file that comes with the game on what the default key-bindings are. A few, very brief tutorial windows will pop up here and there for how to open your menu and a couple other basic things, but that’s it. In relation to that, you’ll need to do some searching for your quest progression, whether that be collecting stuff, or talking to some person; there is very little hand holding here (which I love). Also, you cannot name your character, which was a little disappointing, but oh, well. Another minor problem is that the music doesn't loop very well.
For the creator, I don’t know if you’re still updating/working on this game, but I have a few suggestions I’d like to make (I apologize is this seems pushy to you, and you definitely do not need to take any heed of me.):
One: Adding in a prompt right off the bat about where to find the controls, or even having it as a menu option on the title screen or in the menu in-game. might not be a bad plan.
Two: Making the default controls a little more ergonomic/conveniently placed would definitely be a plus. It’s fairly hard to hit the buttons I want with how they are set up. “A” being the sprint button, while “Z” is the shield makes for a strange yoga session for my fingers, and I keep accidentally using my items. I haven’t looked into re-binding the buttons, if that’s even a thing I can do (I’m not quite sure where in the files the controls file is), so this may not be much of a problem, yet. Also, a quick Quest Log and a quick save button would be nice, which, again, might already be things that I simply need to find.
Three: Make the characters name-able! Their default/recommended/canonical names can be the same/be filled in already, but the option to name your main character is a simple, but huge bonus, in my opinion. There's a certain sense of attachment and involvement when a character you've named and leveled up kicks butt that I feel just isn't there when you're simply given a name to live with.
Also, I hit F12 by accident which took me to the windowed/fullscreen option, and it took me back to the title screen! Is that supposed to happen, or is it a bug?
And I guess that’s it for my long-winded review. Time to get back to slaying monsters and saving the land!

A Survival Horror game by Red Barrels.
Yes, I did.
It's one of the most atmospheric Horror games today and gives you the feeling of being locked up with many psychopaths. There also are multiple notes and documents to collect for people that want to know more about the backstory. The graphics are very detailed and look pretty good.

The story and especially the ending of the game is quite poor and will probably leave you more confused then you already were. Apart from that there aren't any other big flaws I've noticed.

Game has somekind of immersion which pulls you in it's world. Gameplay elements are fantastic. You can struggle to survive or play peacefully, however you wish. Audio background is simply amazing, I can't even describe how many times I though wolf/bear was behind me, or how many times I felt like I'm gonna fall in the water just because I heard ice cracking right beneath my feet. This game has LOTS of potentional and devs never fail to amaze me. The Long Dark is only game which can fully pull you in it's world, make you feel the actual struggle to survive against mother nature, and I really like that. Graphics are not the best, but they are certainly unique. That drawn style adds specific element to the game which other games in same genre don't have. Even though I'd rather have realistic, detailed graphics, "drawn" graphics aren't that bad. On the other hand, game lacks fun after few months of surviving. You've basically got everything you need, you could sleep/eat/pass time anyhow in your little cabin for next few weeks without needing to get out ( Normal difficulty ). Sometimes I feel like I'm the only one in the whole world ( even though I know devs probably wanted that feel ). Sometimes I find myself walking from point A to point B and I get bored pretty easly. Few times I've duct-taped W button so I could get there faster or sometimes I used to browse Facebook and listen to music while not paying any attention to game because it was too boring to watch character slowly walk 10 kilometers.
In the end, I still think this game is great, and I'm happy to recommend it to any gamer-survival expert out there. :)

TLDR: Move on people, there is nothing to see here. Release presumably in 2020.
The sandbox is fun in it's current state, but I would consider it not even a half finished game.
As year after year passes by, this seems to be another developer that does not understand what makes people get into Early Access in the first place. It is not some convenient option to get secure funding in advance and then "maybe" work at your own pace.
The game was released in 2014 and accompanied by a kickstarter campaign but is still nowhere  near finished. Meaningful updates have not been released since December 2015 after the last new map was made public, then communication ceased to roadmaps that are highly unrealistic, given that milestones in the first slot (1-6 month) have not been adressed in over 12 months, and then in 2017 communication seams to have stopped entirely.
From the TLD roadmap ca April 2016.
We now have April 2017 and almost nothing has changed. Concerning "near windows 1-6 months", at the current rate of progress I would substitute that with "1 -6 years"
Because Steam only has those 2 options and nothing in between I have thought hard if I will now click "recommended" or "not recommended" and finally decided on the latter. I will gladly change that if the game ever gets finished before I die. So far I can only say that I enjoyed the parts that were included, but would not recommend giving another developer a free pass for not fulfilling their obligations.
Synopsis: If your not prepared to work on all cylinders then don't go to Early Access. We all would want a fixed income to finance a secure tech life for us, but gamers are currently running out of time and goodwill to finance YOUR laziness and lack of commitment.

Many people hate this game. Many people say that other MMORPGs are waaay better. I am NOT one of those.
They say that your first MMORPG is shaping your online playing. My first was WoW and I absolutely hated it. The free world was too much for me and I needed something I could explore properly. Several years later I bumped into Ragnarok Online 2 on Steam. I was a fresh Steam user and the game had been out for 2-3 weeks when I saw it. Since I have seen the anime Ragnarok: The Animation, I eagerly downloaded it and set forth.
As an inexperienced player, the game lead me along perfectly. Some things came along the way, but that made me feel like I learned something and that I grew a little more into the universe. The starter area is gorgeous and I LOVE the atmosphere there. The maps are limited, but leads somewhere. You can't get lost and there's a lot of people around to help and boost you. I have never met nicer people in an online game before.
Do you like to play solo in an online game? It's cool, you can solo your way up to the Master Levels (you might need some random help with some dungeon here and there, but no need). Do you like to play with others? Join your friends or make new ones as you play. How you play is your choice.
People also say that this is too much grinding. I say it's the same way in every game like this. You just need to find the one that suits you the best.
As you can see, I have played this game. A lot. Over 1000 hours and still counting. I vote recommend on this game, since I have a special connection with it. If you find the same, is up to you. I just hope you try it out before trashing it. But know this: I have still to find a better online community than this.

This is consummately charming. A clever homage to the self depricating fandom surrounding sentai shows that uses simple systems to provide a perfectly playable strategy game.
Some abilities from the player's side don't work as clearly as I'd like them to (especially the teamwork jumps) and some of the monster abilities feel a bit unfair but once you wrap your head around those things the game plays smoothly and is perfect for a few minutes of sentai fun.
The crafting system unfortunately is the major downfall, some items being so rare to find but so common for building that I only used the cash gear for an entire tier of equipment out of expedience rather than any meaningful, tactical choice on my part. Additionally some of the numbers and upgrades to the crafting system make absolutely no sense. After beating it I still don't know what "Crafting Rate" means.
Still, I enjoyed the meat of the game. The style (which is perfectly Behold Studios) is a lot of fun, the strategy was a good time, and I got to wax nostalgic for something I haven't really thought about for 20 years.

Because other negative reviews of this game are so bad that the reviews deserve negative reviews, I thought I would provide some input. I actually did seek this game out unlike some others, though I did acquire it in a bundle, I bought that bundle just for this game. Pretty good deal, really.
I love Super Sentai stuff, I love Voltron, I loved the new Power Rangers movie. I love tactical RPGs; Final Fantasy Tactics, Front Mission, etc. It seemed like this would be the perfect game for me. Unfortunately, there's also a tactical RPG I hate: Disgaea. Disgaea and this game only have a few things in common.
In Disgaea there is a Sentai (Power Rangers) Parody mission, and Disgaea's plot is full on joke after joke with never a serious moment. The Power Rangers mission was the best joke in the game, but it gets dull, especially when you don't find the jokes funny. Like many Indie games, Chroma Squad cannot ♥♥♥♥ing turn it off. It's full on quirky so much that even the cute jokes like Construction Walkers (Zombies Construction Workers) lose their appeal in the sea of 'hilarity'. It's too much.
Yes the writing in those older shows, and some of the newer stuff based off of them, was not Shakespeare. But, let's be real. It was not as terrible as people remember, and some of the plots are legendarily entertaining. This game does not have good writing, or good plots. It's just 'intentionally' bad. The stories Framework as being in a studio pretending to film a Sentai show wears thin, and meaningless upgrades are rendered to you via a meta joke that gets old fast. In fact, since it's an indie game you can expect endless meta jokes. In fact, the plot of this game where they cannot really tell reality from what they're doing sometimes because it's all so meaninglessly squished together itself becomes a meta joke, which begets the plot, which was another joke all along. It ends up being a confusing, incoherent mess that wasn't enjoyable. It totally fails to capture the enjoyment of the genre it's parodying and it comes off as not even understanding it.
The gameplay itself is low rent. It's missing vital options like enabling the grid, which really would have helped with coordinating movement ranges which become a major thing. Especially when mid game becomes a bounce house of everyone being tossed all over. Ultimately the gameplay is 'fill this meter by repeatedly using the same tired special skill over and over'. It's fun at first, but then it gets old fast.
Then you have the mecha fights, which should be the absolute coolest. They aren't. Do you like QTE? Because it's a QTE. And after a certain point it's in every mission.
There's something called Director's Missions which are technically required. You could ignore them but it would result in basically failing after a certain point. Some of these missions are poorly worded, and use very unclear terminology that the game hasn't actually gone out of its way to explain. Other times they're literally impossible without foreknowledge or RNG. One example was to get 6 consecutive combo on an enemy in mecha. Unfortunately I was too strong and it proved literally impossible due to the way the QTE sequence is designed to reset after each health bar is knocked off.
As far as RPGs go, there's no leveling up. It's 100% equipment based. Some of the equipment does look pretty cool as you move on, however it also all has its own unique look. So that kind of makes the squad look weird when half of them are dressed differently, again somewhat going against the theme of the game.
Sometimes the game itself doesn't even know what it's talking about. In the late game I still have trouble hitting a certain mook who's been around since chapter 2 at least, if not 1. Yet it tells me a boss has a super high hit rate and that I have to use skills, but I never once miss the boss. Now you could say 'that's just the RNG' and speaking of RNG, one of the director's missions was to never miss a hit once. Thanks, you can guess how well that went over.
I don't hate this game, but I would not recommend it to anyone unless you love indies and need to kill time. This is a weak excuse for a tactical RPG or a Sentai/Power Rangers reference. I just can't help but feel that the vision of what was announced for this game is not the end result. Not even for $15 do I think this game is worthwhile. Maybe $5.

First of all, I must acknowledge that Bioshock is indeed a great game. It's mechanically sound, contains a fine narrative and is visually pleasing even a decade after its first release. Everyone should at least try it at some point.
As for this version; be careful what you get yourself into. The game suffers from a number of problems which may or may not be limited to my computer. These include
* Losing of sound after intro
* Difficult access to changing files (If you want to for example skip the very long 2K-intro sequence)
* Crashes. Constant crashes.
* Stuttering when moving around
* Screen difficulties and crashes whenever Alt+tabbing (although, let's be honest. That's expected from PC-port to an old game)
To make these problems even worse, the game resets your configurations after each crash. The moment I had to stop playing was when the game froze with audio still on and with no possibility of reseting (Ctrl+alt+del did nothing).
All in all, maybe you'll have better luck in running this game than I did, but don't say nobody warned you.
P.S. The hacking sucks. Thankfully it was done better in later sequels

You find yourself pinned, your pistol only has three bullets.
You hear those damned voices again. You don't know how many are out there, Just that they will not stop until you are dead.
So what should you do? Run, Try to make a last stand? Could you possibly kill them all, Weaken them?
You take a peek out of the bushes and see them looking through the grove to your right. They are sweeping to area in a counter-clockwise fashion and will soon near you. So you grab a rock and lob it in their general direction, in trying to keep their soulless eyes away from your hiding place.
Success! The rock appears to distract the hunters from your impending ousting. You wait for them to turn their backs to you while they attempt to find the source of the noise.
This is your chance! You decide to take out the first hunter you see and make a break for it. You grip your pistol with both hands and start squeezing on the trigger, raising your weapon up in front of you. The crude sights aiming near the sounds of footsteps and crunching of the grass.
Now! You burst out of the brush and hastily fire off two shots into the back of one of the automatons before veering into the opposite direction of the group.
You hope you sent that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to android hell.
You assume you are southbound but you don't have time to check your compass.
"I'll try to find a path out of this place later, the only thing that matters now is that this direction is away from those monsters."
Inhuman screeching followed by gunshots breaks your train of thought as bullets whiz past you. Your speed doubles and your heart pounds faster than it has even pounded before. You were never a working man, your legs and heart used to feel as if you had just ran a marathon after you went up the stairs.
The fact that you are possibly having a heart attack is the least of your worries right now as a second volley of lead is the more immediate danger.
You make it over a hill and believe you have broken the predators line of sight.
They will catch up soon, think fast! You leap over a fence and sprint towards a nearby ditch. You lie down in an attempt to make yourself less visible and make yourself quieter. You start piling mud on top of yourself to make some impromptu camouflage.
Catching your breath you greedily inhale air for your deprived lungs. You hear voices approach and you slow your breath, hoping that they will ignore you and move past. You hear the wet thumps of metal hitting mud as the pack nears you. Your body tenses up just like the metal demons that are hunting you. You attempt to stay quiet and motionless as they search through the nearby brush searching for you before you finally hear them move on. You lay for what seems to be the longest few minutes of your life before letting out the longest sigh of your life as you reflect on these last few hours and how you nearly died multiple times. The last words you heard before you were deposited on this accursed archipelago echo through your mind.
"Sir, You are being hunted."

This game is interesting. It really isn't your basic adventure game like, say, The Elder Scrolls, I would compare it more to the likes of Minecraft or Don't Starve except for a few things, such as the night being your friend, or the complete inability to make anything. It's really a great game, but it's price really isn't quite worth if you're looking to buy this game, I say get it when you can, it's lovely, but wait a bit, until it's out of alpha, because $20 is a bit pricey. I bought this game for $10 on a weekend sale, and I don't regret it at all. But here's some more about the game. The gameplay is great, the controls are a bit odd for me, but they can be changed, and there is never a loss of excitement. Robots hunt you for sport, and you have to choose at every junction whether you want to fight back or lay low, the latter generally being the smarter choice. Believe it or not, there IS a possible ending, but don't worry. The game is in no rush to get you there, and you can simply run around the island (or 5 islands, as there are a total of 5) shooting robots if that's what you like best. This isn't really a "horror" style game as it is categorized. I'd say more adventure.  But, it sure is a heck of a lot of fun. Whether it be unlucky and scrounging for food, or simply hacking away at robots with your trusty hatchet, it's truly fun for all.

My Review for The Adventures of Tree
Taking on the role of a formonger named “Tree”, you have to save the island from the evil Florps. There are a number of ways to win, such as to
Story 8/10
Good Different choices brought more game time and fun
Good Very fun and clever dialogue make this game enjoyable
Bad The florps are not in the game (Only 1 or 2) until you get to the final parts of the map which was annoying because I wanted to see more
Graphics 7/10
Good The cartoon like graphics showed happiness and joy but it also knows how to make the enemies look evil and dark
Bad Most of the items are poorly drawn and don’t have any straight lines or symmetry. Sometimes I enjoy that simple drawing but I believe it could have been done better
Gameplay 8/10
Good The combat was at first very difficult and I had to spend a bit of time trying to hit the enemy without being hit. But after you master this, the combat is very enjoyable and has a good level of difficulty
Good The weapons and armour had a good variety and each item had different effects to help the player
Bad The quests were basic but many didn’t point me in the right direction and I had to spend quite a lot of time looking around for just one item
Bad The consumable items had a good variety but many of these items (such as poison) had no reason to be in my inventory and there was no quest I could find that wanted that item
NPCs 7/10
Good The enemies attacked mostly in close-up and they run towards you when you are close enough but some do attack with range and some enemies just run away. This made sure I didn’t have to repeat the combat over and over again so I had something different all the time
Good The friendly NPCs sold items, gave quests or just random chatter. Each NPC looked different so everyone in the game was different
Bad Some NPCs were hard to find for quests and it would have been useful if they all had names so then the quests were easier, although I do enjoy the difficulty.
Music/Sound 9/10
Good The music in the whole game was so fluid and I loved it completely
Good The sound effects of fighting and actions in the game were on average because some sound effects didn’t make sense to me but I did not mind it that much
Good The NPC sound effects were very good and each enemy sounded different so when I couldn’t see the enemy in caves, for example, I could hear the sound of them so I would know what enemy it is
Settings/Configuration 8/10
Good Setting the audio was very easy and there were many options
Good Setting the graphics was basic and many of the options are already set perfectly for me to play
Bad There was no difficulty setting so I couldn’t make it a harder/better experience for me
Final Rating

Five Nights at Freddy's is a clever concept with a unique theme, but whether it's a "horror" genre game is debatable.  A thriller maybe, but there is a distinct lack of gore or much sense of the macabre, and it has a distinct tongue-in-cheek quality to it.  Unfortunately, that tongue is haunted!  *WooooHooooo!!!!!*
You play a newly hired night watch person at the Chuck E. Cheese-esque establishment.  Your job is to man the cameras and make sure the animatronic characters, who roam around at night, do not make it into your control room.  You can pull up a laptop to view stationary cameras set in various rooms, operate door switches leading into the office, and operate lights outside the office.  You are limited in how much power you have to utilize all these electric devices, and thus it becomes clear what the game really is:  a resource management simulation in an apocalyptic world where there is no power grid.
There are some genuine jump-scares, initially.  The longer you play the less sensitized you become to it though, because there isn't enough variety in the "attacks" that happen.  There is some dread, or defeat, you feel when in the last hour or two you realize you do not have enough power left to make it to the morning.  Each night gets progressively more difficult to make it to the morning, because the animatronics become more active and you are forced to use more power.  I guess, ultimately, this has to do with your boss being a penny pinching miser (just look at your paycheck at the end of the game!).  There should be an expansion to this where you become part of a class action lawsuit with all the other Five Nighters to collect for withheld pay, physical pain, and emotional suffering.
As you become more proficient at the resource management they throw a twist at you in the form of "Foxy" - an animatronic character who can run and will sprint down a hall into the office.  You can close the door, if you're quick enough, but you still lose.  You lose because every time Foxy gets to the closed door he bangs on it - and when he does it depletes 6% of your precious power.  If he does this 3 times in one night - that's 18% of your power!  *screwed*
I give props for the originality of the game itself, but the execution leaves something to be desired.  Hitting ESC, for instance, doesn't pull up a menu screen or pause the game as it does in 99% of PC games.  Instead, it quits the game.  No problem, because the game saves what night you were on last.  Great!  What the game doesn't do is provide for more than one game file, so if you accidently click "New Game" instead of "Continue" it wipes your game file.  *son of meat packer!*
I like the concept, but I'm tired of being r@p3d by robotic automatons.

I found this game by complete happenstance. I've noticed for a few months that a few users spell out a word or phrase on their Steam profile using the images of the achievements unlockable in the game. I decided to humor the idea of seeing what kind of game this would be, and I've been left nothing short of amazed.
The concept is rather simple: Create lines between like shapes, and don't intersect others. It's a bit more complicated than that later on, but that's the jist of it. The lack of a soundtrack, only accompanied by chimes and soft sounds, is beautiful. The basic color scheme, and calm graphical design, create an immediately calming presense. The level design is something else. While some are incredibly easy, others will almost certainly impede your progress, but without leaving the bitter taste of a poor puzzle. I found that each harder puzzle was only one or two mouse clicks away from being correct, and completing such a puzzle leaves a pleasant aftertaste. Not to mention the seductive chime that plays after every completed level.
I haven't played terribly far into the game, but I've realized just how clever, how beautiful it really is. I tend to find solace in video games after a long day, and lately, my only interest has been to complete more puzzles here! This is a fantastic game, a great stress reliever, and for whatever reason is incredibly useful in spelling words on your Steam wall!

pros -
- all of the chapters that take place outside are visually stunning. the color scheme really works here
- puzzles are challenging enough, and platforming elements are surprisingly difficult
- excellent sound design. i don't know if it counts as sound design but i love how controller vibrations correspond to movement, too
- minimalist storytelling done....okay
- despite what others have said i think that the length is okay. not worth $9.99 maybe but still okay
- achievements add a little bit of replay value
cons -
- puzzles rely too much on timing and physics. this game doesn't handle like a true platformer so i would have liked for it to be more puzzle-focused. a lot of the time, you can know how to solve a puzzle but you still die 50 times because of timing. (i'm not talking about timing based mechanics either, like the gravity switcher. the momentum-based puzzles all sucked)
- the second half or 2/3s of the game is ugly and boring. although i understand why it happened in the narrative, i felt cheated that the first 8 or so chapters were so pretty and the bulk of the game is spent in a different setting. the story completely disappears for the majority of the game, and you're just solving puzzles in an ugly factory. ("ummm...it's because you're in limbo, sweetie :^)" no kidding but it's still lame and lazy as hell)
- speaking of the narrative, it's bad. it's executed okay enough, but it honestly feels like the most fake deep game i've ever played in my life. "wow, this game shakes me to my core. it's all in black and white and you're a kid and you die gruesome deaths" based on the minimalist storytelling it seems like the creators are proud of this atmosphere that they've created, but it's just...bad. "oh man there's a kid hanging from a noose!!! oh my god!!!! oh my god!!!" limbo doesn't say or do anything interesting in its story or atmosphere. this is one of the few games i've played that feels pretentious without having a line of dialogue

All right. Well. How do we tackle this one. After spending hours reading the positive and negative reviews of this game, the 100hrs I have of this game (and additional 40 hours not counted from the beta) I'm going to give it my best shot to objectively review this game.
Evolve is an incredible experience. To this day I have yet to play a game that has the sheer (totally did that on purpose) level of anticipation, adrenaline, and team building this title offers. Working together, each in seperate but all extremely important roles, you and your hunters are creating an arena for a fight. Sadly, the reviews stating "not enough content" or "repetitive" are just so completely false. Each game of "hunt", and please understand that my review will be only around this game mode, is a completely different experience. This has to do with the change in map, the change in creature spawns in that map, the slightly different path the monster took, if the monster decided to sneak or not, the character you're playing, the people you're playing with, the monster you're up against, and the character perk you chose, everything is exciting and new. That being said:
Do I think this game is for casual players? Yes and no. That truly depends on the opinion of the buyer. For me? No. I spent $60 on this game, and will continue to spend money on this game's content, to be in a competitive format building great teammwork. For others, publicly gaming with people they do not know from the internet is fine for them, and good for them. Personally, I enjoy the intricacies of a group of friends, who have a well-established field-captain calling the shots, and participating in strat discussions. This is the ideal of a team game to me. Oh wait, did I say team game? There's another part of this game that requires no teamwork at all and is essentially a new game altogether? Wait, what??
The monster play is its own entity. The player makes his/her own decisions on the spot, an adrenaline filled exciting experience. I have yet to play a game that has two completely different games in one. The monster experience is a brand new game altogether, with a completely different learning curve of its own. It requires no teamwork, no "playing with annoying pubs", you can play who you want to play like. In this, there are three different monsters (a 4th already announced) that allow you to play exactly how you'd like to. If this isn't just the best thing I've ever heard I don't know what is.
I will briefly state the DLC argument, although I think it's hardly worth my time. I don't think there's any debate that the general public is upset with how the game was setup for pre-release. The DLC was already being offered BEFORE the game was out. I get that. It's annoying, it seems like they just want to make money, I'm with you. But listen, if they're offering up a new monster and hunters as DLC? Oh boy does that change the gameplay more than any DLC i've ever heard before! Like I said earlier, there are two parts to this game (at the very least, both hunters and monsters each have many roles). So when the DLC comes out for a new monster and hunters, you have two sides to experience it on! It's a whole new game of hunting, an entirely new experience altogether.  Oh and are you seriously upset about skins? They're skins. You don't have to buy them. Get over yourselves.
I can't say it enough. I recommend you try this game with three other hunters who know something about this game. Watch an Evolve developer streamer, watch someone who is knowledgeable about the game. Or don't. That choice is entirely up to you. I'm telling you all this because I truly love this game. It's one of the best experiences I've had in multiplayer gaming, and I can't wait to see where this game takes me next.
Thanks for reading
-Jaryd

You've basically got everything you need, you could sleep/eat/pass time anyhow in your little cabin for next few weeks without needing to get out ( Normal difficulty ). Sometimes I feel like I'm the only one in the whole world ( even though I know devs probably wanted that feel ). Sometimes I find myself walking from point A to point B and I get bored pretty easly. Few times I've duct-taped W button so I could get there faster or sometimes I used to browse Facebook and listen to music while not paying any attention to game because it was too boring to watch character slowly walk 10 kilometers.
In the end, I still think this game is great, and I'm happy to recommend it to any gamer-survival expert out there. :)

They have stated that all the maps and real DLC will be released to everyone. Take a moment and consider the fact that modern videogame entertainment being what it is, this is actually a pretty damn good deal. Obsessing over the price isn't really doing anyone any good.
I hate expressing my opinions like this, but this game is worth every penny, but I would give it a few weeks to clear out the bugs that are still present in the game. So yeah, for now I'm giving it a 7.5/10

The game is so much fun. As a hunter, you need good teamwork to win. While it can be frustating when everyone is on a different page, when you're in a good group, seeing everyone work together is an extremely satisfying feeling. Conversely, the Monster requires no cooperation, but has a fairly high learning curve. When you play well, it is very fun to see the hunters go from angry hornets buzzing around you, to scared cockroaches skittering away from you. Overall the game is well balanced, although if you're playing against people who are good at their role, it will always be a struggle to win. Graphics are beautiful, the characters have funny backstory, and my experiece has been quite stable and bug free, outside of a few party matchmaking issues.
Variety is a little lacking (everything is basically monsters versus hunters) but there are different game modes/objectives and you can play offline with bots if you want to practice. The DLC is whatever; skins are overpriced, but that's pretty much always the case in my opinion, and future monster/hunter packs are expensive, but if you end up really loving the game, spending an extra 10-15 bucks isn't too bad. I've 100% completed this game so I not only feel entitled, but also morally obligated to shove my opinion down your throat. Deal with it.
Chroma Squad is a tactical RPG in the same vein as Nintendo's Fire Emblem series, but with a strange twist. Instead of being a knight or a dude with spikey hair and a giant sword, you play as a group of five stuntmen who act in a Power Rangers inspried show, complete with cheesy catchphrases and mech battles.
Chroma Squad's story is pretty simple. Your goal is to film each of the gangs' adventures for their TV show. Things seem fine at first, but the group begins to realize that their adventures may be more fact than fiction. I won't spoil any of the three endings, but they're all great.
Gameplay: As previosuly mentioned, this game runs in a similar way to the Fire Emblem series. For those who are uninitiated into weeb culture, Fire Emblem (and this game) do away with the idea that in turn-based battles your characters all stand in a line. Instead, you move them around a grid to get an advantage and perform special moves. One of this game's most important features is its' teamwork specials. By having a member of Chroma Squad perform the Teamwork move, other member can perform teamwork attack, Finishers, or Team Acrobatics which extend your sprint range. At the end of each episode, how well you did will be tallied into "Audience Points", which are then converted into your profit and fans. You'll also recieve materials which can be used to craft better weapons and armor for your squad.
Mecha Battles: These are, in my opinion, the most fun part of the game. At the end of most episodes from Season 2 and on, the boss you fight will grow to gigantic size! In order to combat this, your Squad gears up thier Mecha bot. Your bot and the enemy then take turns hitting eachother, defending, and performing specials. Each time you attack, your percent chance of hitting goes down by 10%, meaning you'll have to be careful to balance your attacks and defences. You can also use the materials you recieve or buy to upgrade parts of your mecha in order to increased attack, defence, hit chance, or give new specials.
Customization: There are a total of 5 rangers on your squad. The techie is best at dealing ranged damage. The Scout is the best at sneaking in, dealing damage, and getting out. The Assualt is good at hitting things really really hard. The Support is for healing your team, and the Lead is for keeping your team organized so they don't become too thinly spread. Within each ranger, there are 6 actors you can choose from who each gives their own extra stats. For instance, the lead in my first playthrough had the Asimobot actor, while my second playthrough used Mr. Beaver. Beyond that, you can also choose the nicknames of your rangers and what colors their suits are! :D
Pros:
1. Simple gameplay that's easy to pick up, but still has some depth for experienced players
2. The story is just interesting enough to keep you invested
3. Multiple endings adds a ton to the replay value
4. Four levels of difficuly most different types of players (Casual for those who want to see the story, up to Legendary for those who want a callenge)
5. It's so gosh darn charming! Each boss has their own personality and taglines, and it makes me feel so fuzzy inside. <3
Cons:
1. There are occasionaly a few visual glitches, but unless you're a real stickler, they shouldn't hinder your experience much.
2. The only real complaint I have is how short the story is. In total, one playthrough of the campaign takes about 15 hours. Again, this is brought up to about 45 hours between 3 different endings, but the 2nd and 3rd playthrough are mostly filler until the last season.
If you don't play this game, you're doing a disservice to yourself. This game is filled with so much charm with it's characters, palette, and story, you'll find it hard to stop playing. Prop all of that up with awesome gameplay, and you've got yourself an awesome way to spend 40+ hours.
9.5/10, HIghly recommended.

When somebody sees this game, they might think it's just another early access zombie survival game, most of which being awful. However, this game is not another game where you play as "the Rambo of the apocalypse," shooting every zombie in sight, crafting better and better weapons. Instead, you play as the average Joe, who somehow managed to not become one of the hundereds of zombies occupying Knox County. Instead of having some crafting table where you can build a castle right off the bat, you need to find everything needed to build the walls just to protect your garden. The loot system works pretty well, you find stuff where you would normally find it. Houses have average loot, including food, bats, golf clubs, and the occasional gun or case of bullets. Warehouses will generally have crafting supplies, police stations will have guns and ammo, and so on. You will find the occasional out-of-place item, like a gun or bullets in the elementary school. You need to debate doing anything in the game, since one slip-up could spell certain death. There have been way too many times where I decide to go loot a building by the highway and am ingulfed in zombies. The dev team, The Indie Stone have done a superb job at creating this game, and every update makes the game much more fun, realistic, and, of course, difficult. You will not find a better zombie survival game out there, and I more than reccomend it.

When it comes down to it, If this game was delivered in the exact state that it was and there was no buzz about DLC, I don't think there would be any complaints.
This is a full game for $60.  There are 12 hunters and 3 monsters.  That's plenty; the developers don't owe us more.  We don't have any rights to a ton of characters or limitless content.  They like money, though, and I can't blame them for wanting to ask for compensation for their extra efforts.
I don't want to make assumptions, but I feel as if many people are complaining without knowing how much work goes in to what the developers have made and how much work is going in to the DLC they are going to deliver.  I'm ignorant, too, I'll admit; for all I know, it takes one guy a single hour to make a character, but chances are likely that it takes a lot more work and man hours.
Bottom line, it's a solid, full game.  If there were no mention of DLC, the complaints would be less verbose.

I've wanted this game since 2011, I saw Dopefish play it and I thought it was real fun, I tried buying it but it was not on Steam or any other trusted platform. The've come a long way from 2011, the game looks MUCH better and polished, and it's not even done.
* You can pretty much turn the game to whatever you like, if you like classic dumb zombies you can do that, or superhuman fast zombies.
* Don't let the looks fool you, you can farm and build in this game. Medical attention is very fun since it's not just "drink soda or eat something to restore hp", It actually focuses on the parts of the body that are damaged and require tools to attend to your wounds.
*Skills are good, but I feel like it's kinda tedious how the XP system works at the moment (just an opinion).
*The map is HUGE. and there's custom maps. I'm really excited for vehicles cause It's pretty tedious to just run whenever you want to go, and you have to travel several days to other spots of the map.
*The map actually degrades overtime. Trash accumulates, windows break, walls crack, vines grow over walls and windows, grass starts to grow around the concrete, it's very nice.
*Multiplayer is fun but it's better to play with friends if you don't play on a daily basis.
*NPCs were removed but they are working on them again, so you won't be alone when surviving.
Overall it's a pretty fun game so far, a couple little bugs and a couple things I'd love they implemented but it's still under development. Devs are cool, they give you every monday a blog post about what are they working on and the news about the next build. It's very much worth the 15 dollars.

I heard about the DLC fiasco surrounding this game before I had actually tried it out. I pre-ordered the game for myself and 3 friends because I saw that it was a co-operative game that we could play together similar to the L4D games. I was just excited for another game with high replayability with friends. I was slightly skeptical going into it from all of the things I heard surrounding the DLC, but I have to stand up for this game and say don't let that affect your decision to buy it. If you disagree with the business practice that much to not buy the game, fine. However, I think it is highly unfair that the game is receiving poor reviews based on its business model and not the gameplay.
The game is extremely fun. I had no issues connecting to servers with a friend and the games lasted anywhere from 10 to 30 minutes on the longer end. Evolve in NO WAY pressures you do buy DLC. There aren't notifications on the main menu like with Call of Duty. Honestly, I forgot that so much DLC was out there while playing. I did not feel like I was lacking any content and there was plenty for me to look forward to as a player. Seriously, there are a number of games already out there that remind you of its DLC for sale more than this game does. The variety in classes is enough to inspire me to try all of them. Plus, the characters within classes have builds that vary depending on the team strategy you want to do. I like that you get experience points as a player and then for character mastery separately. I feel like the content is very deep in terms of what there is to learn about the monster, hunters, and the wildlife. I would definitely recommend this game to any friends looking for a fresh new co op game to dive into that will be worth their while for a long time.

I picked up evolve because the urge was just too great. I read the steam reviews and saw everyone 'Not Recommending' it and I was on the fence because of this for a long while. I read these reviews and it was all "Amazing game content"..."so much fun"..."really unique"... "BUT £$?!??!?!?! Way too expensive and DLCs announced already?! NO NO NO don't get it."
I counter this money issue short term with the argument that for £35 you get all the playable content in the game currently. That is 12 hunters and 3 monsters. There is no advantage to anyone who has paid extra so far. The only things in the in-game store are vanity skins for hunters weapons, no skin (as far as I know) change the actual model of any character. This is great, it means you change what you (as the player) see on your character but don't force it onto other people like many skins do it other games.

I bought Disgaea 5 on the Nintendo Switch and it was my first experience with a tactics/strategy RPG. I sold it after about an hour of forced gameplay due to the price I'd paid.
This is now my second experience with a game like that... and I think this game is downright fun, and amazing. The 2 games are not identical by any means, but for those new to a strategy RPG, Chroma Squad is an excellent place to start whereas something like Disgaea dropped you in with no guidance at all.
It is most definitely influenced by the likes of Power Rangers and other hits from this genre. The gameplay is so much fun and it's made incredibly easy by design. I love the challenge that this game has but it also is very understanding for those who have trouble learning the tactics of a game like this.
I know that there are plenty of games similar to this and many have their favorites. When I saw the first level of this was strategy play, I immediately thought "here we go again with another crap game I got in a bundle" but then I beat the first level. And another... and another.
And I kept playing and I haven't stopped. Something about being able to make your own team of fighters is so much fun. You have a lot of options to make the Chroma Squad feel like your own. The bosses are really funny and play into the mechanics well. It banks hard on nostalgia does it perfectly.
The story is not amazing but it's definitely cheesy and hits all of the right notes for the game. I skip the scenes every once in awhile because I'm just ready to play more of the game. This is a lot of fun for the right price, or if you're looking for this type of game I'd recommend it.

- The class system. I honestly wish other games would implement something similar, where from the three main classes you can branch off into 100's of different paths. Of course, I would appreciate more variation (more starting classes?) but this is pretty unique to Luna Online; you're free to learn whatever skills you want to learn, and build your character the way you'd like.
- The gameplay is bland (when you actually do play and not just leave the bot to do everything for you) wherein you click a target, hit a few keys to cast skills, and that's the end of it. Rinse and repeat. Story isn't at all immersive either, but I guess that's something you'd expect out of an MMO nowadays.
- The graphics are VERY outdated. You'd think that calling something "Reborn" means that there have been improvements but honestly there are none.
- Poor character customization. But really, what can you expect from a revived, nearly 10 year old game?
- There is an in-game bot. To be honest, its a double-edged sword. It's helpful for some but ultimately it just ruins the experience. This is basically an idle game where you do minimal work, leave it running for a bit (it hunts monsters for you), then restart the process.
- Uncontrolled PvP. There are three channels for each map, but essentially there are only really two as in the higher level maps, one of them allows PK. It wouldn't be bad if the channel was level restricted, but as the game stands, there is literally nothing stopping someone that is 20 or so levels ahead of you from going to that server and one-shotting you. Worst part is, you lose 1% of EXP to revive and they gain and lose nothing from doing it. 1% doesn't seem like much, but when you have to kill 100 or so things to achieve it (mobs give approximately 0.01% of EXP) it's an enormous waste of time.
- The community is actually pretty toxic. As I've mentioned earlier, there's really no benefit to PKing and there's nothing really stopping someone from doing it (no consequence, which there really should be, at least one for killing someone 5 levels under you). Literally high level players waltz into low level map's PK servers just to screw people over.
- The game has no depth. The story is null, the translations are bad (this was made by Korean developers and translated by English publishers), and the quest instructions are misleading (they don't even tell you where the 50 things you need to kill are).
- The camp system. During character creation, you are forced to choose a camp with absolutely no inclination as to the significance of doing so. You soon realize that the dominating camp provides benefits to players in the same camp, such as increased EXP and drop rate. Doesn't seem bad, but it makes the entire thing pretty useless as once you realize this, you can just make another character and change camps. Essentially, everyone is in one camp and the other camp is just there. This system is pointless.
- The EXP. The reason why the bot NEEDS to exists. It'll probably take someone CENTURIES to hit max level with the EXP that mobs give, in comparison to how much EXP one needs to level up (it grows exponentially while the amount you receive does not). But I guess it makes sense because:
- There is nothing to do at end-game. Literally nothing. All that hard work (not really) for nothing. It's not even a little bit rewarding. Once you hit that ceiling, it's over for you. There's nothing to do, no end-game content. Endless grinding for naught.
- Poor instructions on what to do in the game. You're basically left to figure things out on your own.
- The game crashes a LOT. Due to memory leak? I have 16gbs of memory. I don't even understand how this is happening. Supposedly some files are missing also, but Suba Games can't do anything about that because they've stated themselves: "We are not the developers of this game. We cannot fix bugs." Absolutely ridiculous excuse, as the actual developers of this game gave up on it AGES ago. So who's going to fix it? Absolutely nobody.
- Pretty much everything else. The feel is not even similar to the old Luna (which I have played), it's just a game with the same name.
This game had a lot of potential to be as good as it was before. But it seems like the recent publishers don't really care much about it. Didn't bother fixing bugs before releasing, didn't bother adding new and exciting content, didn't bother fixing the text, the UI, graphics, etc. It seems like Suba Games hasn't even PLAYED their own game, seeing as this game needs a LOT of work.

I hesitated a lot before buying this game. Being not much of a crafter guy I had misgivings. Furthermore, being in early access and all, I had some bad experiences before. Last, I feared that it would not be that much interesting or challenging. No real ennemies and all that. Boy, I was WRONG!
I thought I knew about survival, I thought those zombie games had prepared me. Not in the least, they hadn't.
First try, I found a gun, went all rambo after I missed a wolf and decided to track it down. I got lost, got surrounded by wolves and got killed. Ok I learnt to respect them. There were some ennemies after all. New game, I thought I knew what to expect but no, I still hadn't met the most fearsome foe of all: the cold.
After I found a very comfy cabine beside a frozen lake I decided to go to one of the small fishing huts. It was 500 meters away, tops. So I decided to dump most of the clutter in my backpack (you know, silly useless things such as spare clothes,wood, soda cans, food in general). So here I go in the bright morning to do some fishing. I did fish, but when I looked up from my fishing hole an end of the world blizzard was bellowing outside. Complete whiteout, I started to get very cold. So I looked through my pack, found some wood and (I was lucky there was a heating apparatus in that hut) started warming up while cooking the fish. Two hours later, visibility still a big fat zero.
So started the most adrenaline filled, terrifying moment I've had with a video game in a long time. I decided to hoof it back to the cabine through the wind and the snow.
Five meters toward the shore. Ten. Can't see the hut behind me, cant see the shore either, I'm hoping I'm not getting lost. At last I see some trunks. I take a right to get back to the cabine. I"m getting colder, I start shaking then growing numb. Rocks, trees, snow, still no cabine.
AT LAST over there I think I can see the roof... No. Just another boulder. At that point I was completely exhausted, badly dehydrated and almost frozen to death. It felt like I'd been going for hours. I kept telling myself "nah, its just 500 meters, that's not much, you must be real close!". And when I could barely walk anymore, my bag seemingly weighting a ton, then I saw it. THE CABINE only 10 PACES AHEAD! I made it. It was really useful to try and memorize how I could use the  shore as a rail to go back but still... I was shaking with relief as my character collapsed in a bed to get ten hours of shuteye.
Last thing, I thought I'd never say that but it's the first game to make me go "OMG YES, A FROZEN HALF ROTTEN DEAR! T'IS MY LUCKY DAY!". For a game in early access it has a great feel to it. It already beats a lot of AAA titles, the replayability looks great from where I stand. Buy without hesitation, support the devs!

Game has somekind of immersion which pulls you in it's world. Gameplay elements are fantastic. You can struggle to survive or play peacefully, however you wish. Even though I'd rather have realistic, detailed graphics, "drawn" graphics aren't that bad. On the other hand, game lacks fun after few months of surviving. You've basically got everything you need, you could sleep/eat/pass time anyhow in your little cabin for next few weeks without needing to get out ( Normal difficulty ). Sometimes I feel like I'm the only one in the whole world ( even though I know devs probably wanted that feel ). Sometimes I find myself walking from point A to point B and I get bored pretty easly. Few times I've duct-taped W button so I could get there faster or sometimes I used to browse Facebook and listen to music while not paying any attention to game because it was too boring to watch character slowly walk 10 kilometers.
In the end, I still think this game is great, and I'm happy to recommend it to any gamer-survival expert out there. :)

Absolutely wonderful puzzle game from the beginning till the very end.
Quell Reflect is a logical game with very simple rules yet various and challenging levels. The aim of the game is to get all small orbs while guiding big bubbles with as few moves as possible. Those big spheres can go only in four basic directions, but once they move they stop only on obstacles. Except ordinary walls, there are also deadly traps which pop our bubbles.
There is no rush while playing, there is not a ticking clock. The quick precise movement is not required neither. What is really needed is a good thinking.
Even though some levels are difficult, the player has always a chance to buy a solution with coins that they receive for solving levels. Solving only the easiest puzzles should give enough coins to smoothly go through the harder ones.
The game is created in bright pastel colours, which along a calm beautiful soundtrack compose an unique atmosphere. 84 levels are shared into groups of 4 and every group has a different nice background picture. All those things brings tranquility and some kind of meditation.
In my opinion, Quell Reflect is a game for everyone. It is like taking a break from a daily rush.

"Quell Reflect" is very similar to it's predecessor, "Quell."  The developer added two new play mechanics:  movable pins and gold pearl/block pairs.  Unfortunately, they also seemed to have made many more of the puzzles hard.  It took me 9.6 hours to complete the game with 100% Achievements.  BUT, I had to use a LOT of walkthroughs.  Very frustrating.  I'd have preferred easier puzzles, so I'm right on the border with the game.  If you liked "Quell," and don't mind tough puzzles, then I have no problem recommending the game to you.  If you don't care about Achievements (so finding that hidden gem and getting the puzzles done in the minimum number of moves doesn't matter to you), I again recommend the game whole-heartedly.  But, if you're a perfectionist, a completionist, and get frustrated with tough puzzles, you might think twice about "Quell Reflect."  Still, two out of those three groups should be happy with the game, so I'm sticking with my Recommended rating even though I wasn't overjoyed with the game.
Thanks for the refund, Valve.

The second instalment of the enchanting Quell series, offering up another neat collection of 80+ levels. It retains the wonderfully familiar mechanics, style and gorgeous soundtrack from before, but augments them with some fun new elements. Some levels now involve multiple rain drops, and others have gold blocks which can only be removed if you find a golden pearl first. They blend seamlessly into the existing game, enriching an already serene puzzler.
The difficulty has scaled nicely, creating a very natural progression from the first title - ultimately making it hard not to love if you enjoyed the first one.

My overall rating for this game is going to be a 9.5/10. Thats to say for its current state. The Forest is progressing in the right direction with updates coming out ever 2-3 weeks. It sounds like a long time but each update is beneficial to the game. Whether it'd be patches or additions to the game. Most of the time its both. I have over 100 hours put in to The Forest and love every minute of it. I always find myself coming back to play it all the time. I've bought The Forest 2 years ago I think. Back during the 0.16 or 0.17 update.
The campaign sets the scene as a famous actor (you) and his child take a vaction. As they travel to their destination by plane, they come across an island that holds various mysteries to it. As one of the only survivors of the plane crash you must find the location of your son who was taken by a man. Jumping from cave to cave, location to location, you search for anything that can help you in your search for your son. Pictures, colors, and names all help to point you in the direction of your son. Amongst the campaign portion of the game, you have the Survival Aspect
Hunting, building, protecting, and securing yourself a steady location to rest your head is a big part of the game. Setting traps for small creatures such as lizards and rabbits help you to survive the day. Placing defensive walls around a location is a must-do part of the game. Place small planters to grow aloe, berries, and other plants help you to survive in your mission to find your son. Survival is what this game is about, but you must build yourself structures and traps to survive.
The building in this game is great. Everything you build is beneficial in your survival. Building small food planters, water collectors, meat drying racks, all of this is beneficial. Along with prebuilt structures such as a log cabin or a small hunting shelter, their is custom building that allows you to build structures to your liking. Custom houses, walls, towers, tree houses, and even a zipline. Along with custom building you have traps. Traps come in 2 different categories. 1 for the small creatures such as rabbits and lizards, their are also larger traps for the more, dangerous, creatures of The Forest. The island is home for many mysteries, including the origin of the island's Cannibals.
The Cannibals come in different shapes and sizes. I mean that literally. Some are more human like, while others are just more, alien like. Some are faster and weaker than others, while others are slower but stronger. The longer you survive the more of them you will come across along with the more dangerous they are. They will also come in larger groups. Using the traps you've made help to your advantage to take out the Cannibals. After killing some you can turn their body and limbs into effigies. Effigies help to ward off other Cannibals. But don't rely of these effigies, the Cannibals only get stronger.
Multiplayers is well made. Bringing in one of your friends to survive along with your is always fun. Especially if you bring your whole squad with you. Utilizing tactics to fight off groups of Cannibals is always a blast. You must use a walkie-talkie to communicate over long distances which is always fun to use instead of having to use a skype/discord/teamspeak chat to communicate you can use the walkie-talkie. Although with connection issues to the steam server a skype/discord/teamspeak chat might work better.
This game is great in every way, I would like to see some kind of leadership over the Cannibals. Maybe capturing and taming (sort of speak) them to utilize them to your advantage. Maybe as some kind of weapon. If you give them what they want, something like food, they are calmer towards you and become neutral for awhile and may carry out an action you tell them. Nothing like chopping down a tree or scavaging for materials/food but to give you the location of the nearest cave entrance or other Cannibals perhaps. Maybe more prebuilt houes. More planters that you can create. If not a planter then even being able to farm straight out of the ground after you condition it.
The game file size is small. Something like 3 or 4GB

The Beginner's Guide commits the cardinal sin of a follow-up work: it makes you retroactively question whether the first was actually any good. I remember The Stanley Parable as being really enjoyable, but based on how incredibly pretentious and boring Wreden's subsequent game is, maybe I'm misremembering.
The Beginner's Guide's framing device is that a fictionalized version of Wreden is walking you through his former friend's game design history. You travel through various simplitic vignettes while Wreden discusses his history with the designer, "Coda." What seems like like it could be an interesting concept for a game ends up essentially being a commentary to a pretentious indie movie accompanied by some grapics and design that would have been underwhelming a decade ago. The Beginner's Guide acts like it's making some profound statement about the nature of game design by forgoing standard game elements like actual interactiveness, but merely results in an excruciating experience of extremely slow-walking down virtually identical hallways.
Even ignoring the game's many significant flaws, it's not worth the $10 price due to it's extremely short length. I finished it in under an hour and a half. Given how limited the actual gameplay is, I'd suggest just watching a walkthrough on Youtube if you're interested, but I'd recommend just skipping it.

I'd actually never heard of this game until quite recently when a friend showed it to me, so I gave it a try and... wow. This is easily one of the best multiplayer FPS experiences I've ever had. It's so unique to all the more arcady WW2 games I'm accustomed to that it just feels like a whole different animal.
This game is shockingly brutal and gory, which works well with the realistic historical setting. The focus on realism makes it incredibly easy to die in this game, which can be frustrating but very rewarding at the same time. So for the new players: prepare to die,
. The game blends brutality with realism and low health so well that teamwork and communication feels instictive in order to stay alive, which almost
happens in less realistic shooters like Battlefield or Call of duty. The teams along with their weapons and equipment all feel very balanced. Both Axis and Allies are very fun to play as. Rising Storm, the pacific variant of Red Orchestra 2, does an especially good job of making the two armies balanced but drastically similar at the same time. Japan has knee mortars, grenade traps and the ability to banzai charge, while the Americans have the engineer and flamethrower classes.
Over all, this game is a hardcore, but exciting WW2 FPS shooter that can appeal to many demographics of FPS fans. If you're sick of of overdone sci-fi shooters, and arcady war games, this is definitely for you. I give this game a 9/10.
Note: I highly recommend downloading the Heroes of the West mod on steam alongside this game. It is basically just Red Orchestra, but on the western front with new maps, weapons and a new team(the British). It is incredibly detailed for a community-made mod (the Brits even have their own custom voice lines!), so I recommend you check it out.

All right. Well. How do we tackle this one. After spending hours reading the positive and negative reviews of this game, the 100hrs I have of this game (and additional 40 hours not counted from the beta) I'm going to give it my best shot to objectively review this game.
Evolve is an incredible experience. To this day I have yet to play a game that has the sheer (totally did that on purpose) level of anticipation, adrenaline, and team building this title offers. Working together, each in seperate but all extremely important roles, you and your hunters are creating an arena for a fight. Sadly, the reviews stating "not enough content" or "repetitive" are just so completely false. Each game of "hunt", and please understand that my review will be only around this game mode, is a completely different experience. This has to do with the change in map, the change in creature spawns in that map, the slightly different path the monster took, if the monster decided to sneak or not, the character you're playing, the people you're playing with, the monster you're up against, and the character perk you chose, everything is exciting and new. That being said:
Do I think this game is for casual players? Yes and no. That truly depends on the opinion of the buyer. For me? No. I spent $60 on this game, and will continue to spend money on this game's content, to be in a competitive format building great teammwork. For others, publicly gaming with people they do not know from the internet is fine for them, and good for them. Personally, I enjoy the intricacies of a group of friends, who have a well-established field-captain calling the shots, and participating in strat discussions. This is the ideal of a team game to me. Oh wait, did I say team game? There's another part of this game that requires no teamwork at all and is essentially a new game altogether? Wait, what??
The monster play is its own entity. The player makes his/her own decisions on the spot, an adrenaline filled exciting experience. I have yet to play a game that has two completely different games in one. The monster experience is a brand new game altogether, with a completely different learning curve of its own. It requires no teamwork, no "playing with annoying pubs", you can play who you want to play like. In this, there are three different monsters (a 4th already announced) that allow you to play exactly how you'd like to. If this isn't just the best thing I've ever heard I don't know what is.
I will briefly state the DLC argument, although I think it's hardly worth my time. I don't think there's any debate that the general public is upset with how the game was setup for pre-release. The DLC was already being offered BEFORE the game was out. I get that. It's annoying, it seems like they just want to make money, I'm with you. But listen, if they're offering up a new monster and hunters as DLC? Oh boy does that change the gameplay more than any DLC i've ever heard before! Like I said earlier, there are two parts to this game (at the very least, both hunters and monsters each have many roles). So when the DLC comes out for a new monster and hunters, you have two sides to experience it on! It's a whole new game of hunting, an entirely new experience altogether.  Oh and are you seriously upset about skins? They're skins. You don't have to buy them. Get over yourselves.
I can't say it enough. I recommend you try this game with three other hunters who know something about this game. Watch an Evolve developer streamer, watch someone who is knowledgeable about the game. Or don't. That choice is entirely up to you. I'm telling you all this because I truly love this game. It's one of the best experiences I've had in multiplayer gaming, and I can't wait to see where this game takes me next.
Thanks for reading
-Jaryd

One of the keys to a good puzzle game is creating something that feels new, but also has an air of familiarity. It is a feat rooted in simple and intuitive design, a form which conjures the thought that, surely, someone must have had the idea already.
Thomas Bowker's LYNE does exactly this. And, no matter how hard we wrack our brains, we can't think of another game that does what it does. Or, at least, none that do it as well.
As the name suggests, the simple goal of LYNE is to draw a continuous line that links shapes of the same type together.
The basic grid pattern upon which the puzzles play of allow for movement along the eight ordinal directions. To complete each stage, you simply trace the desired line between each point. The only initial complication is that you can't visit the same shape twice, or allow lines to overlap.
The game's minimalist visual design, and panpipe soundtrack, provide a meditative feel to these early puzzles. But it doesn't take long for LYNE to completely destroy this illusion of calm

LYNE is a fun and addictive puzzle game. It doesn't try and dress itself up in a story, like some other puzzle games i've seen, which is definitely a plus. You just start it up and play.
The basic premise is to fill the "board", drawing lines between nodes and switches, except you can't cross the lines. It's kind of like sewing buttons, but on a digital canvas. Complete a set of 25 to earn points. It is fairly simple to play, but as levels increase the solutions become much more complex, and like most puzzles, take breaks. Otherwise things can get very frustrating.
This game is mouse controlled, but I've found streaming it to a mobile device to be quite a fun experience as well.
The graphics in this game are very minimal and simplistic, and you can unlock new backgrounds as you earn points. This is good, as it helps set the focus on the puzzle. Similarly, the sound design in this game is very simplistic, but well done.
There is pretty much no limit to this game (at least none that I have found). There are new "daily puzzles" that are generated, well, daily to keep you playing as well as a mysterious "???" puzzle that you can start to decode after you earn enough points.
This is a very good game if you like puzzles, just be sure to pace yourself.

Hmmm. I'm on the fence with this game. I'm going to give an honest review with no spoilers (Even though this game has been out for a while) and hopefully people find this useful.
The positives In my opinion is the realistic and mechanics of the game. Meaning that you definitely feel human-like seeing as in some games you run about rampant like you're some god. This game really limits you in terms of capabilities, hiding spots and resources. In addition to that, the immersion with your surroundings and the visual aspect itself is fantastic with low requirements to run (So you could probably run this on a potato :P). The game's lighting, sounds and soundtrack were all well thought out and you can tell a lot went into this game.
Now for the negatives... In the positives it really seemed like I love the game, but i only love the game for it's technical side. However when it comes with story and interraction with foes really let me down. The game "borrowed" the mechanics from Amnesia - the dark descent and/or the Penumbra series in terms of defense. You have to run and hide in order to survive and yes it can be very thrilling, it can also be very, very repetitive. In addition to that, the game has cheap jumpscares. Only a beginner to horror/scary games wouldn't last in this game but i found myself getting more frustrated than scared because of the predictableness of the game. You complete an objective, someone scary tries killing you, you run and hide and run some more, then you've made progress - woohoo. But seriously, it got very boring. Alongside the repetition, i thought the game was VERY limited in terms of exploration. Yes you get documents for exploring and what not - maybe a few batteries. But if i want to immerse myself into this vast world of Outlast, at least have more corridors, rooms and areas where i can simply go and explore. Because i feel like the game puts you on a very basic/linear route where you can even stray from temporarily because all the doors are locked.
Don't get me wrong, this game is good. Just not for me. So I'll definitely give it a thumbs up because it's worth a shot. (Yes i have completed the game)

Copy of my review for Quell, as it applies to this one:
- The levels are well designed with a difficulty going from easy to hard (but not too hard) levels
- No timer at all
- You can play as as little as you want and continue where you left off or go back to previous levels to complete unfinished objectives

- Finding and getting the jewel in every level gives you a different objective
- Not a huge number of puzzles but more than adequate for the price
It's very well done too:
- Graphics, music and sound are nice and polished
- Graphic options work as the should (several fixed resolutions, full screen, windowed mode)
- Music and sounds can be muted separately
- Movement can be controlled with keyboard
- Resetting a level or going to the next one can also be done with keyboard
