I understand that there are layers to what this game is attempting to do. The game uses a number of tricks and mechanics that deliver a powerful emotional message, but I can't fogive it because of one thing (SPOILERS, but you should still read):
---
---
---
We don't know whether the game is fiction or not. The creater refuses to comment on whether it is or isn't. I imagine that he thinks it will have a more powerful emotional impact this way. He's right, but that's not fair or ethical when this game is so immoral if it's non-ficiton.
The game is almost certianly fiction, I can't believe that someone would spend all of these hours creating it without realizing that what they were doing was wrong. If the game is ficiton, and the creator made it clear that it was fiction, than would be fine. It's fine if the game is ficiton. It's even fine that we were decieved for the entire game into thinking it was non-ficiton. That's all fine.
But it's not fine for the creator to be vague about it, and let there continue to be doubt about whether or not it's fiction. If it's fiction, then just tell us at the end or in interviews or something. Continuing to let us doubt things is just a tactic to increase speculation about the game and make the experience more powerful. But it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. EVEN IF this game's actual message is to make us feel angry at the game for these reasons, it's dumb. We don't know for sure if the game involved something potentially highly immoral, so we shouldn't have anything to do with it. Letting there be doubt about potentially immoral acts involved in creating this game is immoral in itself.
I don't see myself ever buying another game from this creator unless he sincerely apologizes and clears things up.

DLC conundrum aside, this is a great game for people that like teamwork oriented games, or lone wolf type of playstyle. The asymmetrical gameplay allows for two very distinct playstyles.
I'm just going to briefly explain the main game type: Hunt.
As the monster, it requires cunning, wit, quick reaction time, and punishes you badly for poor decisions. The monster must kill wildlife and eat to evolve and become more powerful. Eating also provides armor that takes all damage until depleted. Health does not typically regenerate, so eating is a must for the monster. It is very important that whoever plays the monster knows when to feast and when to flee. If you get caught with your pants down, it's likely going to get you killed or severely cripple you for that game. One way to remain undetected is to "sneak". This costs the monster some mobility, but does not leave tracks for hunters to follow. The ultimate goal of the monster is to kill all the hunters and have them dead at the same time (I will explain that a little more later) or to get to the peak form (level 3) and take out a generator.
It's the job of the hunters to track, trap, and kill the monster. Typically, it is desirable to find the monster early on in their first form. The Assault does the most damage and has is the toughest to kill. The Trapper has an array of tools to keep the monster in a given place. The Support can shield provide a variety of buffs to the team, while also having a few gadgets to deal some damage. The Medic is a sniper who has the ability to heal, or extra revival capabilities that other characters do not have. If a hunter gets knocked out (loses all health), they can be revived by a teammate twice on the battlefield. Each knock out causes their max health to drop. If they aren't not revived in time and bleed out, they die and must be air dropped back into battle. If any hunter dies, it starts a 2:00 minute countdown for them, and any other hunter who dies before the time is up to be dropped back in simultaneously. If all hunters die before the 2:00 countdown for the air drop, then the monster wins.
I didn't want to get too into it, but just let anyone know that is considering buying this game that, aside from 2k trying to nickel and dime their consumers, this is genuinely a fun game that creates a lot of unique and memorable scenarios. It's not a perfect game, but it's the best multiplayer game I've played for some time.

Let's Play: REIGNS
Reigns is a great little game that really captures that classic choose your own adventure feel. You play as a young king who assumes the throne after the previous king died. Each turn is 1 year and each year you are presented with a request, problem, or event which requires you to decide between two options. The result of your choice will effect one or more of your kingdoms 4 groups, the church, the people, the military, and the treasury. Your object is to rule as long as possible, keeping all 4 groups happy, while completing objectives. You do this until you inevitably die to the plauge, the angry mob, the religious zealots, your dinner, or any other number of things that can kill you in this game. You then assume the role of the next young king and do it again.
-PROS:
- Great content for the price
- Decent replayability
- Easy to pickup and learn
- Enjoyable and funny gameplay
- Steam Achievements
-CONS:
- Events tend to repeat, could use more events
- At certain points there is no way to keep your king alive
TLDR: Great game to just sit down and play. For the price, absolutely recommend!!!

I was running across a frozen lake having just stocked up a few various shelters in the area with supplies. I had made it eleven days at this point. Food was plentiful, supplies were more than I could carry and I had a nice rifle and half a dozen rounds to go along with it.
It was four hours from sundown. I was just a stones throw away from the base of the hill where my main shelter was. It was a glorious two story, wood panel cabin with a bed with my name on it. I could see it at this point from where I stood on the lake. But between myself and my gloriously warm bed, right at the base of the hill, crept a bear. It was a big, overbearing giant. It was easily three, even four times my size. But it was also a source of majestic food. Food, pelts and guts for curing.
I lowered myself into a crouch and slowly approached it. Rifle drawn, crosshair as best I could place it with my shaky hands, I got within twenty meters of the beast. I slowed my breathing as best I could, placed the crosshair center mass and pulled the trigger. The crack echoed in the eerie cold silence, ripping the air apart as it reverberated. There was nothing at first. No movement, no accompanying growls or grunts, just nothing. I stood up, chambered another round and took aim once again. I approached the lifeless corpse hesitantly, still aware of the potential danger if it weren't to be fatally wounded. I got within an inspecting distance and peered at it. Still no movement. It was truly dead. I...this cold, hungry and very frightened woman shot this great beast with one measly round and killed it?
HA! TAKE THAT NATURE! I WILL PREVAIL!
With just over three hours of sunshine left I dug straight into the corpse, carving hide from flesh and tearing flesh from bone. There was so much it was just incredible, I mean the food alone could easily last another fortnight! I'll harvest as much as I can so the wolves don't take it. After all, the cabin is just up that small hill there. Hours ticked past and all the hacking and cutting was slowly tiring me while the sun slowly dipped further past the horizon.
I wasn't even halfway through it all when I realised the sun had completely dropped from the sky and the chills of night had crept upon me. Its icy fingers had slid its way into my clothing and all down my extremities. My vision was numbing and my pack was too heavy to run with. I started the short climb towards the cabin with my lantern in front of me, my vision starting to fade. Suddenly, the snap of a twig, the howl of a wolf. He's just meters away. I drop my lantern and pull out my rifle. BANG! The bullet whizzes past the wolf's head and he squeals, turning heel and running the other way. Phew. I won't be that lucky again. I continue the short walk to my cabin. It's just up there. I can see it right ahead now. I can just about touch the doorknob, smell the fireplace. Then a loud growl and a sudden impact and another wolf is upon me. With my very last bit of energy I put my arm in front of myself and watch as the wolf rips into my throat and severs my jugular and sends me fading off into The Long Dark.

Never meet your heroes and never replay your favorite games... Unless they are Bioshock. I was hesitant to return to Rapture after 9 years. As amazing as the first trip was, 9 years is a long time in video game years. The thought of tarnishing my memory of what very well may be my favorite game of all time was horrifying. Nonetheless, I couldn't resist the temptation of revisiting such a masterpiece on a modern PC and on high settings. I plugged my nose and dove right back into the choppy waves of the Atlantic. Man, I'm glad I did.
While it does lag behind modern games graphically, the PC version look considerably better than I remember the 360 version looking. Gameplay still shines as one if it's bright points as well, but none of these are the true heart of Bioshock.
While I could appreciate the tone and mood of Bioshock in my early 20's, many of it's themes were lost on me. Now, in my 30's, aspects of the story that I never really understood really resonate with me. Balancing the frustration of the government's heavy-handed role in our lives with the potential chaos of a world without any checks and balances is conundrum only life experience can help one understand. I also feel the game does a great job of building a story around this theme without blatantly picking sides; an important but often fumbled task for mainstream arts and media.
If you have fond memories of Bioshock but are not sold on a return trip to Rapture, I recommend giving it another shot. This oldie has officially become a classic.

Overall, I think Chroma Squad really has a lot of great ideas going for it. I'm not a power rangers/sentai fan, but I do like srpgs and I was pleasantly surprised by a lot of things in this game:
+ The gameplay is simplistic but satisfying. Where you can sometimes have maps that last for ~30 minutes in a game like X-com or FF Tactics, it's not uncommon to find yourself done with a Chroma Squad map in about 15 minutes. This is great if you have that strategy itch but you don't want to commit a lot of time.
+ The teamwork abilities are a very nice inclusion that offer some depth. There is a nice sense of risk/reward in choosing how you control your team - for example, do you throw a ranger across the field to take out an enemy, potentially leaving them too far out? Do you chromatize now, or wait until your actors' health bars drop significantly in order to take advantage of the full heal? These are things I caught myself thinking about before I committed to any actions.
+ The presentation and story are charming enough, even though I found myself skipping through the cutscenes more often than not.
+ Micro base-building feature that allows you to do things like respond to fanmail and improve the studio so that you can make the most out of your next battle.
+ It's obvious that the developers loved making this game and there's always something to be said for that.
There are some really deep flaws, though:
-The giant robot fight sequences. You trade out a decent-sized field for a setting similar to a really basic fighting game where your only options are to hope you click the right thing to defend (which only blocks a meager amount of damage) and hope your attacks keep hitting. Even if you lose this fight, there is a safe-guard that brings your health back to full, so I never really felt like these fights were as climactic as they probably should have been. Compared to the surprising depth you can get out of the field combat with the rangers, the giant robot fights feel really underwhelming and lazy.
-Dumb boss fights. "Sir, You Are Being Hunted" is a game about survival. in it, you have been stranded in a set of five islands after a mechanical device you made malfunctioned and sent you there. Your goal is to survive long enough to gather all twenty-five of the pieces of that mechanical device, in the hopes that completing it will allow you to escape the islands.
Now, you might be thinking to yourself "You keep on hinting at some danger and survival elements in the game. What exactly is threatening your life and preventing you from just gathering all the parts or deciding instead to live out your life on the islands?" The answer to that question, simply put, is: British Robots.
No jokes, no puns, no witty humor (which is normal from me). I honestly mean British robots. Upon your arrival to the islands, the robot denizens will do their damnedest to search you out and kill you for sport. These guys mean business. They've got shotguns and rifles, as well as robotic dogs, hot air balloons with spotlights, and many other things at their disposal that they will use to get you and mount you as a trophy on their wall. You don't want that. Being a wall trophy sucks. Trust me.
This map is randomly generated each time, with resources distributed randomly throughout. There are food items (because yes, you do need to eat), distractions you can use, useful tools, and the occasional weapon that you will thank whatever you worship for. As you find more parts, the robots try harder and harder to end your puny organic existence. Have fun trying to survive. I know I have, and I completely recommend that you at least give this game a try to see if it's for you. I love it, and I hope you do to.

The rules of playing LYNE is simple: 1) connect the shapes that are identical with a single line, 2) you must connect all shapes without missing a single one, and 3) you are not allowed to cross over the same line twice.

Sometimes they introduce a new puzzle element that temporarily hinders you, sometimes you find yourself hindering your own progress. But once you master the puzzle elements, you might be able visualise the solution just by looking at it.
If you are looking for a neat and simple puzzle game to buy, especially during Steam sales, consider getting this humble mind-boggler that is sure to occupy you for hours.

Let me quote you a bit of my original review for Cast of the Seven Godsends:
That was a year and a half ago, and I still remember the repulsion I felt at how stiff, garish, and low-budget the entire affair felt. It's heart seemed to be in the right place, a return to the old Ghosts 'n Goblins style of brutalist platformer (which I never appreciated to begin with) intermixed with some peculiar folklore and beasts. But so much of the design felt wrong in a fundamental way that I couldn't see any redeeming qualities in it whatsoever.
Since then, the developers released a Redux version of the game which featured a host of improvements. Chief among them (for me) are better animations, smoother movement, and new graphical options, all of which proved to be cures for what ailed me about this title. I didn't expect much returning to this one but what I got hardly resemble the game I had torn into a year prior. It's not without its flaws and I'm still hard-pressed to recommend it, but the efforts the developers made are actually enough to change my mind about its merits.
Cast of the Seven Godsends opens with your baby being stolen by a demon and a wizard for some unpleasant-looking ritual, and then you being sacrificed on a totally unrelated altar. The titular godsends bring you back to save your offspring and mete out justice, making use of their strange powers in your quest. I mentioned Ghosts 'n Goblins for good reason, because from the start you can only take two hits before expiring again but you can score armor to be knocked off in place of death. Your weapons are also varied projectiles you can claim from orbs that just appear when you pass, each with its own behaviors like flying straight, arcing, circling, and so on. Oh, but you can shoot up and down too, which proves to be incredibly useful.
If you can cling to your armor long enough to score an orb powerup, you can choose a godsend to take on the powers of. While none of them have outrageous powers they can vary greatly, such as the floaty white ninja who throws birds or the pink spike-hucking thing that slides around all over the place. Their aid will be invaluable in taking down the hordes of beastmen, ghosts, dolls, murderers, rocks, and other weirdness that approaches from all angles and takes tons of hits to defeat. Seriously, if you're without your powers you'll be pounding on some late-game enemies for ages.
That's hardly the only knock against the gameplay, either. As much as the movement  has improved it's still clunky enough to lock you in place while attacking and limit your jumps to weak hops. The levels you'll traverse with these limitations are also composed rather haphazardly and feature some frustrating traps like sawblades mixed with moving platforms and a glacially-paced lava crossing. The bosses aren't too complex but feedback on hits is lacking, and with no visible life bars it's impossible to tell how we'll you're doing in a fight.
While it may stumble on some basic design tenets, I can't help but admit I enjoyed the time I put into it this evening. It's such a far cry from the disgust I felt the first time I tried the game, which illustrates the importance of polish and presentation. The art was overly bold, poorly animated, and badly stretched last I played, but the new graphics options and additional animations made all the difference in the world. And the optional scanlines proved to be the real MVP here, tying the overall style together with warmer colors and a welcome blunting of the bold lines outlining everything.
I don't know that I'll ever finish Cast of the Seven Godsends, but it's certainly not outside the realm of possibility. It can be a challenging game and a little unfair at times with how some enemies can move and corner you, but the checkpointing is generous and you can dodge or run past a lot more of the threats than I expected. The biggest surprise of course is how the Redux corrected so many issues I had with it before that I can give a recommendation now rather than complete dismissal. This isn't a very strong recommendation, mind you, but if you're looking for a new take on the old Ghosts 'n Goblins formula, Cast might just do the trick for you.

Ok, I promised a review- although I haven't played the game through yet.
First off I want to mention this- the developers are one of the nicest I have had the pleasure of talking with.  If you research a little history about their project, it has been several long years and a lot of work for a small group of people to put together.  They are also kind and willing to listen to feedback from the community.  I can say from personal experience in talking to many other developers- this is a rare and treasured quality that you cannot learn to be but simply - ARE.
Now, as one more aside, I have bought copies of this game for several people and one of them is a developer of AAA titles who found the game to be way too hard haha-  but also a quality product with few issues.  He used to love Ghosts and Goblins and this was of course a great throwback.
About the game:
- This game is a niche title.  You must fill several pre-requisites to enjoy this game.  You must have time, patience and a high tolerance for repeating levels in almost its entirety.  You must also be a fan of the Ghost and Goblins series and their spin-offs.  The game adheres to many of the limitations of the characters before him- no throwing weapons at an angle but only up.  You also cannot double jump or drop down a platform.
- You DO have a health bar of a sort that you build up through picking up protection(s) when you have a special armor.  Armor are easy to come by and once you learn their locations you can power up quite a bit to withstand monumental colossal screw-ups.
I can understand some people's complaints about the game:
- the difficulty: yes even on normal it is punishing.  But this is the style of the title.  It is supposed to be so.  However, in today's gaming market overflowing with companies who want to strike it rich in the new virtual gold rush, it is more of a negative than a positive.  I love the challenge personally, but I have come to realize that because many gamers are now older, esp. the retro crowd, they do not have the time available to dedicate to learning tough and complicated intricacies of any one particular game.  Jumping in and jumping out with a mild or moderate challenge is enough for most people.  The challenge needs to be tuned to this crowd first, with the choice available for the purist hard core challenge seeker.
Also following Ghosts and Goblins tradition, you cannot avoid sometimes picking up some of the WORST weapons for a situation at some of the WORST times.  And you may end up stuck with it for a long time in the duration of your run through- Just like GnG.
- There are a lot of positives though.  The sound track is great.  I love video game music and the sound effects resound sharply throughout and the music captures the mood perfectly.  The weapons can be amazing- like the sword.  I have flown through many a level without any truoble because of default armor and a sword in hand.  It is just amazing.  Once you start holding onto your magic armor abilities of the seven classes of gods you can choose from, you will have fun discovering all the variations in their powers.  There are a lot of imaginative ideas balanaced with fair charge shots versus the power of each transformed bullet you throw.  The game has some interesting art- I love the style and it feels like I am running through a rotating painted scene inside an intricate fantasy story book.  The bosses are strict- meaning that you must adhere to their patterns that you have very little time to learn the first go around.  Again, you will die quickly even if you have a lot of hits to spare.
Lastly, the demon armor is hilariously OP.  Once you start not taking unecessary hits, you will earn this armor through multiple drops and then destroy the game in many places.  The game will reward tenacity and perfection with what will end up seeming like a breeze with OP gear.  But what you wont realize is, that getting there, you earned it with a lot of hard work.
*One important detail!!!
- There is an update coming eventually that will address a lot of concerns, new animations as well as some gameplay changes and item pickups.  I do not know about a save option yet, but this would be great.  I personally hope they allow for a level select feature!!!
I recommend this game because I respect the developers, their passion for this title and it is a fun and challenging tribute to GnG.  Good luck.  If you ask, I may even buy you a copy :D

Project Zomboid. This game is about surviving in a zombie apocalypse in rural Kentucky, and you are tasked with doing it alone, or with a friend in the very rare PC local multiplayer. I would mention the online multiplayer, but this game requires fast reactions in order to stay alive, and I can't find a server with a decent ping to "save my life" as it were. This game has many realistic elements about it, such as exertion, injury that halts ALL progress, panic as a game mechanic, zombies hearing your footsteps and following noise, sight, and smell, and perhaps my favourite touch of realism, the inability to see all around you at once. You need to rely solely on your senses in order to gauge the number of zombies currently breaking down your door, and surrounding your base, there's no minimap with radar, you just need to run out and hope for the best. Another great element of this game is that it is permadeath, which in case you are a dunce, means that when you die, you're ♥♥♥♥ed. In sandbox (Which I heartily recommend over survival, as you can tweak the settings), after you die, you respawn in another random location in your spawn town, and have to work your isometric♥♥♥♥♥off to get back to your base, and rebuild your skills.
One large issue with the game right now (which will in fact be fixed), is that the world is rather lonely. There are currently no other NPC's to hang about with. The biggest flaw of the game is that once you have nailed the perfect farming cycle, got all the guns, and fortified yourself to the point that a nuke couldn't dislodge you, there's nothing left to do! You're done at that point! I mean, if you set the zombies to never respawn, I guess you could clear out all of the zombies in the game, but that accomplishes nothing at the end of the day! Some might say that you could explore the vast map, and look for all the best items, but you don't really need to. If you use the PZ crash map like I did, finding your way around is no longer a challenge! Now I know that I shouldn't have used the map, but I thought it made the game more realistic, I mean, I know my city very well, I know where things are, and even if I didn't I could simply raid a gas station and get a map!
So, overall, this game is worth dumping your time into. It's a great zombie survival game, and I personally think that it is underrated. I am still super amped to have vehicles and NPC's but that's not happening for a while.

Kind of wish Steam had a neutral option but having played this through, I'm afraid I would not recommend it to my past self.
To start, advertising that can feel misleading:  Attaching the Stanley Parable name to this game just fools people into thinking there are choices, or maybe even a bit of humour or wallbreaking.
The Beginner's Guide is the opposite.  It's you, a narrator and a selection of one-way corridors.
The trailer in the store page makes it seem that as a player I would start this game and be presented with multiple snippets of games to play in any order and piece together an understanding of the creator through them to interpret as I like.
In actuality the narrator picks which games (or rather short corridors) you go through and forces an idea of the creator on to you.  Think of it like an English teacher at school who overanalyses a book to the nth degree putting meanings that never existed to add a depth that just isn't there.
While this forced viewpoint is given a twist at the end, the suspension of disbelief required to believe this story was simply too high to me.
I can see where people would enjoy such an experience but I would prefer a bit more clarity in showing people what they are getting into first.

SUPERHOT is generally an okay game. Clean and simple in regards to gameplay, cool sound-design, sleek retro aestehetics combined with a more modern feel inside the actual game world. Time moves when you move. Shoot, punch, and throw items (including your weapons) at the enemies coming for you.
The campaign takes under two hours to complete if you've played shooters before and once you're done, other modes unlock - such as speedrun-modes (real-time and ingame time), katana only, arena, and more. Story is delivered through chats, messages getting overlayed on top of the ingame world, and your interactions with the world at times. You also gain another superpower later on mixing things up a bit more (hover for superpower spoiler:
).
This all makes for a generally quite enjoyable experience and the combat feels like part puzzle and part twitch-shooter - time still moves when you stand still, but very slowly and you need to realise when there are bullets heading for you that you can't see while moving. This is basically a perfect blend for me.
Interesting mechanics, somewhat clever meta-stuff, solid and clean execution, but a bit short in regards to the campaign and at times feeling a bit pretentious (it feels like the developers are nudging you with their elbows saying "LOOK AT THAT, wasn't that clever???"). Lots of non-story content once you're done with the campaign.
I recommend this game, but you should get it with a discount.
If you need a score, then I'd say around 7.5/10 - well worth your time.

The Beginner's Guide is a delightfully meta experience. You enter a world made up of small "games" created by a developer named Coda. The games themselves have no real point, other than the experience of being in them. There are no goals, no real purpose to the games, and only one puzzle to solve.
As you play, the games change and take on a different feel. It feels as if you are watching someone go through a very real and difficult struggle. The narrator is trying to understand and connect to the game developer as he seems to spiral into some sort of depression. He seems to be developing games to give him someone to talk to about his insecurities. He is making games, talking only to himself.
In the end, you're left trying to figure out what happened to Coda. I won't get into the details so as to not spoil any surprise. But this game, about a developer of games without any obvious point, is itself without any obvious point. And the more you think and process what you see in the game, the more you understand the point, and it's beautiful.

The Left 4 Dead creators and the Borderlands Publishers come together to make Team Fortress 4 Dead, and how is it?
Well the positive:
- The game is amazing fun and super addicting
- Before seen Mechanics with a slight twist that are easy to use, difficult to master
- Cryengine. The game is drop dead gorgeous
- The sounds, both ambient and other are fantastic, effectively immersive
- The hunters are wonderfully unique, with no two hunters looking, sounding, feeling, or playing the same
- Each creature and monster is beautifully designed, with AI that brings the world to life
- Map design is very well thought out, with strategies changing on the fly due to environvent and terrain
- The Evacuation mode is a very cool concept, with varying degress of fun (More on that in cons, sadly)
And now the cons, because for all it's fun, it still has a lot wrong.
- The game feels like a beta, so many bugs (Falling through map, hunter spawning early, monster model bugging out     causing you to move insanely fast as a monster, etc.)
- The alternate gamemodes (Rescue, Defend, Nest, all except Hunt) are boring, often unbalanced, and albeit, bad.
- Evacuation, the 5 day campaign is an amazing concept, but ends up being drawn out and boring, with odds often stacked against even the most proficient monsters
- Many mechanics need re-working or tweaking (Ex. the sneak mechanic allows you crouch in plain sight of a hunter while they shoot you, and pounce them, leaving them defenseless)
- Day One DLC, Though cosmetic, this joke of a trend is infuriating, forcing gamers to pay extra for an already pricey title to make their characters pretty (For hunters, not even characters! Hunter skins are weapons only, stupid.)
- The Wraith, oh my jesus this thing. An incredibly unbalanced, no risk, high reward character that it suppose to specialize in stealth, but does well no matter what, that needs to be nerfed, a free win for the monster past Stage 1 (Sometimes at)
- The pricetag (This has me very mad), For the 5 (maybe 6?) gamemodes that are in the game, you'll only play one, the only unlockables outside of characters themselves are character skills, badge customization items, and Elite skins, your reward for grinding out a single character (Which btw, are terrible, and not worth the grind at all, just pay $5 for a better one I guess...) replay value, which we'll get to, is seemingly low, making this $60 title feel like it's worth no more then $40, if Im feeling generous, $100 Edition is also not worth it, advertising so much, and getting so little, you get the Magma skin for your Monsters, and the Season Pass to accompany your game.
And the final con,
- The Titanfall effect, everyone knows about it, the game was a ton of fun.... for about two weeks, unfortunately, this game suffers from that, I find myself having a blast with it for a few hours, and then craving something else, something better, and I fear for the longevity of this game.
Overall:
The game has it's ups and downs, you may question why you spent that much, you will growl in anger at the sight of a Wraith decoy killing your friend, sending him through the map, and you might even try to get a refund on Daisy for sniffing you instead of reviving you before she runs away from your dead body, but this game incredible fun, easily addicting, and a mandatory game to have with friends.
I will (and currently do) reccomend this game to anyone that craves the gameplay this game delivers, however, maybe not for it's current price, wait for a sale or for consoles, a pre-owned version :)

This is definitely a unique game, giving you one decision per year that will affect your kingdom in one of four areas.
The trick is to keep all of them (somehow) in (some form) of balance, and with very little knowledge ahead of time about how your decision will affect the future.
While this is obviously a steam port of a mobile game (or one that was simultaneously developed for all platforms), the lower price definitely makes this something that can be overlooked.
The majority of the game is very tongue-in cheek, full of basic visuals and vague choices. If you're a visual person, there's every chance this might bother you, particularly if you don't like the sort of art style they're going for. (Check screenshots if this is you first.)
The gameplay is very basic, and one of those "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of situations. I've done several playthroughs, and I still am not sure how to do the fencing minigame, for example.
A single playthrough can be easily done in ten minutes, and in true quasi-roguelike fashion, one playthrough can sometimes affect subsequent ones.
Expect to fail often, because the game very obviously is counting on it. That being said, the speed of your individual kings' lives make this far less frustrating than many other games of similar fashion, because you never really have time to get invested in a particular ruler. Also, your rulers don't exactly have much in the way of a personality (it's all just 'you') so there's no big loss when you die.
The pick up and play factor is quite attractive, whether you're simply not a PC gamer as a regularity, or you're pressed for playtime. Casual players will probably find this game very appealing, as would someone with a laptop or otherwise low-powered machine. However, there's enough meat to the game that a more hardcore player simply looking for a change of pace would find this game appealing as well.
All in all, based on price, depth, and ease of play, this is pretty much a no-brainer, as far as I'm concerned.

Chroma Squad is a game that begs to be great -- begs to be loved -- but just doesn't quite get there.
There is something lacking to this game in its basic combat system, and the way it feels. It's difficult to describe, whether attacks just don't feel satisfying, the skills your character possessing not being as useful as they ought to be, or maybe something else that somebody else can better elaborate. It doesn't help that it's almost impossible to pin down if the AI is just a little too good or just stupid enough to get lucky too often. Having played for almost two hours, managing budget, character equipment, studio perks, etc. seems just a little too frustrating and nervewracking.
The writing goes for light-hearted and funny, but it's just not up to snuff enough to be charming and actually land. Like everything else, it gets close, but doesn't quite hit the mark. Unfortunately, fixing that doesn't really make the game enjoyable.
If only the combat system was made a little more in-depth and satisfying, or if studio/equipment/money management didn't seem so futile, this game could be played and enjoyed. It doesn't even require both -- just one of the two will do the trick. But because the game is as it is, it falls flat and is almost perplexingly boring. And that is such a shame, because it looks fun from the outside -- and from the inside it really feels the game deserving of Chroma Squad's hype is buried just a couple inches away, but nobody's digging deep enough to hit it.

Chroma Squad starts as a simple Strategy Turn-Based Game but it offers many surprises. The teamwork mechanic is a simple concept that opens a lot of choices and suits well with the game genre and setting. Each character has a different role on the team and can be customizable from the name, looks, traits, abilities and equipment, making room for multiple play-styles and different tactics which make the game fell fresh and new as it proceeds. Fans of Sentai (A.K.A. Power Rangers-like shows) will be pleased to see that transforming into your Power Suit and gigantic Mech Battles actually play a role in the game.
Aesthetically the game makes use of Pixel Art with vibrant colors that suits with the lighthearted tone of Chroma Squad. The sound design is spot on with a great Sentai themed main song and a happy chiptune music that fuses together with the game’s vibe. The bosses are really interesting both in abilities and design and also very silly (like the giant pigeon with macho arms) but the minions do start to get a little repetitive specially as they get recycled as stronger versions with a different color scheme.
The plot is not very forward thriving but it does have some intrigue right from the start and it is a fun setup for the rest of the game. You will most certainly have some good laughs with Chroma Squad as long as you are ready to read through the characters’ dialogues. Although the game is very smartly written, it may sometimes become boresome as the scripted events drag on. As mentioned the game has a very lighthearted tone and it doesn't take itself too seriously which is actually connected to the main story.
• Final thoughts
Chroma Squad is a game that excels in the strategic battle gameplay with great, fun core mechanics and offers other pleasant side activities like the Mech Battles, Crafting and Studio Management which make the game flow fell fresh and non-repetitive. The direction of the story may seem a little odd sometimes as the silly, lighthearted, “not taking itself too serious” plot develops but it is a game that I recommend, specially for those who enjoy a really good squad strategy turn-based game.

A top-down shooter in a somewhat retro style, which is no bad thing if thats what you like. The action is not as fast paced and frantic as the trailer would have you believe though. You basically walk through each level blasting waves of enemies and jumping into "powerful" mechs and vehicles as you come across them. I say "powerful" because you don't really get the  feeling of being in big dangerous mechanical monsters, although they are mostly preferable to running around on foot. Character and machines can be levelled up as you progress, though there is not much functional variety between the weapons and special abilities in my opinion.
Gameplay is pretty repetitive and doesn't really differ much as you progress, but thats ok if you enjoy what it is. Multiplayer mode is a little disappointing as its just a co-op version of the single player and currently has no ability to communicate with your team mates.
Also at the time of writing this, you cannot remap the key bindings. You have the choice of the regular WASD and then some strange QZSD which I have never seen used before, but you cannot choose your own. A little annoying for those of us who might be left handed. The game does support gamepads though, which might be a better option.
Can't see why you would want to buy extra characters to play, as you spend most of the time in mechs/vehicles and the characters special abilities rarely come into play.
Overall I was a little disappointed, but if you like this sort of gameplay you will get a good few hours out if the game. For me, its one I might buy in the sales, but otherwise probably not. Lots more details and footage in the review video below.

First of all: this is a single player review as I haven't tried the game online... yet. I love almost anything concerning zombies and apocalyptic scenarios. And, in the case of project Zomboid, the well-established formula of scavenging-fighting-surviving in a harsh and hostile environment has been polished and taken to a new level. As in any zombie-related game, you will expect to have to fight and hopefully kill zombies. And you won't be disappointed, because in PZ fighting is vital to your survival. With bare hands, improvised, crafted and scavenged weapons, from axes to wooden spears to sawed-off shotguns, there is a quite generous arsenal at your disposal. But even if the threat of the undead is omnipresent, the thing this game really gets -RIGHT- is the feeling of despair, the constant, ever growing paranoia of finding a zombie right behind a door... and getting the bite that will eventually kill you and make you one of them. The scavenging part of the game is great, with a lot of different types of food, tools, crafting materials... and almost anything you will find is part of at least one crafting recipe. Running from a horde, buying yourself some time by shutting a door in their face before they break through... you look inside a wardrobe, find a sweater, rip it apart and craft a sheet rope on-the-go and make your escape from the window. PZ is full of these great, movie-like moments. And each time you play, traits and skills (recently revamped, in a very gdr-esque way) influence your playstyle, and your eventual demise. Yes, there's no happy ending in PZ... the very introduction tells you that each playthrough WILL end with your character's death. Be it for the ever present threat of the zombie virus, an infection, by starving, dying of thirst, or the most classic death: being eaten alive... you will die nevertheless. There are lots of things to be said about this game: there's a deep farming system, trapping, carpentry and much more. And considering this game is very much in development, with a great and very active community (for example, a well-received mod, Erosion, was included as a feature and makes the nature inside the game world slowly reclaims roads, buildings and so on) and the developers are listening to the players' feedback - adding a lot of interesting features (npcs will come back in the next versions, with a much improved AI and interaction with the human player) I can definitely and wholeheartedly recommend this game to you, even if you are only remotely interested in zombie games. It's already a great game in its current version, and, with hard work and a good amount of feedbacks, it could very well become the definitive post-apocalyptic experience.

Bite Size Review - SUPERHOT
The Good:
- Clean and Unique Art style
- Unique time and movement game play
-  Gun play is very satisfying
The Bad:
- Story is stylistic but has very little payoff
- Very little replay value other than challenges after the story is over
- IT IS VERY SHORT, I finished the complete story under 110 minutes
The Verdict:
This game is quite unique, fun, and interesting to play. When you move your character time moves as well, and when you stand still so does time, which allows you to move in short bursts to avoid bullets and line up kills on the diamond red enemies during the game's cryptic missions.
I enjoyed my time with this game and would go as far as to say any shooter fan should play it because of its unique-ness (there really is nothing like it that I have played). That being said though, please do yourself a favor and purchase this on sale if at all possible, this game is very short (minus the challenge modes that unlock after beating the game, which I have no interest in). I beat the entire story mode in under 110 minutes. So please keep this in mind before paying full price.

The Beginner's Guide is a delightfully meta experience. You enter a world made up of small "games" created by a developer named Coda. The games themselves have no real point, other than the experience of being in them. There are no goals, no real purpose to the games, and only one puzzle to solve.
As you play, the games change and take on a different feel. It feels as if you are watching someone go through a very real and difficult struggle. The narrator is trying to understand and connect to the game developer as he seems to spiral into some sort of depression. He seems to be developing games to give him someone to talk to about his insecurities. He is making games, talking only to himself.
In the end, you're left trying to figure out what happened to Coda. I won't get into the details so as to not spoil any surprise. But this game, about a developer of games without any obvious point, is itself without any obvious point. And the more you think and process what you see in the game, the more you understand the point, and it's beautiful.

When I visited Gamescom Cologne in 2014 and played Evolve for the first time I got hyped like crazy, cause I played it together with three friends against some random dude. It was great fun, nothing bad to say about it at that point.
Then the Alpha and later the Beta got me and my friend playing it for hours, trying to unlock new hunters over the Alpha/Beta-weekend. Still we had great fun.But in Beta the Game got a strange feel to it according to the content it offers to the players. Since not very much changed since Alpha, I was wondering how much content the game is going to offer.
Now that I played for like a week I decided to list some points for everyone and give a brief feedback:
PRO
-Great fun when playing with your friends
-The Maps look great
-Controlling the monster or hunters is pretty easy when you play for the first time, but mastering every single character is a challenge
->Even Beginners can quickly jump into it
-Custom games can lead to crazy matches
CONS:
-Not so much fun when playing alone
-->sometimes voice chat bugs, when playing with random people in matchmaking
-After some hours, you get the feeling like playing the same game all over and over again
-Matchmaking System "unfair". A Elo/Ranking would be better,since the lvl does not represent skill
-Balanced on high lvl ---> Unbalanced on lower skill levels
-No story mode
-It is like Cs:go --> play against other people, because bots/Ai are to bad..... -> not fun
-You can unlock and level up in custom games against the computer-> People unlock stuff and get lvl up, but do not improve->Matchmaking puts together player of same lvl but not the same skilllevel :(
---------------------------------------------------
After all I had great fun with the game when playing with my friends,BUT
Evolve is not worth the money you pay for. For 50 Bucks you get 12 hunters and 3 Monster and 12 Maps, and some gamemodes, that don't differ from one another. Therefore the amount of content is just to low. When i look over to some Indie-games that cost 10 Bucks, but offer the same amount of Content(-< time  spent, since it does not have a story you will only play multiplayer until it gets boring)I feel sad for the potential lost right here. The rest of the game will be coming out via DLC for the publisher to get even more money for little content. Like in "The Sims" you get a game that is fun to play, but to experience every part of it you are forced to buy a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of DLC, once you are hooked.
If you did not buy it yet, think twice before buying it.

I blessed this game with my typing fingers on the official Evolve Steam forum. I got banned because I posted a topic about a site for low spec computers to play the game through. And all I asked in return was for them to refer me. Since I saw that some people had problems running it. 14 days banned. No warnings.
But this is not why I am writing a negative review. The point is, the game is almost like a demo with multiplayer. The 4v1 is not a model I really like after testing it out. It doesn't feel competitive or nice to win against 1 person as a 4 player team, even though the monster is buffed up to counter this.
Playing the monster is not fun at all for me. You rely on yourself, and you can only win against bad pubs. Against a co-ordinated team, you can even lose as Wraith or Kraken.
But on the other side, if you are a casual pub player that just want to rank up in the leaderboards... well, there is no solo queue for you to do that (unless you count Monster as solo queue). This is rated 18+ but has game features for little kids that play one of their first games.
So, I stopped playing and went on after there were no more people to play with (in the morning). I had to wait a long time only to become my least favoured role (the monster) against a high level team of hunters.
The DLC in this game is just not okay. I defended it, but now that I am not biased because I bought a product from my bank account, I can drop my cover and see it how it really is.
So, the only way to support a game like this, according to the game devs and publishers... is to put all skins (except for elite skin) for sale, the characters that didnt launch with the game - for sale, and the monsters for sale (which already has a small roster) for double the price of a hunter. They want you to pay them to play the game, and then buy in-game stuffs. Advantage or not, we have yet to see, but with buffs and nerfs common in multiplayer games, it's obvious the newest will be UNKNOWN how to handle with and A BIT TOO STRONG.
Now I don't even want to play the game for a one round match. I get sick even thinking about the sad, depressive graphic environment around it. Not even a dark game like Diablo has this depressive environment.
I don't recommend buying this game, unless it goes F2P and gives the buyers of the product real life currency to use in the game. Which won't happen, because they will get even more bad rep then. I wouldn't even like it either, I would appreciate if I got back my money after they go F2P a lot more.

Evolve is one of those games that doesn't last long if you can't learn to have fun with it. Looking at it from the outside it seems very repetitive and boring, but if you have some friends and a few hours it's a blast. Gameplay is somewhat challenging as you have to work together as a team to hunt the monster, especially during stage 1 so you can deal significant damage to it before it gains more health. Gameplay is also really fun with the multiple strats you can pull together with different characters. Every match is a bit different and keeps it entertaining. The main thing people complain about is the matchmaking puts everyone in the same pool. I think in the future there should be a skill pool or ranking to match more experienced player with others and not newbies. Although sometimes it is good to learn from better/more knowledgable players rather than learn everything yourself. Challenges are there, but they are usually easy to obtain and relatively not that important. It takes awhile to get through them, but you usually accomplish them while trying to play without going out of your way to do them which is nice. Another thing is DLC. The DLC that costs up to 100$ is only cosmetic and is purely irrelevant, but I guess Evolve was the breaking point for gamers on the this issue *cough* CoD *cough*
TL;DR
Gameplay=Fun and easy to learn, can be brtual for newbies if against a good monster/hunters
Visuals=Great, but might have some FPS issues on some dense maps
Length=As long as you can make it last, depends on the player, challenges not really worth going out of your way to do
Things to know=Play it with friends or make friends, communication is key, makes it better overall
Hunters=All diverse with different class abilities and special gimmicks (Bucket blows, Cabot OP)
Monsters=Play Kraken to make the game no fun, Wraith OP, Goliath 3sneaky5me
Rating: 8/10 or 4/5

(Note Review is covering both Red Orchestra 2 and Rising Storm)
After playing 60+ hours, and playing on every map I can say this is one of my favorite WW2 FPS Realism games. You can play as 4 major factions each in their respective enviorments. The Russians vs the germans and the US vs the Japanese.
The core of the game revolves around working with your team to accomplish assaulting or defending objectives. The roles are broken down into a variety of classes such as Machine Gunner or Assault trooper. While most games you will find yourself playing as a basic grunt (rifleman) you can still be on par with any other unit on the field making balance feel perfect. In addition the gameplay is asmetrical, meaning each faction has its own weapons and play style. For example the Jap's can use Banzai chargers that when done as a group give the enemy suppresion and the chargers increased health. The Russians can "Ooorah!" charge suppressing the enemy and giving health increase as well.
Now if we look at how the community is it is around 1k easily on the weekend and somewhat less during the weekday. If you are from the US you should be able to find a Pacific or Stalingrad campaign at any hour but with minimal server selection.
TL;DR
Its a great game with a good community and highly recommend it.

Not a game for me. Reasons off the top of my head:
- Story, while ok for a short joke, is extremely boring and cliché for a long game. The conversations between the team members really don't help; "I am not good enough" -- "you are an important team member and we all love you" -- "I now know I am good enough" is just infantile writing.
- Mecha fighting is trivial with one repeated QTE that is just annoying. Yet is still a gear check, so if you were silly enough to not upgrade your mecha a lot in the start, you can get to impossible fights.
- Fighting with your team is reasonably varied, but gets very repetetive after you get far enough into the game.
- Fight setup is sloooooooow. Monsters arrive one at a time when fighting is about to start, and later stages have up to 20-25 monsters slowly jumping in and moving into place. Doesn't help when certain fights also do similar summoning of mobs/mines/etc. during them.
- Cutscene skipping is not a thing. At best you can fast forward (much too slowly), while the screen shakes, which quite frankly is annoying after the first time you use it.
- Studio upgrades (base upgrades, essentially) are not interesting and by mid-game there aren't any more new ones.
- Crafting, while interesting, has the very big weak point, that you buy upgrade packs with random items in it, which makes getting specific items annoying. Also, one item for mecha upgrades can only be found in mid-level fights (and certain one-off event), which makes getting specific upgrades for your mecha impossible once you use the last of that item and move on to higher level fights.
- I wish games would stop using the method of slowly typing spech one letter at a time for dialogue. Reading is not done by reading each letter and then building the word, it's based on recognizing the entire word and understanding what word it is, which is why you can read text even when all but the first and last letter have been jumbled up. Also, most people can read much faster than what games devs set the speech speed to.
I would not recommend this unless you honestly truly love power rangers in the way that bronies love my little pony; the joke setting really doesn't work for a long game and the core gameplay is not strong enough to make up for it.

Finished a playthrough and just don't get what LIMBO is going for. It creates a somewhat noir, immersive atmosphere and has elements that suggest a lot of potential, but failed to deliver to me on every front.
There's no story, the boy doesn't develop any character throughout the game. I wasn't even sure if I was done or at a cinematic checkpoint until the credits start rolling. The most interaction you get with this game is through your character's deaths.
The gameplay is deeply unsatisfying, as every puzzle appears to be a variation of "rocks fall, you die." Even after seeing/figuring out the solution there were multiple instances where I would miss obvious jumps because of how clunky the mechanics can be.
My biggest qualm with this game is that all of this feels avoidable. The game implemented physics to understand swinging on a rope, and sliding/tossing objects. The sparks, creatures, death scenes all look, sound, and feel amazing. Some of my favorite games are ones that are able to overcome their resource limitations creatively, like the way Firewatch avoids having to model people by trading it for rich dialogue. But in the instance of LIMBO it felt like the creators just chose not to fully utilize the resources they had. It's like I went to a restaurant and ordered a sandwich, and they gave me two slices of well-made bread, but they had all the other ingredients sitting in the kitchen.

In
's case, a single screenshot is sufficient to get a good a idea of what the game's about.  It's a simple minimalist puzzle game rooted in graph theory.  The puzzles are similar to
, with modifications to make things more interesting.  Don't worry if you don't know what I'm talking about; the game has a gentle learning curve.  The puzzles are short (you'll solve some in 5 seconds, and probably stare at others for 5 minutes), but there are 650 of them predefined, and the game procedurally generates more on a daily basis.  It's generally a fun, relaxing game, but can grow challenging and even frustrating at times (in a good way).  Graphics are just lines and soft, solid colors, which works well here, as do the equally soft and minimal musical sound effects.  Given the reasonably low price I highly recommend picking this one up.  You'll have fun while learning something about graph theory (though you may not be aware of the latter).

This is only a short review after finishing the campaign once with Ivan.
The game is exactly what was promised. A classic top-down shooter. End of debate. It's not tactical, it isn't really diverse with it's mechanics. It focuses on shooting things. And it does well at that.
You select one of (so far) three characters and jump into the action. The story is....well, it's there. Not more, not less. It isn't that good but again, this isn't what this game is about.
You watch everything in a top-down view (surprise). You have a primary weapon, a secondary weapon and an ultimate ability. While on foot, you summon a mecha, walker or whatever you wanna call it. On your missions you can find several vehicles you can use, and you will probably use them most of the time.
There you have: a small mecha, a big mecha, a small tank, a big tank, a helicopter and an airplane...thing (which is awesome because of stealth!).
In the missions you get several objectives which you have to do in order to advance. Alternatively you can go ahead, screw the objective (for some time) and just blow stuff up.
The game is relatively fast paced and easy to learn. It's not too easy, even on the easiest difficulty and you will need about 5 hours to finish one character-playthrough.
Graphics are okay. Nothing special and not well optimized yet (rare framedrop-spikes, even on decent machines), but it works and suits the game. (Note that highest resolution is full-hd, 1920x1080, no ultra-wide-screen support yet.)
Sound is mediocre. I'm missing some beef, especially with the weapon sounds, but it's not too bad. The soundtrack is really good, the voice acting not that much.
Controls are fine. Controller (Dual-Shock 4 with input mapper) as well as Mouse/Keybord work really well, even on standard-mapping. Until now, you can't map controls by yourself, so you have to use (the well working) default.
In short: The game is fun, yet nothing groundbraking. It offers you exactly what's promised, it can get challenging, you have unlockables and tons over tons of stuff to blow up. I haven't tried the coop yet but it's promising. If the developers do some fine-tuning, this could become even better.
(PS: Some people complain about getting shot from the edges of the screen and the "unbeatable difficulty even on easy". As for the edges, you are no sniper, so go ahead and approach in a non-linear way and get close. As for the others...the game isn't that hard. Perhaps you should learn to play instead of ranting on forums. People want to beat everything without effort these days...)

This game is almost literally Ghosts 'n Goblins/Ghouls 'n Ghosts, down to the intro.
While the art is nice, something feels wrong with it, like they added too much to make it look good, but it ends up being too busy, making everything blend together and may give you some problems playing. And for some reason whatshisface keeps rollerskating in the map screen.
The commands are responsive, but the character moviment and animation feels slow and heavy, maybe the devs are trying to emulate Arthur's moviment or maybe I'm too used to playing the actual Ghosts 'n Goblins, because whatshisface jumps are not high enough for most platforms. It doesnt helps that I get random slowdowns when there is
a light source on the screen.
The game only uses 2 buttons besides moviment, attack and jump, and for some reason the jump button is set as the cancel/quit button, making me quit the game twice before actually finding out what I was doing.
You use literally every weapon from Ghosts 'n Goblins, they only differ in appareance, and probably for fidelity, they kept that one weapon which the throw arc makes it fly just above the enemies, screwing over your aim.
You also can find magic armors just like on Ghosts 'n Goblins, although there are at least 6 of them. Instead of having one armor that boosts your current weapon, each armor comes with a preset weapon, so you have to know which armor has before equiping it.
Getting the armors is also a bit weird, you break the orb (like the chest in GnG), a beach ball comes out of it, you hold your attack button until symbols start to flash above you and let it go once the icon you want is showing up.
Enemies are a pain, the first level has TWO different enemies that are immune to frontal damage, one can only be hit while he is attacking (throwing a brick with infinite horizontal range) and the other only by hitting his back, but getting too close makes him turn around and hitting him only once also makes him turn around, and he only turns back if you get really far from him.
Bosses are another pain, the first one took me several tries because 90% of the time he would teleport to outside my range and the second one was almost impossible since I had the previously said arc weapon, his fireball attack had a ridiculously fast tell and it made a firefield where it hits, so you have to pull a tricky backwards jump, face him, shoot away and hope the weapon arc hits his head (the only place he takes damage, of course). Then he would jump to outside my view and spam fireballs from there, where I had no time to react because I couldnt see the goddamn fireballs.
In short, it tries to be a Ghosts 'n Goblins, but it doesnt plays as such. Not a bad game, but just makes you want to play Ghosts 'n Goblins. Maybe if you never played one, you will do far better than I did in this game.

Although it strives very much to live up to expectations, it seems like it cannot be done. At least not in full blown frontal 3D.
*If* you want to play something that will remind you of the original Ragnarok Online, then you will be probably heavily disappointed. The only thing that binds them together are a parts of the lore (still, very fuzzy).
*If* you are looking for yet another 3D MMO, then this is probably the right spot.
- Graphics are meh. Not in terms of the quality, but in terms of the visual style. I would expect something more from Gravity. Something that would fit into the sprite style of the original, but in a refreshed enviroment. Pastel Colors & outline more? Hard to tell, but for sure this one looks just bleak and boring.
- Controls. Could have been way worse. They mostly kept the RO style so quick bars, and shift-ctrl bindings, which are just perfect.  The camera seems a little sluggish though.
- Mechanics. Ruined it all. Boatloads of stuff, which at the first glance, have no coherent meaning and connection to the way the game play. Given for example the *new and confusing* card system. Took me a while to figure out. Also, the forging system looks a lil bit grindish' (but hey, that's ragnarok after all).
- Micro-payement. Reason for which i dropped the game. Don't get me wrong. I would like to pay, it it's done in a sensible manner. Here it is NOT. You have very slight idea of what you're paying for, what you will get, and what YOU ACTUALLY NEED. There are tons of stuff, most of them undescribed. Sure, you can buy *something*, but you need to do some digging to get the info on what it is, can you actually use, or how long will it last.
The whole game, minus the messed up micro payments is bearable.
Sooo... with the payments, it's not. That a NO from me.

Chroma Squad is the indie power ranger, an strategy rpg like FF Tactics. Its a unique game that uses props as armors and weapons, its because the story is involving a movie studio. What I like about this game is a mecha fight or megazord fight. No problem with optimization, game run flawlessly, but it lacks of graphic options.
Pros:
- Mecha fight, standard fight, 1 on 1, basically just hitting a def, atk, or skill button. Its repetitive, but still is a unique concept.
- Power ranger theme game, you can choose who will be the rangers from humans to dog. There are also space rangers that you can get when you pick certain choices in the game
- Story is OK
- Because the game is about making an episodic tv series, you can upgrade your studios, equipping your studios with new and high tech equipments, and ofc you can hire a marketing team, each team has their own perks, to activate these perks you need fans, yep sacrificing your innocent fans to the devil to gain some bonuses. You can gain fans in battle, every action you do will grant you a small amount of fans, you get more if you can fulfill the director's mission (sort of side objectives) everytime you go to do missions.
- Finishing move, there are 2 finishing moves here, both of them are executed by positioning your rangers around the enemy and use Teamwork command to finish their turn and the last ranger has to attack the enemy. Pretty neat.
- Crafting system, you can craft weapons, armours and robot parts. Fortunately, you can buy materials from the crafting shop, but its randomize though. And unfortunately, you cant grind money or materials in this game. Its kinda hard when doing the challenging difficulty because of this.
Cons:
- Graphic is bad, really bad. Because of lack graphic options, my rangers has become square rangers.
- The weapon I equipped to my rangers are useless aside from the skills attack. I dont know why the dev decided that any equipped weapons cant be used to attack the enemies, but can use their skills. I dont know if its a lack of animation or this is how the game designed the game
- Battle system is too simple and unpolished, aside from skill attack from weapons and from level up, there is nothing more. So, battle will become boring after a while.And because I cant grind materials or money, with no means to upgrade your characters, I had a bad time a few times on challenging difficulty.
Its not a bad game nor a great game, its OK game. So, I dont recommend this game. If you are a power ranger fan, you're good. If you're a casual, stay away. And if you're an achievement hunter, go for it.

is a masterpiece of platform games.
is a puzzle platformer indie game released in 2010. It was first released on the Xbox 360 in 2010, before moving to the PlayStation and PC in 2011, it latter got another port to PlayStation Vita and iOS, and yet another one onto the Xbox One and PlayStation 4.
A memorable game.
demonstrates that a game is not all about crazy graphics or well produced story line. It's hard to classify it: it's a platformer, but it will rarely require good timing; it's a puzzle game, but you won't spend hours trying to figure out solutions; it's a horror game, but there's no blood, no jumpscare, not even fear, just a disturbing atmosphere.
You’re a boy who wakes up in a lonely world made up only of black, white, and shades of gray. Video game logic demands you walk from left to right, jumping over obstacles as they appear, a simple task that needs little attention in the initial moments. This is your chance to absorb your surroundings. The background provides an illusion of depth, but its branches and bridges are out of focus, as if you are dreaming them into existence. The pint-sized hero, his bright blinking eyes shining from his blackened silhouette, trots ahead with the charming gangliness of a six-year-old.
Then comes death. Limbo is a hostile place, home to giant spiders that would feast upon you, and traps apparently scattered by the world's other denizens. You step onto a claw trap, and it closes on your neck. Your head falls to the ground and wobbles just for a moment before lying still. No tears are shed, no music plays. The game provides no grand gesture to honor your demise. It simply happens, and you revive at the most recent checkpoint to try the puzzle again. Some of these deaths aren't outright fair; stepping on a pressure plate could mean certain death, but so could jumping over it. Such inconsistencies aren't common, but your first time in Limbo requires some trial-and-error experimentation. Loading times are short, and checkpoints are frequent, however, so death is rarely a frustration, though often a horror.

LIMBO is one of the best indie games I've ever played. It was first released for iOS and android and I got a copy for the latter. The best part of the game is that it doesn't consume your time with tutorials. The journey starts as the boy, our protagonist, wakes up in LIMBO, the game doesn't even tell you that you've to press Ctrl for actions.
The dark black and white environment creates a really deep atmosphere with no music. The developer did a really fantastic job with sound effects. If you play the game with headphones on, it'll really sink you deep into the game and will make you love it straight away.
The gore in the game is unexpected. Usually when there are young protagonists in a game, their deaths or damages are not usually shown in a gory way. But don't expect something like that on LIMBO. The boy will drown to death, stabbed to death, chopped up into liitle pieces and may get impaled by a Spider if you are unlucky.
The game contains easter eggs too so observation is a required.
Overall its a fantastic game with many a difficult puzzles, and the best part is it doesn't give you the slightest hint in most cases.
10/10

Yesterday was some kind of day i was bored. Nothing to do and the Meeting with others in WoW Legion 2 hours away. So i took a look on the new entrys of steam and find this game. Hmm ... shooter ....hmmm ... tanks ... hmmm MECHS!!!!!!! Having a look at the graphics, pictures from the past rises into my Mind. Far far away, there was a game noboddy knows today anymore, or did you ever heard of FUTURE COP LAPD? No? Thats okay.
All right, the vids looks nice, just like FUTURE COP and yes of course MECH COMMANDER. Well, i like mechs very much. From the beginning of my childhood. The 80´s. Girls were playing with barbies, boys with cars and me? Me was playing with Mechs (on my AMIGA 500).  Looking at the price ... oh ... okay. Music sounds good, 2 Euros more ... got the Special Edition. Starting installing and 30 Minutes later starting the game.
So, lets have a look. This game is an old school top down shooter. In this Game, Story set into the future, you were at first playing a Lone Wolf in a battle armor, who was hired by a corporation. You can jump, run and shoot. You also got Primary and secondary weapons. Following the story you complete one target after another until the end of the level. After 2 Targets i got my mech. This One is slower but heavenly armed. You can enter and leave the Mech each time you want.
Following the game Episode after Episode more and more Units can be set free. At least you can have the control on a light Mech, a heavy Mech, a light Tank, a heavy Tank, a battle Helicopter and a Stealth Helicopter.
The interesting point is, that each Unit gains experience only, when you use it. They can raise Levels and you get points to raise your Units. The Maps you are playing are big and everywhere are units ready to enter. So, the game let YOU the choice wich One you play to complete the levels. From my experience you can survive with each one, also the battle armor. By the way, if they shoot one of your Uhits down, you are not dead, you will be pushed out of the wreck in your Battle Armor. The Battle armor has an interesting feature, with the secondary weapon you can turn smaler enemys into friends or stun the bigger units for a while. Also you can call another Heavy Mech if you fill an energy bar.
Hybrid Wars is really great shooting fun. The gameplay with the Controller is really good. With one stick you controll your moving and with the other the shooting. This game is a shooter not a tatical RTS Game, but it has slightly tactical elements. From upgrading you units (No play -> No experience -> No upgrade), to the choice of using each of them.
Also i like the music, that fits perfectly into the game. And the music is really great.
IMPORTANT: If you buy the normal Hybrid Wars you get one character, with the Special edition you get the second character and another one if you create a Wargaming account for Multiplayer. More charaters are DLC`s.
The only negative point is, i can`t find other players in Multiplayer. Seems dead. Wargaming should get the Servers of Europe, Asia and America together.
So, if you like fire and forget games with good music and nice graphics, if you liked MECHWARRIOR 3050 (Mega Drive) or FUTURE COP LAPD, if you like just having fun, this game is for you.
Oh yes, my WoW Legion Meeting i mentioned at the beginning, i forgot it. Because of this game. Sorry Mr. Illidan ....

Even though this game is in early access, it feels much more complete and fun than most early access games that I've played. I've always been wanting a more immersive survival game experience, and this game delivers. One thing that I've noticed is that if you can do it in real life, it's most likely possible that you can do it in the game. For example, you can hang sheets over windows, rip up clothing to make bandages, farm, fish, cook food, collect rainwater, etc. Even though this game is a zombie survival game, compared to other games Project Zomboid puts a heavy emphasis on survival and is where this game shines. After a while all power and water is shut off, you can cut trees to build walls and shelters, you have to deal with scratches, blood loss, infection, fractures, heat, exhaustion, fear, pain, hunger, thirst, and a whole host of other difficulties.
Another thing I really like about this game is that it has local co-op. If you have a way of plugging in an Xbox controller, you can play with someone else on your computer, which is nice if you want to hook it up to a TV or something and the controls aren't too bad for the controller (although somewhat clunky at first).
I really like the way this game is headed and the changes the developers make (like the recent addition of all of the different occupations for your character which give you different strengths and weaknesses) and it was worth every penny!
My one gripe is that the online server system hasn't worked well for me. I usually get ejected from servers randomly and I've tried making my own server but it's just too much work. I hope they make it easier in the future to host a game (unless I really missed something and there's some easy way to do it, which means I'm probably dumb).
I recommend this game!
P.S. The music is fine, but after a while it gets kind of old. Maybe add a few extra tracks in the future? Thanks :)

This is by far one of my most favorite games to date! It blends the minutia of management of supplies with the frantic running, scavenging and fighting of a great action game.  It has fun, believable crafting and RPG elements, with the ability to really customize your experience. You can modify the difficulty in various ways from rarity of spawns, type or speed of zombies, what kind of weather, how long the day is, etc.
Also, this game is amazingly fun and easy to modify. As a modder myself, I can attest, with a little trial and error you can get the hang of the lua coding fairly easily. The modding and forum community is over at the Indie Stone forums is fantastic, there are incredible mods already (some of which the dev have fully implemented in the game like the Erosion mod). On that same note, the Devs are responsive and willing to take and respond to criticism/suggestions. Also, there are weekly progress updates so you don't have to worry about the game being abandoned by the devs.
So, moral of the story, BUY THIS GAME. I have played many other zombie games (which I loved) like Left 4 Dead, State of Decay, etc. but this one tops the list by a long shot.
Edit:
I have had to since this review stop working on the mod I was doing for this game. That said while I was the devs worked very close with me.  Whenever an update would kill a part of my mid,  they would go back and fix the game to be compatible so ib wouldn't have to update my mod for every change. Hence my vote for the Labor of Love award. Kudos to IS. 5 more starts for you if I could.
