I played the entire season before writing this.
It's very funny and the dialogue is excellent.
It's one of the newer point-and-click adventure series, though it's actually one of Telltale's older games because it was made during 2006-2007.  However, I see it as "newer" because it's broken up into smaller chunks and doesn't require you to pick up that many objects.  Older adventure games usually pack your inventory with all kinds of things and some serve no purpose in solving the puzzles.
Like many other Telltale games it's split into episodes, so I will summarize what I think of each one:
Episode 1:  It introduces you to the characters and emphasizes the hypnosis theme which is prevalent in all the episodes but especially in this one.  The Soda Poppers are funny but a little creepy, and the main enemy is pretty silly.  I liked this episode alright but it's not the best one.
Episode 2:  You again deal with a hypnotized person, but before that you have to succeed in a variety of TV shows.  This is is one of the funniest episodes and I highly recommend it, especially since you don't have to go back and forth between areas quite as much.
Episode 3:  Funny if you like Chuck E Cheese parodies, but ultimately I didn't like the main enemy in this one.  I didn't get a sense of what I needed to do in this episode quite as much.
Episode 4:  Well, if you ever wanted to meet Abe Lincoln here is your chance.  This episode makes pokes fun at the American government a lot and the best part involves a campaign speech you have to sabotage.  It's one of my favorites for sure.
Episode 5:  This one has a lot of old-school video game references so I found it very amusing.  The main enemy reminds me of SHODAN slightly and the colorful environments are quite attractive.  This is probably my second-favorite episode next to Episode 2.
Episode 6:  You finally find out who is behind all the hypnosis issues and well, it's not particularly surprising.  It's a trippy episode and fun if you hate silly New Age philosophy cults.
Overall it's a pretty hilarious adventure game, though it doesn't offer the challenge that the older adventure games did.  Also, this game is quite old now and the 3d graphics are somewhat underwhelming.  Even so, this is a good place to start if you are curious about Sam & Max and want to play a comedy game.

Was so excited for this. I figured it would be like a megaman type or any other platformer. Boy was I wrong. Apparently its a ghost and goblins rip off. Which basically means theres like 20 guys on screen shooting at you or homing in on you with traps all over, and if you get hit 2-3 times total you die. Theres like no health. You have set lives, and then continues, even though we're in 2015 and this isn't in an arcade, so you should get unliited lives. Theres no diagonal aiming, which once again, we're in 2015. It just feels frustraing for the sake of it. Guys respawn within 5 seconds of killing them, meaning theres always guys coming at you from all sides of the screen. regular guys have WAYY too much health. Instead of normal platformers, where guys take 1-3 hits, many commong guys take 8-10 hits, which hilariously is more health than you. Love games where common guys have more health than you. No joke, in one part, I killed an enemy, then then jumped past where he was, but he'd already respawned and hurt me. You pick up random things, but you have to destroy globes just to get them. Random weapons have different firing arcs, which can screw you in certain situations. The jumping and platforming are also kind of janky. Skipping text is also poorly done, leading you to instead of speaking up just skipping entire lines. It's cool how you can morph into different guys. There's aren't many checkpoints, and you accidentally destroy the checkpoint. I guess if you like constantly dying and redoing things with limited lives/continues and guys that take too long to kill, this is your game. If you were looking for a good platformer not ripping/mimcking off an old NES game, then skip this one.

An absolutely stunning experience, the game was a blind discount purchase just for the hahas, and now I can't force myself to turn it off. Over 33 hours played and I think I just only start to fully enjoy the game world.
Cons:
- No maps! Guys I badly need the maps! Of course, I can find them online, but it would be cheating. I think it is quite realistic when a lost man FINDS some maps in a car glovebox, desk or wherever. I personally believe that having at least fragmented (torn, burnt etc.) region maps would only make things more interesting. Otherwise, the signal pistol challenge is sooo unforgiving.
- Some actions are often quite schematic and overly simplistic (especially behavior patterns of the wildlife and wolf atacks). But it's a game, not real life, so with all the following pros these two cons are utterly forgivable.
Pros:
- Really thick atmosphere, so thick you can cut it with a knife (if you ever find it, of course).
- An unforgettable feeling of natural awe and helplessness when things go wrong.
- Variety of weather conditions. It all depends on the weather, like they say!
- Absolutely great maps and locations. I really enjoy all of them, Pleasant valley being the best!
- Automatic and quite boring actions and processes suddenly become really interesting (I could never imagine I would love so much to collect firewood or sort-out bad chocolate bars by a campfire).
-The skill improvement system is decent. It adds another dimension to the gameplay. Not an RPG, of course, but the idea that you can progress makes you feel even more aggrieved when you finally die.
- The graphics are better than I expected. I really love how they did the lighting thing and the blizzards!
To sum it up, The Long Dark looks like a really promising game for now, and it's already 100% playable (although being in Alpha). I wonder what the campaign mode will look like. And I really would love to have some extra content too (more new regions and please introduce the map orientation challenge too!)     :)

That's a game I discovered through Youtube, and that I bought on a whim. And I don't regret a single cent.
The graphics are really beautiful (no, they're not realistic, they're not meant to be), the audio is on point, gives you hints of animals approaching or weather changing, the gameplay is relatively easy, the sandbox huge enough to have fun for hours, especially if you try on the different challenges (which ARE challenging, don't fool yourself). In this game, you will die, and die, and die again.
So it is a survival, and it is a sort of rogue-like. Your death is permanent (meaning you can't come back to a save point, if you die), and the game automatically saves (and cancels all previous saves) when you are injured or suffer from something (and god there are many things that make you suffer in this game, from hypothermia to food poisoning). Some might find it punishing, some might like it.
However, there are some problems.
First of all, the impossibility to jump ANYTHING is a problem for me. No, I don't like being stuck on something which looks like a 15 centimeters patch of snow while a wolf runs behind me. I don't want to be forced to move 3-4 steps on the side just because, in the middle of the road, the texture of the snow slightly changes. Maybe link the jumping capacities to the stamina bar, and make it impossible to jump when your stamina is low, that would be okay ; but absolutely no jumping is a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥tty.
The wheel to use your inventory and crafting abilities is a good thing for consoles. For PCs, it's not. Having to hold a button to have the wheel and then moving your mouse to select what you want is not as easy as just opening a crafting menu and selecting something. Small detail, but still.
Last concern (but a big one) : the game runs like♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on mac. And I really mean it. I have a good enough config to play most games at 40-70 FPS. Subnautica runs at 30 FPS for me, which is still playable. The Long Dark runs at 7-8 FPS, which is NOT playable. So, if you're on Mac, I suggest you wait a bit for some update/patch that will help correct this. Or that you equip special goggles allowing you to play at such a low FPS.
Overall, it's a great game, it's still in development, take it if you're not afraid of experiencing some problems. If you don't want absolutely any problem and want to have a finished polished game, wait until this one is finished. There are plenty of patches/updates, quite regularly, and they always bring something new. Can't wait for the full storymode to appear!

To add even more scares, you play the whole game with your trusty camera equipped with night vision that slowly drains your battery life. Throughout the game you must balance between using the night vision as saving your batteries, but don't worry you'll find more along the way. There are your occasional jumpscares, but it's not a main factor.
The game scares you by its atmosphere and its characters, and not just by jumpscares. This is how you make a horror game.

.hack//G.U. was good on the PS2, and despite a few nitpicks, this remaster is the definitive way to experience it. It's an old favorite of mine, and I'm thrilled to see it more widely available, since the PS2 version's become rare and expensive.

Chroma Squad is a nicely simple tactics RPG and a very cute parody/homage to Power Rangers and Super Sentai. Tactics RPGs can be hard to get into because they're often 100+ hour epics with large numbers of characters, classes, and items to sort through; Chroma Squad strips away a lot of that to create a tactics RPG that doesn't require the same level of commitment, while keeping enough elements to maintain a certain level of strategic depth.
For the most part, beating the missions is relatively easy - the tricky part is usually trying to fulfill the optional objections to maximize your audience. This worked pretty well as a way of challenging the player without punishing them too much for the occasional failure. Unfortunately, the giant mecha fights are more difficult and rely fairly heavily on luck.
The character statistics are pretty straightforward, but some of the global boosts aren't as clear as I'd like. For example, how much is +10 Drop Rate? I guess the base Drop Rate is 100, but it doesn't seem to say that anywhere. +2 Fan Conversion Rate and +25% Crafting Rate are similarly unclear.

Outlast. I had heard about Outlast for a while before I played it. I was a horror-game enthusiast prior to this game, as I became hooked on the story of Amnesia:The Dark Descent and it's sequel - Amnesia:A Machine for Pigs. Both games were brilliant, both for story and the aspect of horror. I was skeptical of Outlast, at first, but as I began to play the game, I also become hooked. I wanted the Journalist to escape, and bring the corrupt Asylum down. With a motive to play, I sat down and just kept on playing.
Outlast is, primarily, a horror game. And it excels in the subject. It terrified me. From the jumpscares, to the atmospheric buildup, to just the general level-design. It was not just horror, though, it had objectives, and I had to solve puzzles and figure things out for myself. One scene in paticular was extremely horrific, and made me appreciate the game a lot more. Fearing for my character's life, I cautiously progressed through the game, hiding beneath beds, outrunning escaped lunatics, looking around with seemingly no way out before I decided to jump out the window...
The game was gripping, and terrifying.
For it's horror aspect I would give it a 9.5/10.
But scares aren't everything. The story felt somewhat lacking and cliche. The notes I found were mostly just patient analayses, with subtle hints at things to come. I didn't feel much character-progression, and when I completed the game, I didn't find myself feeling like I had just read an incredible story, but more like I had just narrowly escaped with my life, a suitable feeling to be left with in a horror game, but I felt it needed more in the way of a storyline.
Overall, the game was definitely worth the buy, and provided a horror game experience like no other, it outranked even Amnesia:The Dark Descent in terms of horror, but felt like it needed more story and character development - something that was mastered in Amnesia:The Dark Descent.

Anybody can't do a ghouls and ghosts clone... And this game is the living proof of it !
While animations are pretty nice (and I like the death of some enemies) just like the graphics (it's RPG maker graphic style, if you like that kind of stuff, especially the hero is a clone of some RPG maker character), while the powers (infinite until you get hit too many time) are superb and changing following your weapon and so are the attack animations... I can't give this game a thumbs up and I would discourrage anyone hoping to find a reasonable ghouls and ghost clone to buy it !
So why don't I advise this game? Let me say that hit box are not well defined and so are the platforms on which you seem to jump on or not randomly + the graphics make it sometimes hard to define what is a platform what is not which makes it really frustrating.
The game play of the character doesn't feel good, you can upgrade his jump and speed ability with some powerups you find here and there but it still make the character lousy to move around and jump.
And probably the most annoying way this game plays: Enemies ! They are repoping so fast, you don't even have the time to make a jump to cross a platform or move forward ! And let me say that you will most oftenly die because of enemies spawning from out of nowhere that from the lack of your platorming skills.
The game is unforgiving but you will encounter a lot of "automatic ave" spots to restart from that point and that was a good idea seeing how the game is and how frustrating the fast enemies spawning is.... It will always prevent you from moving.
At the volcano level you will see boulders rolling towards you and that's okay but the platform they are on is not very well defined and they will fall right on your head when you think you're crouching on a safe spot... disapointing.
Then there is the problem of speed... the game is simply overdoing it with speed ! It is way too fast and the platforms and other saws are going to frustrate you because you do not have the time to jump on them and when you do have the chance to jump on a moving platform you will probably get it by an enemy you killed 2 seconds ago (no really, it's spawning that fast, 2 seconds... maybe less !)
Then there are the bosses... graphically very nice, they aren't much of a challenge... you might die a couple times against a boss but when you will defeat them, it will always be because you just mash buttons like crazy so they will die insanely fast without even casting most of their attack ! So it's either all or nothing with them, you will meet one casting spray of fire and fireballs really hard to avoid and you will keep dying until you start over and kill it crazy fast... you won't even understand why? Also, there are a lot of small bosses all over and they're all that way.
You still want to buy it because you think the powers look amazing? You're right ! But think twice !
To get a power you first need to get one of those big sphere, since you start naked, you will first get an armor (yeah!) and the animation of getting it is really nice, I give them that ! But to get the so called power which seem so cool, you need to wear the armor and find another one of those big sphere... Let me tell you, it's not happening that much at all ! You die really quickly and I do not have any issue with that, it's unforgiving and wants to play that way? Okay, I can accept that ! But holding the armor until you get another one of those sphere to get the power is insanely hard since the enemies spawn so fast and from every corner...
I reached the ice level and the only time I got one of those power was twice, in the very first level and slightly later in the swamp... Each time I didn't keep them very long because of spawning enemies.
Charging the power is okay but takes quite a long time and when enemies spawn so fast, you don't have the time to really charge it that much... And anyway, it's better to mash enemies and try to run forward than trying to charge your power to kill everything on screen... Same with bosses!
And I get fed up of the game already because you don't have the time to jump on a platform that enemies are preventing you from moving but when the platform is slippery, you're sure to die after a couple try !
Anyway, huge disapointment, it's nothing like ghouls' n' ghosts which played much better than this one !
If they ever change the speed of spawning enemies, the speed of moving platforms and make fights against bosses more ballanced and so more challenging, then the game might be worth it and a serious opponent to ghouls'n'ghosts.
Meanwhile, do not buy it, go instead buy tiny barbarian which will give you a lot more fun and challenge because this one here isn't challenging or fun, they got everything wrong ! They tried to make it unforgivable by using stupid mechanics like crazy fast respawn of enemies, crazy fast traps and moving platforms and bosses which either gives you all (and won't possible to even touch) or nothing (and you won't understand what happened).
Seems the game was developped too fast as well... Thumbs down ! Devs, I would like a patch which fix those issues !

The game isn't easy, but it is fair and the levels aren't very innovative, but still well designed. The gameplay reminded me a lot of Ghosts 'n Goblins and I think that is intended. I'd like to leave a few words about the developer of the game as I think it does matter in this case. Afterwards I posted about a gameplay problem that I had and again the developer looked into it right away and offered a fix within a day. That plus the price of the game really show that there are indie developers out there that love making games and care for their customers. My sincere respect for that.
If you like retro games and/or challenging games you should really give this game a try.

EDIT: There IS a way to easily fix this on your Windows 10 computers! What you need to do is this...
(credit to Kong)
The following is working for me with Season 2 on Windows 10:
Open the files folder for the game on your harddrive.
Backup prefs.prop and all .save files.
Delete those files from game folder.
Run REGEDIT
Go to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Telltale Games\Sam & Max Season 2
Modify Windowed from 0 to 1
Run game. It should now be running windowed!
I had to play through one episode in a very compressed Windows mode, but by the next I was playing at full screen again!
If you want full screen, follow this guide...
Step 1 : You need to download and install Notepad++ from the following link:
(NOTE - Didn't need to download Notepad, I had it already).
Step 2 : Open up your Steam folder, by default it's in 'C:\program files (x86)\steam'. in the Steam folder you must go to '\steamapps\common' and there you must look for the 'sam and max' folders with the season and episode number behind it. Here you must open up the folder of one of the episodes that won't work for you.
Step 3 : You might want to copy the 'prefs.prop' to a save place in case you break something in the next steps, but this is not required if you know what you are doing.
Step 4 : Open the 'prefs.prop' for the Sam&Max episode that doesn't work for you by right clicking the file and selecting 'Edit with Notepad++' (or edit normally)
Step 5 : The file opened will look unreadable at first and you must scroll the bar to the right to find the word 'Windowed' followed by the number 0. You could also use the Search option inside Notepad++ to locate this word. Now you only have to change the 0 to 1 and save the file. (In case there is no 'Windowed' in the file, rightclick the game in the library within Steam go to 'Properties', and then click on 'SET LAUNCH OPTIONS...' and enter -sw. Launch the game once, it will crash but the 'prefs.prop' should be altered and have 'Windowed0' in it again after opening it with Notepad++. after this remove the -sw from the launch options)
Step 6 : Start the game, this is to check if the game runs in Windowed mode like it should. You can change the resolution to what you like, but never ever click the fullscreen option again or you will have to edit the 'prefs.prop' file once again.
Now we can make the game run in Fullscreen using Borderless Gaming
Step 7 : Install Borderless Gaming and start it (after you bought it offcourse). After that go to 'Options' and make sure it starts every time you start Windows by checking 'Run On Windows Startup'. You could also go to 'Tools' and click 'Disable Steam Hook' to make sure Steam won't tell you are in-App Bordelless Gaming all the time each time Borderless Gaming is launched.
Step 8 : Start Sam&Max in Windowed mode and in under the Applications window in Borderless Gaming you will see 'Telltale Games' appear. Click on that and then followed by the arrow pointing to the right so 'Telltale Games' will be visible under 'Favourites (automatic)'. Rightclick 'Telltale Games' in here and make sure that 'Fullscreen' and 'Auto-Maximize' are checked.

Sam & Max: Season One is made of 6 point'n'click adventure games, connected by the plot of hypnosis.
It's one of the first games to use episodic model of releases. And unlike many others, it used them with success, making TellTale produce more adventure games in similiar fashion. It also seems to be one of few games to be on Steam before it was cool.
Oh, and it doesn't support widescreen. Sorry folks, 2007 year and all.
Episodic model is also used in good and bad way, in a sense that you have common location and few common characters (outside of those that are unique to single episode) that keep reappearing in each episode. Sybil is most amusing, as she changes job every single episode. Such familiarity works nicely. But then, there are some negativity about it too, like, in the last episode you can suddenly pick up object that main hero refused to keep in all previous episodes.
Graphics and music have style to them, even though they are a bit weak. Both of them. Well, or not so weak.
Fine, music is nice, but more of staying in the background. And graphics are fine for cartoonish style. Lacks some good shadows though. But hey, was designed for low-end machines back then.
It's quite usual old-schoolish point'n'click by gameplay and plot, following same mindset of "puzzles are the main point". Which isn't bad thing. Combined with expected humorous approach. Mature one even. You do get few hard puzzles that I am sure you would want to use at least some hints from the almighty Google. But at least you feel clever when solving some of harder ones, at least I did, when figured out Checksum puzzle.
Did I mentioned humour?
Actually, characters interaction and humour is one of the best in when it comes to "old-school by being linear and humor-based", outdoing most of older titles.
It's a pretty nine series. Some may like it, some may not. Others will choke on rainbow bliss. From smiling too much.

The fight mechanics of this game are really interesting - monsters come in groups, different in number, members strength, stats, attacks and abilities. Furthermore the damage and delay of attacks is quite random, so the situation is ever-changing and therefore interesting. Every character has some arsenal of spells/abilities at their disposal, so development and execution of effective fight strategy adapted to the situation is the key if you are going for ambitious kills. Now multiply that strategy bit by party playing, where you have a friend or several; engage monster group with that small army and it goes even more strategic and interesting (to some point).
PvP is rather standard boring stuff as usually you don't know the level of character you are matching against (except the more known experienced characters that are well-known), and the character level and equipment makes the real difference (the choose of skills and strategy being rather obvious quickly). So you win or lose at random, no much playing value there. There is also no in-game reward, except some fame maybe, so only bullies might like that, slight exception if you race with friends in character progress or equipment development. Clan-wars are the same PvP stuff just more extreme deviated, as one clan comes to war with 10 lvl-40 characters, versus 3 lvl-30 characters from the second side, so you already know the result, no fun there for losing side.
Finally nations (there are 3 unchangeable nations to choose from at the very beginning): it may be fun to jump on someone who comes in the wrong corner or go for crusade to other country, but the overwhelming hate that is related to this concept is rather depressing in long run. Finally: are we all men or frenzy animals? The game-creators concept is rather obvious in that matter. Languages concept (quite interesting alone) do not help to communicate with foreigners, but it provides feeling of frustration that is very reflective: is it just like that when real nations cannot effectively communicate each other? An excellent Russian movie comes to mind, where Russian man, German man and native Czukcza (Siberian native) woman are trying to live together during WW2, speaking three different languages, their converations are masterpiece misunderstandings.
Quests are not really innovative, but give a strong boost to character experience development, especially on later exp levels. Here where it goes really bad: from some point you know more/less all the mechanics, monsters and concepts, there is no real point in the game anymore, except "exping" here, "exping" there. Quests became rare as they are level dependent but going up to next level takes more and more hours of useless butchering.
Then you say to yourself: what is the real added value that the game gives to me _now_ and the answer is NONE. So: finally you manage to drop this time-waster and the only proof of your weak-will (slightly going to insanity) is the game built-in time counter that says like 50 000 minutes, that you can hide from your relatives but unfortunately not from YOURSELF. What I would happily save others from...

The dialogue is very simplistic in order to match a certain personality type assigned to a character. The translation is rough and you can spot quite a few typos. Quests give plenty of experience, so it is easy to level up a character to 50. However, it is hard to find players to run through dungeons at later levels. It's not uncommon to wait up to an hour to find a tank or a healer. PVP is pretty much P2W and laughably unbalanced. After you hit level 50, you can complete a quest to become a "Master Class." This is where I lost interest in the game completely. The game becomes a pointless grindfest. Every time you die as a Master Class, you lose experience (called master points)... unless you purchase an item from the cash shop to avoid the penalty. Players have been leaving and many servers have been shut down since RO2's inception. The developers have put less effort into keeping players interested and more effort into milking as much money as they can from a F2P game. With the community dying, I don't see much of a future for Ragnarok Online 2.

I normally agree with crowd ratings, but this time I have to disagree.  There are a lot of haters out there, to be sure.
I really like evolve because
, and does it well.  There is a lot going on behind the scenes and a great deal more strategy than you would expect from a shooter.  There are a lot of people complaining about balancing issues, and many of them clearly haven't put in the time to get good at the game, based on what they say in their reviews.  It's supposed to be hard to kill the monster and it requires a coordinated team.  I would venture a guess that today's "monster is OP" crowd will be crying "monster needs buff" when the really good hunters begin rising to the top.  So my advice would be not to make your decision to buy based on what the "balancing issues" people say.
Arguably there is a limited amount of content, but if you are looking for a good chase experience then there is really no substitute for Evolve.  I'm guessing that a lot of the people♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off because of the lack of content are actually unhappy because of the announced DLC prices for new characters.
It's both thrilling and rewarding to chase the guy around, almost win, almost lose, and then win in a spectacularly close finish.  I have a lot of alpha/beta/full release experience and I'm still not bored because there is always something new to learn, always some new strategy to use.  It's possible that some will get bored before they put in the time to really work on strategy, and you should wait for the price to come down if you think you might fall into that group.

If you've ever played Brothers in Arms, this is what this game is similar to. The campaigns in this game mainly involves taking over checkpoints or defending them. So rather than just only clearing an area like in Brothers In Arms game, you have to also take over a checkpoint area for your team. If you've played Star Wars BattleFront 2, you'd know what I mean by checkpoints.
The graphics and and audio sounds and looks realistic when maxed out. Too bad audio appears to be only stereo. The gameplay is similar to that of Brothers In Arms where you're squad leader and can command a group of soldiers under you to do your bidding, but if you die, you don't restart but can control as one of your underlings.
I played this on Frontline Soldier difficulty, the bots you command are next to useless, besides soaking up bullet holes for you. The enemy AI, well they sometimes do the impossible, like a few times I was running for cover and saw a LMG soldier in front running towards me and shooting at the sametime. Killed the people who was behind and then headshotted me! I tried to replicate that(once I was controlling a LMG or had an SMG) to see if I could run and gun and get headshots too, but all I managed to do was get insta killed! Hahaha - the accuracy on these guns - might as well just aim up to the sky and shoot whilst running looking upwards! Also at times, I believe they were able to shoot through walls! Well I am certain of that as the area infront of me, or behind rather was clear of any bad guys as my units were already moved in! I've also noticed they are able to looking in a completely different direction yet still be able to one shot me to death...
Hahaha, all this bullcrap gameplay but I still managed to complete both campaigns! Can't imagine anyone doing it on Hero difficulty...............probably as soon as you get out onto the battlefield and seeing absolutely no one, insta one shot dead. hahaha
Oh yeah and the campaigns/bots are bit glitchy/buggy too and yes I did run into the infamous stuttering bug which seems to be a thing here...but it somehow fixed it self up.....only happened a couple or so times...
But nevertheless, it's a good game to get your feet wet in WW2 era stuff.

10/10 Apocalyptic Zombie Survival Roleplay Game
Why should you buy this game?
1.This game has been in development for many years, and the DEV's have been dedicated to this game since day one! Never in my years as a pc gamer have a seen a development team so willingly accept the ideas and concepts of their fanbase. And because they have acted so, the game over these past years has transformed into something truly beautiful. The attention to detail is quite supurb. With their current track record I can honestly say that they will never abandon this project like 95% of the other Zombie Survival games you'll find on steam littered with bad reviews.
2. In its current Alpha stage it is a very playable product, there are no game crashing bugs that I have run into, zombies don't walk through walls. The soundtrack to this game is godly and makes for a very immersive experience. And the game mechanics themselves are very fun and allow you to roleplay how you would surive the zombie apocalypse from almost every angle you could possibly think of with more to come in the new builds!
3.multiplayer works perfectly and setting up your own server is quite simple enough and if you have any issues the PZ community on the IndieStone's forums are more than happy to help you out. If your looking to play with friends I sudjest setting up your own server because the larger public servers that people in the PZ community run tend to be a bit laggy depending on where you are connecting from. Which has nothing to do with PZ's multiplayer coding it is definately a 3rd party server overtax issue. When I first tried the multiplayer in the public servers I was put off by the lag but when I hosted a private server with friends I got to see how truly awesome It was to survive with friends in realtime. I hope in the future someone will invest in some server space to accompdate a 64 person PZ server because when It wasnt lagging in the Public servers the gameplay was brutally fun.
4. The IndieStones dedication to their customers. I purchased PZ many years ago on a platform called Desura, back then it was just the skeleton of what the game is now but I still loved the idea and hoped they would continue development. This year I saw it on the steam store, and decided to go back to Desura and try out the new multiplayer build. I even convinced a friend to buy it after reading the change log. I log onto Desura and find that Desura sadly will not put unstable versions of a game(Steam Does, because their awesome) So I was almost 4 builds behind and could not play with my friend who just bought the game. "Add the desura cd key to steam! I'm sure it will activate!" A wonderful idea and as I try to activate it steam tells me that the key im using has already been activated on another account. Now I'm super bummed because I must have added it to another steam account years ago and completely forgotten. I'm too poor to afford the 15$, so with a last ditch effort I go to the IndieStone forums and tell the Dev's my story. IN ONE DAY! NO QUESTIONS ASKED. I am private messaged a new CD-Key! Input the key "Key is already in use on another account" ♥♥♥♥! So i reply back to the PM and tell them it didnt work. They reply with a SECOND CD KEY NO QUESTIONS ASKED! That one worked. NEVER! NEEEVER! In my lifetime as a pc gamer has a company so willing and without question offered such kindness. They totally could have read all that as a way to scam some game keys out of them, but no! It was unreal. And that is why I will forever wave the IndieStone flag like a drunken fan boy, because these people give a s*** about their customers. That is a quality in a gaming company that is incredibly hard to find these days.
If you love survival horror games. Buy Project Zomboid, I promise you won't be dissapointed. :) How will you die?

LYNE is a puzzle game, its release date was 17 Mar, 2014. The publisher and developer of this game is Thomas Bowker. This is an intriguing puzzle game, with actual puzzles, you don't walk around and move objects to opens doors and stuff like other puzzlers, in this one it is like a simulation with nifty graphics. The aim of the game is to connect all objects together, and you can't leave any untouched.
The game consists of 26 levels, each letter of the english alphabet is a level. Each level consists of 25 puzzles. All up you will end up completeing 650 different puzzles. But thats not it, there are also daily challanges with can have from 1 to 3 puzzles, some are harder than others.
The game may seem easy at first, but as you get to higher level letters it can get rather challanging. As you get to higher levels you will get harder puzzles, this means you will get more variety of different colours, different grey ones requering more numbers, and a bigger amount of shapes. It can get rather challanging at the higher levels.
You can finish the game anywhere from 10-15 hours, but of course it all depends on how good you are at this game. The achievments in this game are quite unique, everytime you finish a letter you will get an achievment which is that letter, so you can spell words and stuff on your profile in the achievment tab things, its pretty cool.
This game is pretty cool, its challanging, cheap... what more could you want, my final verdict is a 9/10

To me, instead of making a Legitimate upgrade to RO they made yet another basic MMO.
In RO1 I could enjoy the skills, their animations and my overall time played because it felt alright. Here in RO2, it feels like a poorly made clone MMO. Animations cut themselves off or repeat suddenly. Sound effects are insanely annoying due to the sheer amount of enemies that repeat their stupid sound effect over and over again. The UI is entirely made to look cutsy and just cludders up the screen with useless crap. (Yeah, I get they love the poro but give it a rest already!)
The camera movement starts off stupidly fast for some reason, as if this is some fast pace FPS or Third Person Action game. It's far from needed as you'll just walk to target, smack target and then walk to next target. In short, it doesn't feel right. The game is played without issue on my computer but the actual gameplay is not smooth. It feels janky and unfinished; basically lacking quality polish. Then it bombards you with Cash shop stuff and tries to ease you into all their related items and options. It's content first then ask us to buy your crap, not the other way around.
I'm sure the game has all the End level nonsense as RO1 did or jobs within jobs of jobs but I couldn't be arsed to play the game any longer than I did. It litterally brings nothing interesting or new to the table. It takes from existing games and doesn't take the really good parts from them.
I want to enjoy the combat, I really do but if I wanted to play an extremely slow paced MMO there is still RO1 or a list of many other similar games.
If you aren't really wanting to play this game then just don't waste your time downloading the game and then having to patch it afterwards as the game obviously doesn't send patches to steam to download. Play something else.

The Long Dark is single-handedly one of the best games I've ever played. Even in its Early Access state, it never fails to impress on the level of entertainment it provides. And boy, does it provide a lot of it.
But like all great games, it's not without its flaws. Very few of them, but they are there.
Can I just say "everything"? No? Okay.
1) Never had I played a game that awakened the empathetic man in me. When my character is cold, I feel freezing, even in the summer. As soon as he starts shivering, my toes go numb. When he yawns, my eyes go heavy. When he makes a fire, I suddenly want to cook s'mores. When a wolf bites him, it's biting me. I can feel the pain. I can feel the desperation of searching for that next pit stop in search of canned peaches. I connect so well with the protagonist that I fear for his life, for it's not only his, but ours I must save. When he's in danger, I want to protect him, and his ultimate demise fills me with dread. Rarely does a game make me feel this way, so... f***ing kudos, Hinterland.
2) The graphics are unlike any I've ever seen. They resemble colorful construction paper, pasted on a vibrant charcoal background. The uniqueness of it provides a sense of overall joy. It feels real, and yet, doesn't. A very surreal take.
3) The uncomplicated utilities menu, encumberance system, and status screen. I seriously hit tab constantly, even when I don't need to.
4) Commander Shepard.
5) The entire world map is expansive and daunting. Just when I think I'm about to pass out and die, I come across a cave, or hidden cabin. Again that feeling of hope and excitement when I actually find an abandoned house is unsurpassed.
6) Commander Shepard.
7) Random item placements to give an even bigger boost to survival for when you start a new game. There's no memorizing this one, folks. You're on your own.
8) Did I mention Commander Shepard?
9) Hunting and harvesting. Skill-ups in particular things, like stiching and making fire. I love the feeling of improvement and progression, and I think they nailed it.
1) Unfortunately, I have to address that this game has been out for, I think, years now? There's still no story mode, and I have no idea when it's going to be released. The sandbox is entertaining for a little while, and you'll be testing yourself to push it to the limit every time, but a story really would be great for a game like this. Especially when it comes to playing two separate roles.
2) How I want to feel when a wolf comes near me:
How it REALLY is when a wolf comes near me:
Don't let me look, don't let me look-- OH GOD I LOOKED!
Seriously though, when it comes to the wolf attacks-- which make up for about 98% of my deaths-- some of them are just plain ridiculous. I once found a wolf
Yes, THE WOLF WAS CAMPING INSIDE OF A BUILDING. How did it get in? I have no idea. No shattered windows, all doors closed. It's a mystery. I could have made it that one time, if not for a f***ing wolf
.
Without wolf attacks, I seem to do just fine, really. I'm on my fifth game or so, and I've decided to wuss out and play it on Pilgrim. So far I've lived for over five days. It's still some pretty tough stuff, and still pretty threatening. Just in different ways. I almost died of hypothermia one night.
This game is awesome, and I definitely want to see more of it. I can't wait to play more. It's become almost a nightly ritual to huddle up at my computer, curl up in a blanket, listen to the sound of a looping crackling campfire and play The Long Dark!

I never ever liked any sandbox game because I don't like to imagine what I should do in the world, create some purpose in the game to play it. The Long Dark suddenly changed it. Yes, the graphics are schematic for now, yes, maybe some features are missing, yes, there is big amount of slow walking around and long actions like starting fire and cleaning rifle. But, god, this thing is SOOOOO atmospheric! The landscapes look surprisingly real, thanks to warm colors and carefully designed locations plus realistic weather conditions. The sounds and ambience - I won't even say anything about it, you should feel it. These walks with a lantern in the darkness, making coffee on fire in the forest, finding shelter from the sudden storm, ice fishing in some small hut, I want to do this again and again. Support further development of this game and buy it, you won't be disappointed!

Sir is a good game, and a fresh new take on the survival genre. The gunplay is decent, nothing special but nothing particulary bad. The stealth system is almost too easy but still presents some challenge. The robots are amusing as they are terrifiying. The scavenging system is alright, and the cooking function is a good idea as well. The enemies are varied and intresting, and for such a simple engine as Unity, they are actually quite intelligent. Graphically the game is pretty bad, but I dont really care about graphics personlly. The game is pretty hard though. The game throws you absolutely no bones, and your lucky to find anything of real use while scavenging, so the name of the game is adapt or die. In the end im giving Sir a four out of five. It's nothing revelutionary or really any kind of breakthrough. But it does what it tries to do realitively well. If you like stealth and sruvival games, I would definetly give this a try. An absolutely stunning experience, the game was a blind discount purchase just for the hahas, and now I can't force myself to turn it off. Over 33 hours played and I think I just only start to fully enjoy the game world.
Cons:
- No maps! Guys I badly need the maps! Of course, I can find them online, but it would be cheating. I think it is quite realistic when a lost man FINDS some maps in a car glovebox, desk or wherever. I personally believe that having at least fragmented (torn, burnt etc.) region maps would only make things more interesting. Otherwise, the signal pistol challenge is sooo unforgiving.
- Some actions are often quite schematic and overly simplistic (especially behavior patterns of the wildlife and wolf atacks). But it's a game, not real life, so with all the following pros these two cons are utterly forgivable.
Pros:
- Really thick atmosphere, so thick you can cut it with a knife (if you ever find it, of course).
- An unforgettable feeling of natural awe and helplessness when things go wrong.
- Variety of weather conditions. It all depends on the weather, like they say!
- Absolutely great maps and locations. I really enjoy all of them, Pleasant valley being the best!
- Automatic and quite boring actions and processes suddenly become really interesting (I could never imagine I would love so much to collect firewood or sort-out bad chocolate bars by a campfire).
-The skill improvement system is decent. It adds another dimension to the gameplay. Not an RPG, of course, but the idea that you can progress makes you feel even more aggrieved when you finally die.
- The graphics are better than I expected. I really love how they did the lighting thing and the blizzards!
To sum it up, The Long Dark looks like a really promising game for now, and it's already 100% playable (although being in Alpha). I wonder what the campaign mode will look like. And I really would love to have some extra content too (more new regions and please introduce the map orientation challenge too!)     :)

The game is fairly fun and I enjoy the asymmetric nature of the title. However it has huge issues that really hold it back from being something great which makes it hard to recommend.
One of my biggest issues with the game is the unnecessary grind to unlock hunters and monsters. You are forced to level up each skill/weapon to rank 1 before you can unlock the next hunter or monster, if something is rank 1 already it can not gain experience until every other skill/weapon is rank 1. You will feel forced playing certain characters and focusing on using a weapon or ability you don't like or that doesn't suit the situation. It took me 14 hours to unlock all the hunters and monsters.
Next is the issue where you don't get to play what you want and most often then not you'll be forced to play a hunter or a monster you don't like, over and over and over again. The game makes you preference the 5 roles in order, however it does very little to match you with the role you want which also makes the grind more annoying. People get pigeon holed into playing monster and usually leave the lobby. The game will also place you in matches that have already begone, this sucks because you don't get to play the character you want that match and if you're monster then you're probably losing.
The game doesn't offer very much variation and their isn't any interesting single player campaign. The game has bots but they aren't entertaining enough and all they do is follow you around. This is a purely multiplayer title where all the game modes feel a little to similar.
Lastly the greedy DLC model they decided to use for this title really sucks and only makes you feel like you got the "cheap" version of the game because you didn't shell out the extra money for the fancy edition. There is nothing worse then paying full price and feeling like you got the cheap version.
I don't recommend this game now at full price and I don't recommend this game in the future when its on sale! By then the multiplayer scene will be on its last legs, its already hard enough to find matches. I don't think the games crazy DLC plans will breathe new life into this title 6 to 12 months down the line because extra characters and maps wont fix the annoying grind, repetitive gameplay and down right silly match making.

This game is terrible.
Pros:
Conceptually interesting
Uses the pretty Cryengine
Great art design
Voice chat works out of the box (you know you're scraping when something like this is on the list)
Cons:
4v1 Gameplay
Every round completely depends on how good the one person that is the monster is or how bad the team of 4 players are.  When playing as the one monster you can assume to lose from the get go.  It doesn't matter if you are level 1 or level 3.  If the Hunters have a minute understanding of how to play their character you will lose the 4 v 1 fight, maybe not in the first encounter but eventually.  If you win as the monster, the group of Hunters are terrible or were following one fool around without thinking.
Unlocks
You pay your massive wad of cash and you only have 1/3 of the characters and can look forward to a stupid Call of Duty like unlock system that makes you more powerful in the game regardless of whether you win or lose or if you played well or not.  The grinding rank up system was stupid and broken to begin just as it is stupid and broken in this game.  You also unlock more damage and "perks" for every character the more you play.  Really want to do something specific?  Better get to grinding hours of this game rather than enjoying it.
In addition there is paid for DLC and a season pass which is just plain stupid for the lack of content in the game.
The best characters and monsters need to be unlocked, the optimal choices are obvious which leads you back to the question why lock the characters and make bad characters to begin with.
Maps and Gameplay modes
Terribly limited, tiny maps.  A small amount of map knowledge as a Hunter will make sure you can catch up to the Monster earlier than expected, shortening rounds to 7 or fewer minutes.
There are only 2 gameplay modes on a map pool that can be counted on 1 hand.
User Interface
Very distracting, the map takes up a huge portion of the screen when it is up.  Excessively helpful to the Hunter team to the point where even if you are playing someone who has outsmarted you, the "hints" lead you exactly the correct way.
Trash Respawns
Even if you kill a Hunter as the Monster, that person is back in the game in 2 minutes.  There is no reward for taking down just one character and you shoudn't waste your time as the Monster doing so as the other 3 can endlessly kite the Monster and wait for their 4th or kill you.  Evolve's skill ceiling is low already without the helping hand of insanely quick respawns.  Even if you get wrecked for being stupidly out of position you know you'll be back in the game in 120 seconds.
Gameworld Danger
There is none.  Animals in the way?  Ignore them just fly over the top and continue chasing.  There is no impediment to the Hunters, eventhough the game feverishly tries to tell you there is.
Clearly this game was play tested on consoles where FPS is challenging and something that holds back the Hunters team whereas on PC playing as Hunters is easy mode.
I have no idea how the team that came up with Left 4 Dead regurgitated this trash.
The multiplayer community is already dying.  Don't waste your money on this game or even reward the game developer if it goes on sale.

I have very mixed feelings about this game.
I am going to give this a very very weak "recommended," but this review is going to focus on what you need to know about this game prior to purchase.  It's a very, very mixed bag.
THE MISCONCEPTIONS:
I am absolutely appalled by the amount of hate this game receives for its DLC for the simple fact that none of the DLC gives you a distinct game play advantage.  The DLC is on the expensive side, but every character, every perk, every map, and every gameplay element can be gotten through the game's progression system.  The ONLY thing available for DLC that affects gameplay is to unlock all of the characters.  That's it.
The characters themselves are decently balanced.  There are some useless characters and some OP characters, but those are to be expected so long as the patches come through.
THE GOOD:
This game surrounds a very simple concept:  Kill the monster, or be killed by it.  But, within this concept are some extremely rich mechanics that make this game very difficult to master, but the game can very easily just be picked up and played without reading a strategy guide.  Each class has a very specific and focused goal in mind.
The simplicity does not get old because there are very different styles of teams, individuals, and monsters.  Some monsters power farm and try to scale up as quickly as possible, some monsters sneak around all game until level 3, and others will look for ambushes as often as they can be gotten, and very many other styles.  I believe that this game has a lot going for it considering these things.
THE BAD:
The frustratingly bad thing about this game is♥♥♥♥♥♥poor matchmaking.  It's awful beyond belief, with 80% of the time you being thrown in the middle of a game that someone else left.  If you are a new player as I was, you'll be thrown in a match on a completely unknown class, often times right in the middle of a fight!  You have no idea what perks you have ,how many times you died, or even what level the monster is.
That is, when you can get into a game.  Often, I found myself "waiting for players to load" for 5 minutes, so I quit the game realizing that I wouldn't get a game, and then I have to wait an additional minute just to click "find game" again.
Also, there are abilities that belong to certain classes that just seem out of place.  Supports with orbital barrage, medics functioning as snipers.  I would prefer more assault classes to put those abilities on rather than cramming them on team helping roles where they're forced into a conflict of interest.  Give them a sub par weapon for damage dealing and have the rest be supporty abilities.
THE UGLY:
While this isn't the most buggy release, there are more bugs than your average release in this game, such as being stuck in animations, being unable to attack something right in front of you as monster, mobile arena getting you stuck in terrain to where you can't move momentarily and are just floating there.
THE VERDICT:
I recommend this game because of one reason:  When it works, it is absolutely fun and heart pounding.  Even when there's not a lot of action, the suspense will keep your heart beating and you won't ever feel bored.  But, know that this game needs a lot of work, the DLC is very expensive, and the matchmaking is in an atrocious state.  If you can tolerate those things, then your $60 is well spent.  If you don't have patience, however, then save it for something else or wait for a sale.

Currently, I own only the base game, and have played primarily medics.
To start with the thing everyone seems to pick on first, the price. This is by far the most I have ever spent on one game, but I consider it well worth it's price. I was extremely hesitant to get the game at such a high price, but I was able to play in the beta version of game, and enjoyed it so much that I did purchase the base game (three monsters, twelve hunters - the only ones currently available to play in game). And I've not regretted it. I've had an amazing amount of fun with just the three medics, and I'm looking forward to unlocking the other hunter characters in the other classes and learning how to play them. I easily see myself sinking a few hundred hours into this game without getting bored. Not to mention learning to play the monsters, which have a whole other learning curve to go through.
Balancing - I hear this both ways, people say the monsters or hunter are either too easy or too hard to play, either the hunters are overpowered or the monsters are. In my opinion, based on the numerous hunts I've participated in with both incredibly skilled monsters and very unskilled ones, with a great team of hunters and terrible ones, they're fairly evenly balanced. A lot of whether or not a hunter or monster is "overpowered" or not depends on whether that characters play style suits the player.  Even hunters in the same class play very, very differently. Some suit a player, others don't. When they suit a player's play style, they can seem overpowered, but it's really just player skill. Some times it's also a matter of player mood. A lot of people say Lazarus is the weakest medic, but I play all three medics fairly evenly. I don't find any one of them any better than the other. Which I play depends a lot on the mode of the game, and my mood when I'm playing. I play Val when I'm prefer to stay out of the main battle and aide from a distance, I play Lazarus when I'm inclined to be sneaky and stealthy, and on defense modes, and I play Caira when I prefer to be running up at the front lines. I've had great battles with all of them against good monsters (including the wraith). That said, it took me suffering through many a terrible battle when I first started playing Lazarus, until I figured out how to play him properly. Now I find him just as fun to play as any other the other medics. This goes the same for the monsters, some will suit your play style others won't. I saw I guy struggle with Goliath during the first four rounds of an evacuation match, only to unlock the Kraken in the last round and pummel us all the first time he played it. I've seen other players do terribly at the Kraken because they can't coordinate all it's long ranged attacks. The only exception to this is the Wraith, which does need some adjusting done to it's balancing, as it is currently very difficult for a less than proficient hunter team to take out even a reasonably skilled wraith player, but it's by no means impossible. That said, the game is barely a week old, and there will be sure to be balance tweaks soon enough to fix any balance problems.
Game play pacing - Some people complain that the game is boring and repetitive, or has too much "chase" time playing the monster. I disagree with this completely. If you're bored with this game, it is either because you're not playing it right (AKA you're not taking the time to learn how to play your characters or you're not playing as part of a the team), or because this is not a typical first person shooter. I personally do not like first person shooters. I find them annoying, boring, repetitive and generally lacking in any kind or actual necessity for player learned skills and tactics. Yet I love Evolve. This is the first game I have ever felt like I was reasonable competent at as part of a team, and it is precisely because it isn't just a "shoot everything that walks by" type of game. In fact, if you spend the game shooting every wildlife animal that crosses you're path, you'll never catch the monster, and likely will get yourself killed a good number of times and irritate your teammates who have to keep coming back to revive you. It's better just to hop over them all and keep chasing. Learning how to predict the monster's movement, communicating with and working together effectively with your team (push to talk comes in handy here), and knowing how to play your specific character (hunter or monster) all go a long way to succeeding in Evolve. Evolve is not a typical shooter game, and in my opinion it shouldn't be. The fact that it isn't like every other shooter game out there is exactly what I like about it. If you want to play a typical shoot em' up game there are plenty of other games out there for you. Evolve is not one of them. It's a game of mind games and stealth and tactics and teamwork.
Controls - I've only ever been a PC gamer, I find the default controls work find, with the exception that I remapped the push to talk button. If you don't like the default though, you can always remap them.
DLC - Yes, there's a lot of DLC coming in the future (new monster characters, new hunters, and weapon/monster skins), but you don't have to buy it. You can still play against or with those DLC characters, you just can't play them yourself. None of the new maps will be DLC, they'll all be available for everyone. Furthermore, and interesting note about those "cosmetic" DLC skins, particularly for the monsters. They can be used as camouflage. The monster/hunters get to pick skins after knowing what map they're going to be on, so if you know you're maps well, as the monster you can choose a skin that will allow you to blend in with the terrain, which makes it much harder for the hunters to spot you, even when they've got you domed. I've lost track of many a monster that blended in with the terrain, even when it was trapped. It's a small boost, but in the right match it could be enough to win.
Other good things-
I really like the evacuation mode. You get to play five rounds with the same set of people, so you have time to learn how your different teammates play their roles so you can work better together. Usually a full evacuation (all five rounds) takes about an hour to play. You also get a lot more experience for playing evacuation (as both hunters and monsters, even if you lose), and the people playing it tend to be higher skill level, and more dedicated to doing well in the matches, since they're about the invest an hour of their time playing it. Once had two back to back evacuations with the same group, by the time we were through the first evacuation we were coaching the wraith player on how to better play the monster, just because we could and it was fun to really go up against a challenge. We still managed to win the evacuation, but just barely. I like the feel of good sportsmanship that seems to prevail in evacuation mode.
The things that are bad(ish) -
-Matchmaking's not terrible, but it could definitely use some improvements, especially for matchmaking when you're in a party. There should probably also be a way to tell it not to place you as certain hunters or the monster if you really don't want to play as them. Personally though, I've found it pretty rare that I get put into a game as anything other than my first or second class preference.
-Some of the maps are really small, which is irritating as a monster, and too easy for the hunter. When I win a match as a hunter on the small maps I almost feel like apologizing to the monster, because he really didn't have a chance. Again, this is a bit of a balancing issue and will likely be addressed in future updates.
-The jetpack is a little finicky about climbing certain walls.
-Buggy? Some people say it's buggy, I've only encountered a few fairly minor bugs in the final game release, only one ever affected game play (fallen teammate was stuck in the floor and I couldn't revive).

Ladies and gents... I present to you Outlast, aka: Door Slamming Simulator.
Now before I start, let me give you my personal opinion, despite my recommendation being a thumbs down.
I actually enjoyed the game to an extent enough to beat it- BUT. The game has many flaws.
Let's start with my gameplay first. When I first played, I decided to go on Nightmare difficulty because hey, I'm not a wuss. I later guessed that with higher difficulty your battery life probably drains faster and *maybe* enemies are more difficult? (I honestly haven't tested this on the easier difficulties.) I found myself strobe-lighting my camera's nightvision function just so I could see through the dark 6/10 times so I wouldn't be trapped in might-as-well-be-wearing-a-blindfold-pitch-black darkness.
When I'd encountered my first enemy, my first thought was to hide, obviously. Stealth mechanics=♥♥♥♥♥♥ Your ONLY options of hiding are either to move around in the darkness, hide in lockers/under beds and tables/ in crawl spaces. You can't hide behind most objects. I'm almost 100% sure someone is going to give me♥♥♥♥♥♥about that last point, but if there's to be a stealth mechanic like that, I'd like to hide behind something that looks like decent cover such as a laundry cart.
Also, since I gave up on stealth long ago by abusing the "Stealth" mechanic, I simply just walked around in the darkness when it was safe to do so or whenever the enemy was a good distance away. Honestly, halfway in, I abandoned stealth altogether and just ran everywhere while slamming doors in front of their faces. Works every time.
Now let's move on to the "Horror" part of this game. Honestly, I was only surprised 2 or 3 times. The rest of the time I was so afraid of losing battery life because then I'd be stuck in pitch black purgatory. The *ONLY* fear factor from my perspective was being trapped in the dark with terrible lighting(if any, depending on the area) and the occasional "jumpscare". For people who've played Alien: Isolation, Dead Space 2, and others similar to those, they should be hardened enough to anticipate those.
Overall I enjoyed the concept, but not the execution of the game. If others are fine with these flaws, then I'm not one to judge. But in my opinion, stay away from this game unless it's on sale.

Reigns is an interesting title that has all of the allure of the old "pick your own adventure" books. Each choice is alluring and wondering if you are making the right choices is always fun. There are 4 resources to manage. Religion, wellbeing of the people, military, and federal cash. If you let any of these reach bottom, or reach too high. You lose! Example. IF the people get TOO happy, they think they should overthrow you. If you run out of finances, you have no way to ward off merchants. Ect. There are lots of bonuses that last round to round (you don't start over entirely when you die, just a new king). These bonuses are fun and keep the game interesting. When you encounter new things, it adds new random cards to the deck. This game is fun as heck, and I also bought the Android version for my smartphone. Some people complain when an android/ios game gets ported to steam, but I'm honestly glad this is here! If I'm sitting somewhere with my gaming laptop, I'd rather play it on there than drain my smartphone battery. Regardless, this game is fun with either a touchscreen on your phone or on a full size gaming desktop with a 27" monitor. The game has controller support, and its kinda fun to lounge back with a nice mixed drink and play this on the couch. Totally worth the $3, and if it goes on sale then its DEFINATELY worth it! -PR0XIDIAN

First time I played this long ago on PS2 and it was amazing. I loved .hack anime series and being able to play it as the game were just amazing. I wouldn't call it amazing by modern standards, but back then I didn't know better, I guess.
To be honest today it looks kind of bland and still unpolished. The story is great as always, but the presentation is riddled with things which wold be better left back there in the past like absurdly annoying quests which you have to do 3 times each because the game divided in 3 volumes. Yes, I do understand that the game were released in 3 volumes back there due to DVD size limitations, but do we really need these volumes today on the PC? Well, they did make it easier to grind these levels now, and they added option to replay the battle if you loose, which really helps once or twice in the second and third volumes when you accidentally encounter chaotic PK in the low-level location, but these changes turned volume 1 into a massive joke since you end up overleveled all the time. The balance kicks in only closer to the end of volume 2 and never on the arena. Every time I came to the arena I were 10+ levels above which means instant win. Not like I'd lose if the enemy would be 5-8 levels ahead, but no challenge at all? Seriously? That's just boring. Well, I can continue like that for a while.
Also, back then I thought it gives somewhat accurate representation of MMORPG games (minus the crazy stuff), but honestly if you somehow haven't played MMOs yet then don't take this as a reference. MMOs are inherently unfair. ;) However, it still have a great atmosphere with that virtual in-game forum and news site and that's what's important in the Role Playing Game. You actually feel like you live in that world.
Anyway, I DO recommend this game because even with all the downsides and weaknesses of an 11 years old game it's still great. Just don't expect fancy graphics. They did improve it a bit since PS2, but pretty much everything besides the main characters lacks details. Well, this is not a re-make after all, so I haven't expected anything, but HD textures and better models for the main characters and GUI anyway, which they did.
Now, about volume 4. It isn't really a new chapter in the story, however it addresses a few loose ends in it and grants main character another job extension which breaks ugly-nice-fugly-nice pattern from the original 3 volumes and also nice looking and fun to play with at least for the duration of this volume. Which is really short. "I told people online about my problems. In real life, no one would care about them, but online, everyone cares. My online friends are all so nice. They worry about me, they give me advice. I just wish real life was like my life online." -Quote from an article in the game DAMN.
.Hack//G.U. has a great narrative that give reason to invest time in the game. There is more than enough cutscenes to entertain the story and develop the characters. Furthermore, the fictional forums the game provides in its internet sphere offers branching narratives and lore to the world of .Hack in game and the real world. The game was ahead of its time tackling issues relevant today about technology when it becomes too much a part of our lives not just for a solution but more so for convenience (which you would have to read in the in game forum). It also makes you feel like you are in a forum with people discussing these topics like in real people. But even if you don't read them, the narrative will allude to these things or some characters will mention them.
This series was a crazy ride from start to finish. The story was amazing with a lot of feels and unexpected twists. It starts off a little slow but quickly starts to pick up as Haseo, the main character starts to learn more and more about whats going on in "The World" and what he has to do to meet his own goals. Most of the characters Haseo meets are very likable and you get to see them grow throughout the whole series and also help Haseo grow into a better character himself. Everytime you get a new party member you add them to your friends list like you would in an actual MMO style game which lets you invite them into your party for the story, quests, dungeons, etc. You also get the ability to trade with them and give them gifts while in a party. The game does a really good job of making you feel immersed into "The World" with how it has you logging out to a desktop and back into the game as if you're the one actually playing it and having a friends list full of the characters you meet throughout the story.
The combat is pretty straightforward and simple with a one button attack but you get additional skills to execute. Additionally, you also have recovery attacks for more strategy if I may say so. It doesn't sound fun from words alone but it is when you have your hands in control of the game. Gameplay allows you to do general things you'd expect from an actual mmo like guild management, arena, improve gears questing etc.. The game isn't complex by any means. It's straightforward fun as a game should be.
Oh! And music! Music in this game is just fascinating. I even can't say anything else about it.
Overall I would definitely recommend anyone that loves RPGS and MMOs to play this amazing series because it was truly a great experience.

.hack//GU is a game that takes place between and after the anime series .hack//Roots, It is also linked to the first 4 games released on the PS2 back in 2002. This is a treat for fans and for newcomers to the series as it expands past the 3rd disk. You get all three games bundled opposed to buying them all seperately.
The Graphics are pretty dated but slightly enhanced for the HD remake, The game has it's own little charm but suffers from the common overly reused graphics syndrome.  You will find many enemy reskins and most maps are just randomlly generated with slight alterations. Despite this, it really holds up very well.  It kinda does bother me when characters are talking and the game decides to cut in for only a few seconds only to show characters doing something subtle like a hand gesture or a simple mouth movement.  I don't remember if this was the case on the PS2 version as it has been a while since I have played it.
(Spoilers here)
Story is pretty interesting, simply put you are playing a game that goes skynet and puts people all around "The World" into a comatose.(Pun intended)  This boi Tri-Edge slaps your girl's butt and you aren't about to take that and end up getting your face smacked to the floor so hard you go back to level 1.  Later on you go on to solve the mysteries of Tri-Edge and come across best girl. Eventually you save the world from a deadly MMO that was still allowed to continue running despite the cultural backlash and almost dumping a can of whoopass all over the planet.
(End Spoilers)
The soundtrack is really good, it was composed by the same person who did the previous games and you can tell  Chikayo Fukuda has only gotten better with age.
The Combat works like this,  you engage into a battle which creates a ring in which you fight enemies.   The increased fps has caused some issues from its former PS2 varient in which tap weapons require a weird timing that its almost better to just use charge attacks.  You will have access to 5 different weapons each with their own style of gameplay and each weapon can be used mid battle depending how you setup your skill triggers.  It's pretty straight forward and the game is by no means difficult if you lose in battle it's probably only because you are underleveled as enemies damage seems to stagnate to oneshot levels otherwise.
Mechanically the game gets extremely repetitive and leveling becomes ridiculously easy, I don't by any means think its a bad game.  If you are looking for a mindless game then play .hack//GU because its still quite fun.  Menus are easily navigated and there is memoir section if you forget what you need to do.  Party Members you want may not always be available due to how the story progresses.  Armor and Weapons can be rigged to insanely overpowered levels but this has always been the case since the PS2 version. You get a little mini desktop that you can decorate and play a idle mini game called Crimson VS which  plays itself as you play the game.   Lots of lore and flavortext to be found on the pretend online fourms and news of the outside world of the game located in the news section.
Is this game worth playing?  Yes, if you are a fan of the series otherwise find another game because you will probably be bored out of your mind.

This is an extremely different type of Indie Game you would find out there and it is what sets this game apart to the other indie titles you'd find out there.
The graphics and design elements gives the game, what most people refer to as, 'Medeival + Tinder' (This is actually a popular review for this game by Steam user 'Eto_' )
The game at first is entertaining due to its easy to understand mechanics which is to basically swipe left and right. The humour experienced in the game is more of a chuckle than a huge LOL moment but it is ultimately unexpected (For example you can get in love with a male artist, which i find funny considering most games don't touch on being gay and etc).
The UI is extremely fluid though and I don't see old systems having a problem running this game as it is not resource hogging.
EXTREMELY REPETITIVE. I cannot stress this enough. If you are not the kind of person to sit through and remember the hundreds of combinations in puzzle/strategy games, then this game IS NOT for you. The game presents itself greatly in the beginning but after an hour or so, it starts to show its annoying side. I would even go as far as to say its the same feeling you'd get when playing NO MANS LIE. No joke, It is a fair comparison and I'm standing by it.
Save Game problems. The issue has recently been fixed according to Devolver. I have not tested it out yet and I doubt I will. Save games may get lost and you'd be forced to restart a full timeline. I had to do it once which was EXTREMELY frustrating.
'Kingdom Status' type of system. The gameplay mechanic of having to balane out different aspects of your kingdom is a good one but after some time, you start to get REALLY annoyed by it. There are moments where it will deplete and increase so quickly that you'd be forced to make wrong decisions and result in your king dying. Nothing like an unwarranted lost.
I feel that this game has a lot of untapped potential. It should really get rid of the repetitve gameplay and make it easier on casuals like me. Maybe create a more 'casual' game mode to remedy this issue? That's only Devolver to figure out.
All in all, If you are a person who likes a casual puzzle/strategy game with minimal physical movement and not care about repetiveness, then this game is for you.
If not, I would not recommend this game unless maybe if its on a discount.

Alright, so...
You know how Ragnarok was originally 2 Dimensional, had some fun featuers, and wasn't generic and stale...?
Well, that's where Ragnarok 2 comes in.
You see, it all started when they decided to take the 2d aspect of what a good game was, and turn it 3d. The monsters and stuff were put in it, but it didn't feel like the game that we're used to.
When you first enter the game, you're pretty much following orders and quests that are outrageously linear to the games progression... I doubt anyone who plays, actually even followed the story, since it was just that bland.
The reason that Ragnarok was originally great in my opinion, was the fact that it had difficult, and a real fear factor added to it as well... Someone could walk up to you and just beat you up, field bosses roam around slaying newcomers and you were never sure if you could take on certain enemies, especially by yourself...
HOWEVER, this game massively spoon feeds you! Kill 4 of this enemy, 3 of that one, get me 2 of those... You barely have to kill or anything for any of the quests, at least early on. None of the enemies posed a threat or a challenge at all. We even took down a field boss (A giant chonchon called the "lurker fly", also from ragnarok 1, but its a regular spawn on that.) That, was probably the only battle where we almost died.
The classes in this game are unbalanced...I'm looking at you archer. I played a tank, and died in about 4 hits from an archers spammable charge shot skill... I couldn't even get over to my opponent during the battle. (Yes, this was pvp.) In PVE , archers seem to be able to 1 shot ko almost all the mobs that are the archers level, or even a little higher... which is just stupid.
Card drops ARE EXTREMELY COMMON...Like to the point of "F*** it, I don't even want to loot these bodies!
What made RO originally special as well, was the difficulty of OBTAINING A SINGLE CARD...
But here... You kill a mob, hell you might as well make the mobs drop 6 cards at once at the rate you can collect them. Hah, ridiculously easy...
The game just was way too bland, with an unneeded profession system and boring quests. No fun way to travel around and explore, and jumping was just pointless. At the end of one of the dungeons we faced, we killed the boss...didn't get anything. You would expect a dungeon to hold a chest or the boss to drop something?
