looks to provide a classic strategy based experience by making you hunt, scavenge and loot in order to stay alive. Does it hit its mark or misses with a 90% chance, let’s find out;
In Rencounter, you start out an unknown man who has to survive by gathering various resources and fighting other people and wildlife. Initially, it reminded me of Dungeon of the endless, a superb game where you had to open different rooms to see what was inside. Rencounter tries to apply the same mechanic, where you are shown an overview of the map to see which rooms are connected to which place and where you need to go next. The other room might be filled with supplies you drastically needed or may contain enemies you need to fight.
If there are enemies in a room, you are then shifted to a 3D overview from where the gameplay is turn based. You try to get close to the enemy and then attack him to slowly reduce his health to minimum. Here, Rencounter takes XCOM like approach. When you are close to enemy, you are given a few choices on how to hit him. There are a couple of choices like hitting him with a light or heavy attack, and which part of his body to attack. All parts of the enemy have an percentage showing the chances you have to hit him.
This also applies various effects to him, such as attacking his arm will reduce his speed and so on. There are also choices to defend yourself at the start of the turn. The defence mechanic here is actually somewhat bugged. My character was able to parry nearly all of the enemies without breaking a sweat in the early game. This made the early game very easy to run through and later on was rendered nearly useless.
You either move in a turn or attack. There is no way to move and attack in a single turn which is really bad for a game like this. Rencounter also tries to make it unfair just for the sake for it. Hunger levels go down quite rapidly and you might run through a few rooms without getting any sort of valuable loot or supplies. Combine this with the perma death of the game trying to include a roguelike feature and it makes it a lot more frustrating when your team of humans and pets die with something like this.
Not only that, there are instances where you miss a shot with 99% chance of hitting the enemy and that becomes really frustrating. I know it is not impossible to miss a shot with 99% chance but when you miss it 3 or 4 times in one session, that really makes you question if you should even go with the 90% shot. Even though the game is randomly generated, it becomes repetitive fairly quickly with many locations repeating itself over and over. Unlike a game like say, Rogue Legacy, where you expect to see the castle over and over again, here it is supposed to be a little different.
There is not much enemy variety and the story is as minimal as it gets. But if you’re looking for a streamlined strategy RPG, rogue like with turn based combat and you are used to the frustrations of the genre, Rencounter might be good enough for you.
Visually it looks pretty meh. Rencounter tries to go for a modern look but falls apart pretty quickly. Everything from the environments to the characters models are average at best. There is a lot of darkness in most of the rooms and that causes a lot of colours to remain hidden. Nothing brightens things up here and succumbs to a game that tries to force it’s dark atmosphere down our throats. Nothing exceptional can be seen in Rencounter, all it has is a lot of darkness
Even though the soundtrack of Rencounter is average, it actually compliments the dark nature of the game pretty well. The soundtrack is ominous, always keeping the suspense of the next room intact. Every step of your character has a solid crunch to it and it lays a pretty solid foundation and works along with the tense nature Rencounter is going for. There is nothing here though which will make you come back for more, just like the rest of the game.
Rencounter tries to do some really neat things for a turn based strategy game, but none of them come together at any given instance. The visuals, enemy and level design are all pretty bland and there is a certain ring of repetitiveness here. But if you like games like this where you are punished and sometimes is blatantly unfair, you might give this one a try. Rencounter is also suitably priced at 5.99$ which won’t be too hard on your wallet.

Some of the decisions can even have more than just two choices so if Fallout 4's system irked you this shows how something even simpler can still offer a variety of meaningful choices.
While I unfortunately don't have too much to say on the game, I full-heartedly recommend you at least try it. Hardcore survival at it's best. Frustrating and unforgiving , just as it should be. The developers put a lot of effort in to this game and have an eye for detail. Just consider this is all work in progress.
Pro's
- A real zombie apocalypse, society is falling apart and you need to deal with it.
- Realistic survival. You need water, food , shelter , sleep. You can get diseases , bone fractures, panic attacks and much more. Can't sprint forever , you'll tire and need to catch a breath.
- Awesome crafting systems and methods to be self sustaining. Like farm, hunting and fishing mechanics. Once again a lot of eye for detail !
- Normal zombies , they don't look like much but at the moment you get cocky they will swarm you !
- Unforgiving gameplay, so you put 20 hours in your character and think your invincible ? Be at the wrong place at the wrong time and you'll die :)
- Great meta game mechanics. Weather effects , changing seasons , day & night cycle, zombie migration and horde forming.
Con's
- The graphics , i don't care too much for graphics but it would be great to see less pixels. Also , the game seems to lack a lot of animations. Performing actions is seeing a loading bar pop up, no animations. On the other hand this gives the game a bit of old school gaming charm. I guess it's just what you prefer.
- Character development, it seems like the game is depending too much on certain skills and talents. It's almost impossible to play without carpentry for example. It's needed to build stuff that you need end game or you'll just starve from lack of food.
- End game aspect, the survival mechanics are perfect in this game but is it enough to make you put 30 hours + in to a character ? Building , grinding and killing the same godamned zombies over and over might get boring. But then again you are supposed to die eventually, playing this game is more like : how long can you evade dying ?

The main goal of the game is to rule as long as you can. The amount of years your reign lasts is the score you get. Everytime a king dies, you control a new one and you scores goes back to zero. Each decision you make is a year so this means that the more cards you go through (each interacting with different characters) the higher your score will be.
On one hand it feels like an arcade because you want to make the highest score possible but on the other hand it doesn't make you want to play just to beat your previous score. The cards have a wide variety and all of them are unique. It makes you want to keep playing because you want to try something new that might be in the next card you pull up. It could be the devil talking to you or maybe a werewolf at your doorstep. Maybe you want some magic mushrooms or a lover?
What I'm saying is, this game is more complex than some games being sold at 60€ (not all of them of course, but just take a look at EA for example) and it costs only 3€. It's really cheap for what it brings to players and if you do end up getting bored after playing for 1 hour you can always refund it.
So... what are you waiting for to purchase it?

Bold and realistic gem.  So glad I found this game.
The Long Dark is a first-person sandbox about solo survival in extreme condions.  Every other human in the game world is dead, and for yourself it is very difficult to effect sustained survival, especially at higher difficulties.  But you do get better.
I say YOU, because what I like most about this game is that the player must learn and get better to succeed.  Kind of reminds you of, i don't know, that golden time when games took a fair measure of skill to beat.  Instead of a linear story with pre-planned power ups, instead of just a character leveling up to being practically untouchable, the player must learn to balance protection from the elements, water, food, and stamina, and keep respecting that balance for the entire game.  It doesn't matter how good you get at it, the world can still kill you at any time.  The game is VERY, VERY immersive.   It really gives the illusion that you inhabit your avatar's body and are truggling to survive.
For example, you might get attacked by a wolf before you have good weaponry, get the better of the wolf with your hunting knife, then you are chasing it down like a madman, following its blood trail, hoping it will bleed out where you can find it because you know this might be your first chance at meat and having a half-full belly in hours of gameplay.  You lliterally begin to think, feel, and act like you are some starving man in the woods, never mind all that lasagna you just ate!
You might get lost in a blizzard and end up going in circles because you can't see 10 feet.  You just went out for firewood, but now you're lost in a blizzard!  You might find you are in an unsustainable location, realize a slow death is only a matter of time, head out in the middle of the night, go on some crazy multi-hour odyssey, and fist pump/air guitar when you at last stumble on some hunting cabin frozen, starving, with injuries and 5% of your health.
This game is well worth your time and you will end up making time for this game, trust me.  Shout out to the developers on such an outstanding product;  a true work of art.

I cannot in good faith recommend Superhot to anyone. I enjoyed the combat and it has the potential to be much more than it is, but sadly gets let down by the most atrocious narrative I've seen in years.
At the beginning of each level, the player is thrust into a high stakes environment in which they're outmanned and outgunned, with their sole objective being to be the last man standing. Time only moves when you move, leaving you in a near perpetual state of slow motion to consider your moves and search for opportunities.
That part of the game is very good and in a perfect world, the developers would have made a large number of levels and Steam Workshop support.
What they actually did was crudely attempt to shoehorn in a terrible plot that only serves to pad out the time spent playing. The story revolves around you sitting at an early 90's themed PC, being sent updated builds of a game from your friend which you then proceed to play. Plot twist, theres something sinister happening and you may be getting mind controlled and/or going insane. You may also just be really high on some hallucinagenic. The game never tells you what's actually happening so for all I know, the entirity of the game exists inside the lucid dream of a hamster. Your guess is as good as mine.
Almost everyone I know who played Superhot was able to complete the game in less than 2 hours. If the game is ever on sale for lower than about £3 then I'd recommend at least giving it a try because the combat IS fun, don't get me mistaken, I really did enjoy the frantic scrambling around each level for survival, but we needed MUCH more of it.

Let me start off by saying that if you haven't played or at least heard of Bio Shock by now you have been living under a rock. It's one of the best games ever and THE best game of the 7th generation. This came came out about ten years ago when I was a freshman in high school. I hated high school but I loved staying home "sick" to play this game. At the time I happened to be reading a really cool book called Atlas Shrugged, I didn't know this at the time but Bioshock is actually a critique of that book. I finished the game and the book around the same time and my mind was blown. It changed the way I have thought about and looked at things, drastically. There are so many under lying factors and metaphors that make this game great, instead of blowing the secret I urge you to find out for yourself. You don't have to pick up Atlas Shrugged to understand this game, but I would reccomend you do it just to get the experience, right, i guess is the best word.. That's my opinion on the game. Now let's get to the gameplay. Firstly, we are very lucky to now have this game in 1080p on PC. The xbox 360 version, if you can still find a copy is in 720p I believe, which was more or less the standard in 2006. This game is very story drive and atmospheric, so the graphics are important. They do this very right. You really feel like you are in Rapture especially when you have the graphics maxed out. This game still looks good compared to some triple A titles of today. The gameplay itself can get repetitive. That is why you need to immerse yourself in to the story and truly think about the things that are going on, get involved in what you are doing on a mental level. This IS a game to relax to, physically, not mentally. Personally I think the vita chambers suck. This isn't really a spoiler, but death is not punished in this game at all. You come back to life, usually very close to where you died with all your equipment in tact. I think this game COULD have been a good rogue like, but the devs didnt see or pursue that possibility but fans of rogue likes will get what I'm saying. The weapons are cool and fun to use but there is only one of each. One shotgun, one machine gun, one pistol, etc. Variety comes in Plasmids and Gene/Combat tonics. There is no multiplayer in this game. IF you want a challenge, play it on hard. If you are here for the story, play on medium. Youll get everything out of the game and finish the story in a reasonable time without being frusturated or underwhelmed if you play on medium. This game is a lot like a roller coaster, or sex.. The build up and the ride itself are great but the ending leaves you unfufilled and wanting to go again. Still, not many 7th gen games can top this one, unless you count Skyrim.

Played this series a bunch when I was younger, so when I saw this one on sale I jumped at the chance to relive some childhood memories, but what I actually experienced was something that surprised me quite a bit. I didn't enjoy it all that much. The game's atmosphere is absolutely incredible, and honestly I could recommend the game for just that. It's incredibly immersive and intense, and the characters are freaky and fitting, however, this doesn't make up for the games flaws. Combat in this game feels way too kite oriented. You just kite your enemies into traps, or divert their attention somewhere else and hit them 20 times in the back with your trusty wrench 'til they drop. I would have prefered a combat system that was fitting for the mysterious, gripping setting. This combat system makes the game feel as if it was geared towards younger players, with little comprehension for actual strategy. Now, to talk about the last third of the game, especially the ending..... No spoilers ahead, I'll keep it vague, don't worry. The first 2/3 of the game is gripping and fantastic, but there's a certain moment that makes your heart drop and feels like the absolute climax of the story, and I almost wish the game had just ended there. I rarely want games to be shorter than they are, and this one is already relatively short as it stands, but the last third of the game tried to introduce new mechanics and it just didn't work. That part of the game felt boring. It felt like a chore to complete, which is usually when I just put the game down and never pick it back up. I play videogames for fun, and the ENDING of the game, instead of being something epic, was just flat boring. The final boss fight was... ambitious, if you want to be generous, but was way too cliche. The mechanics ave all been done before, nothing new there, and the boss himself is unrecognizable. It didn't feel like I was fighting the antagonist that I had travelled so far to fight. It felt too easy, too simple, too boring. I wasn't engaged throughout that entire part of the story, which made me sad. Overall, this is a fantastic game that has an unfortunate ending :( I still recommend it highly simply for the unique ideas portrayed, the environment, and the characters you associate with, but don't expect much towards the end.

I followed the development of this game back from its Kickstarter campaign, and despite all the fanfarre it got, all I can say is that it was a letdown.
The gameplay in itself is somewhat enjoyable, if limited. Group battles are of a light tactical nature and play decently, but mecha battles are basically just contrived sequences of dice rolls.
There is some fun to be had in customizing your studio, Rangers and their equipment, but it all feels unbalanced, in such a way that there is just "one true way" of doing things, while the rest is filler.
The main issue, though, is the plot and flow of the game... or lack thereof. The story is rife with jokes that read like internal jokes of the dev team or obscure references. It's not even a cultural barrier deal, because even playing on the native language of the studio, the text just felt confusing, weak and generic.
That is compounded by the fact that every other mission counts with "support members" who contributed to the campaign. In summary, they are all dudes who are pretty much alike and have to make an introductory speech stating who they are, what they do, etc. and then be awesome. It gets annoying fast.
It's not that it's so bad that it shouldn't be played, but really, with so many other options out there, why bother?

Some games, as with cooking, follow a recipe. The System Shock series prepared a great dish; BioShock took that formula, substituted a few ingredients, and presented a game worthy of being a System Shock successor. BioShock is not only visually appealing, is jam-packed with sweat drenched palms on the pants audio, but also with a great story that unfolds as you frantically meander throughout Rapture.
Being violently thrown into the game, you are left with no choice other than to go down the rabbit hole, to enter this submerged version of Wonderland; a place that is as dangerous as it is curious. You are informally greeted by a denizen of Rapture, although they do not appear to be a friendly
. Much like SS2, you are immediately put on the offensive, and will remain that way for the rest of the game.
The inhabitants of Rapture are fighting a guerilla war. They know the terrain, have the weapons, and their leaders will stop at nothing to win. You will pick up weapons and skills along the way that will prepare you for the fight ahead. Being that Rapture is located many leagues under the sea, there will be no fresh supplies, no reinforcements, you'll be lucky to even find a way out of this madhouse. You have to learn to fight fire with fire, in some cases quite literally.
Cut to Sam using Incinerate! Sam begins to seize and falls unconscious. A few seconds later Sam wakes up, looks wildly around, and then looks at Billy in a maniacal manner. Sam then lifts his arm, points a finger at Billy, and we see Billy burst into flames. In the foreground Billy collapses to the floor, writhing and screaming, while in the background Sam is walking away and whistling.
Are there any allies here?
Sometimes it is hard to tell them apart. There are several enemy classes here, many of which require specialized ammo or attacks to kill. Life at the bottom of the briny sea and habitual overuse of ADAM has driven some of the more unique characters mad in a way that is both charming as it is horrifying. And some decisions in the game are of a moral nature, almost allowing you to descend into a madness of your own.
The levels make full use of limited lighting, which seems only fitting given the nature of a derelict city at the bottom of the ocean. Sometimes you cannot tell if someone is lurking in the shadows or if even the shadows are a true representation of what you think you see. The audio is phenomenal; whether it is voices echoing throughout the corridors, the overhead
or the sound of metal on metal as an enemy approaches, dragging something behind them.
Other great carryovers from SS2 include:

Game is extremely fun (especially the space combat. Sweet God, the space combat). I played .hack//Infection and the rest of the original series when I was younger, but somehow had never heard of the .hack//G.U. series until recently. So I was ecstatic when it came to Steam and I could finally give it a shot. Unfortunately, I don't think it is an improvement in any way over the original IMOQ series.
I cannot recommend this game to anyone who hasn't already played any other .hacks and enjoyed them enough to want to continue to build upon the story and atmosphere in the .hack universe.
The combat has taken an enormous step back with it now being battles that are sectioned off and cannot be escaped without an item. Not only that, but it's almost always a group of 3 enemies, or a single "hard" enemy that gets quite repetitive.
Areas have also changed for the worse. Instead of having open fields to run in with a dungeon somewhere within each landscape, now everything has a dungeon-like layout to it that has very little variation.
Data drain is now a very tedious mini-game that you are forced to play which always, every single time throughout the entire series, starts off without a brief tutorial message. It's really disheartening to think your audience is so incapable of performing a task you've forced them into doing 30+ times by the end of the series, and still think they don't know how to attack and dodge.
A new resource has been added to the game, probably to make up for lack of grunties and hunting for grunty food called Chim Chims. These creatures serve absolutely no purpose but to make you wait to progress. In order to collect chims, there are various ways to get them, but the most common is sitting next to a switch and waiting for some to come out and flipping the switch to knock them off tracks. These are always included next to the doors that Chim Chims open, so I cannot see any purpose they serve but to inhibit progress.
This game's narrative really tasks you with suspending your disbelief pretty early on, but by the 3rd game I felt so unimmersed by how high stakes the game becomes with seemingly no reason other than to "go bigger". The story trips upon itself multiple times by the very end by plotholes and how frequently the game moves it's own goalpost.
The addition of a new episode, Reconnection (vol. 4), is the most redeeming thing about Last Recode. Its story tones it down and makes it personal again. The cutscenes use a more traditional anime style that is absolutely gorgeous. The game has a good amount of closure that vol. 3 didn't really provide in the original G.U. trilogy.
I can really only recommend this game to anyone who played the G.U. trilogy, but not the additional episode Reconnection, even on a sale.
Here's to hoping they remaster the Infection/Mutation/Outbreak/Quarantine series.

Nostalgia trip from a decade passed, Last Recode reminds us of al lthe things good and ill of PS2 era JRPGs. Entirely too long cutscenes, strange plot pacing, obscenely huge monsters with questional shapes.
Over 4 games you'll get to toy with 5 different types of weapons. One thing Last recode absoutely nails is making each weapon feel different. THe dual swords feel fast and fluid, chaining huge combos with satisfying speed. THe broadsword feels like you're hitting someone with a truck. Somehow, the .//hack team made scythe combat interesting. Wide, sweeping arc attacks make you feel like a true grim reaper. And Dual guns let you chain combos and juggle enemies in mid air as only a JRPG could think to try.
The short but welcome new addition of Volume 4 creates this weird chain sword which behaves like nothing I've ever seen. But it also feels satisfying to use.
Like I said in the intro, the pacing is garbage. In volume 1, you hit a grind that just doesn't seem to stop, then you end the grind, kill 2 bosses, and the volume is done. Volume 3 feels short, and volume 4 IS short. Characters don't always act like reasonable people. Or act their age (seriously, Sakaki is supposed to be 12. Haseo is supposed to be 17. Ovan is supposed to be 25. Yata is supposed to be about 15.) Atoli's voice acting is shrill. Gaspard's voice is infamous among the .//hack fans. the native japanese voice acting is here, if you can't get over the English voices.
Overall, as a package, you're going to get over 100 hours of content. If you're a completionist, most likely 110 to 120. It's not my favorite .//hack story, but this is a good starting pint if you are new to the series.

You can't seem to talk about this game without talking about DLC, understandibly so. Before I get into this review I will state that while I like the core concept of DLC it has been poorly implemented into games in the past few years, this game is no different.
TL;DR- At it's best, this game is a blaze of glory and fun that maybe even rivals L4D's co op central idea. At it's worst though...It is a drab and has tedious stretches of nothing happening. This game went SUPER aggressive on the DLC front and while the dlc is currently harmless considering it's simply skins(Which are usually made AFTER the game is done and is waiting to be shipped, and the artists need something to do. A fact that many people forget)  It is just ♥♥♥♥ing stupid for the monsters to be priced at 15$ a pop, and hunters 7.50$ a pop. Buy this if it is on sale for sure, it really is worth 30$ to maybe even 35$ 60$ is just too hard to swallow. ♥♥♥♥ing great with friends, poor with solo.
Story (5/10)
Chaos! A planet named Shear has become overrun with giant monsters and it is up to 12(currently) of the galaxies best hunters to help evacuate the planet of it's colonist. Nothing special here, no real plot really just a few back stories on each of the characters. Much like L4D and L4D2 in fact, only in those games there were writings on the wall and many conversations between the survivors to make the story seem fleshed out. This game lacks many of those boosters.
Graphics (No rating)
The game looks good, then again it is not hard to make a game look good anymore, you have to TRY to make a game look bad now.
Gameplay (7/10)
It's fun! Mostly anyway. You can either play as one of the 12 hunters which divide up into 4 classes(3 per role) Trapper, who aptly traps the monster. Medic, who you know, heals the team, assault who does the most damage to the monster or the support who can do a multitude of things such as shield allies or bomb the living♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the monster with an orbital strike. Then there is also the famed monster role, you can either be the severely underpowered goliath who breathes fire and can't run away for♥♥♥♥♥♥ The kraken, who reigns death from above while looking like the president of the Cthulu fan club. He seems to be the most balanced of the 3 monsters. Or the wraith, who will supernova your♥♥♥♥♥into next week. Below i will go into each class and monster in a bit more detail.
Assault- As stated above, the main damage dealer of the group is this guy, He has a personal shield when he gets up close and personal and can very from having a gun that shoot lighting to a flamethrower. This class is pretty fun to play and as for the people who complain that they can't use the mines on the kraken, that is why you have Val Abe or Griffin, your team must be well prepared for ANYTHING.
Trapper- My personal favorite class. This class can use harpoons or stasis grenades to impedes the monsters movement, they can bring down the thunderdome where the monster is forced to fight, and use medium damaging guns. The class is pretty well balanced and feels the newest out of all the class types.
Support- I honestly don't know how to describe this class because they do all sorts of♥♥♥♥♥♥and feel like the most versatile of the group. The class is okay i suppose. Hank's beard is magnificent.
Medic- Do I really need to explain in detail what a medic does? THEY HEAL♥♥♥♥♥♥ Minus Laz who just watches his team die so he can res spam.
Goliath- Really underpowered, this monster is meant to be the "brawler" of the bunch but I always found myself getting stomped. Where the other two monsters can run away at stage 1 this guy CAN'T get away due to his slow movement. Stage 2 tends to solve this somewhat. His whole moveset should be able to do more damage, NONE of his moves feel like they pack a punch. This is a shame that even at level 3 he doesn't feel powerful because if they patched him he would probably be the funnest.
Kraken- My personal favorite. Certainly the most balanced of the bunch, between have mostly skillshot abillities that have good payoffs and the flying abillity he is certainly the most refreshing of the bunch
Wraith- SUPERNOVA ALL DAY EVERY DAY. Seriously though, after the post beta patch the wraith feels much more balanced and feels like a hit and run character now, they still have not justified taking abduction though. It just simply isn't as potent as decoy supernova and warp blast.
Oh wait, there are game modes too. Yea it's basic 4v1 and variations of 4v1.  Evacutaion adds refreshing things with map effects that depends on who wins.  It's fun but it will get stale fast unless they add some more FREE content.
DLC ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T- there is something like 100$ worth of dlc already. ALREADY. Now while 95% of it is skins there is no way to unlock the skins in game which is kinda bull. there is also the 7.50$ per new hunter and the absolutely ludicrous pricing of 15$ for a single monster. 2K NEEDS to lower the pricing. Now one nice thing though is that even if you don't buy the monsters or hunters you can still fight them just not play as them. All maps and game modes will be free which is nice to.
Why the game will die in a few weeks- Simple, mod support. The main reason(or one of them) why L4D is still kicking around today is because of the insane mod support for the games and how much they freshing it up even with them being 5 years or older. This game has very few reviews, so i'll post a quickie.
Recounter a spin on the dungeon crawler genre. It's currently in early development (and it shows), but shows a lot of promise and is already fun to play. The general gameplay is divided into three parts: exploration, combat and character management.
Unlike most dungeon crawlers, you don't just walk around with your character peeking around corners. If you're not currently fighting, you're presented with a simple map showing a series of connected rooms. You move by clicking the neighbouring tiles, which in turn reveals more rooms. If there's something worthwhile in a room, you'll have to fight for it. This could be items, allies, shops, healing, food, to name a few. Moving around the map eats up your Hunger stat - more on that in a moment.
When you decide to fight, the game jumps to a 3D view of the room you're currently in. You will see your character/s, the baddies, elements of terrain, and stuff you can later click on to loot. Combat is turn-based and takes place in a classic roguelike fashion - one action at a time. Some actions are faster, some are slower, thus quickening or delaying your next turn (think "ADoM" and energy costs). All charaters have 3 floating bars at their feet, which represent Health, Stamina and time until next turn. Each weapon has two different attacks - heavy and light - which can target specific body parts, thus inflicting various flavours of boo-boo upon your enemies (and you). The specific effects of getting hit and some other actions (like running) aren't described in the game yet, but they're there, you just have to figure that stuff out by yourself.
Character management is rather developed at this stage. You manage your Health (which keeps you alive), your Hunger (which lets you explore), and the money-thing called "Ice". If you deplete your health, you die. If your Hunger drops below a certain threshold, you suffer severe penalty to stats. Without Ice you're weak. Speaking of Ice - you gather it by killing enemies, looting stuff and disassembling items at your inventory screen. In turn, it lets you upgrade your stats and equipment. Also serves as currency when you find a shop.
Recounter is in early development. That means unfinished interface (everything is accessible and usable, just a bit clunky), little variety of content, and balance issues (i.e. I cleared the first dungeon level just fine and then I got completely massacred in the first room of the second floor). The core mechanics are there, and the game is enjoyable already, which is something notable in an early-access game. Recounter is dirt cheap, costing 6 Euro (3E on sale, currently), so if you're a fan of the genre, I suggest supporting the creator. And if you're skeptical about early access, just pay close attention to the title, it may grow into something great.

Jumpscare. The laziest, easiest way to 'scare' someone. Of course a sudden loud noise will make you jump. The creator had the power to make this game a little better by making you feel scared, but after the jumpscare, all the eeriness is gone.
Overall, I highly recommend you don't buy this game. It's terrible.

Honestly, it doesn't seem like this game came out 5 years ago. This is one of my favorite RTS's of all time, right next to AoE. The dual plane RTS mechanic is what makes this game a great balance between combat and building your empire. I have yet to replay  through the story, but I recall it being really fun and quite long (If you consider the different story lines just one campaign, it is even longer). Also, being able to refine and hone in your ground combat skills in the skirmish mode is very helpful, since you don't have to initiate an extensive galactic conquest match. Since I don't want to have a wall of text, nor feel like making an in depth review, just buy this game. Here is a synopsis of why you should:
+ Star Wars
+ Really great space battles
+ Fun ground battles
+Great sounds and sound track
+ A good learning curve; this game can appeal to casual gamers as well as hardend RTS players. It just depends on how much time you want to put into the game, and if you want a challenge (the CPU opponents can get pretty feisty lol)
+ A plethora of units from the entire Star Wars galaxy
+ The cinematic view is cool
+ Space battles in particular are super fun to just sit back and watch. Something about them lasers...
Really the only con(s) would be
- Price. But the game gives you so much content for a fraction of the cost of a big name companies would charge. That said, I'd suggest getting it on sale if you still have reservations about buying it
- Graphics. The game is 5 years old, what do you expect? Even so, it really isn't that bad maxed out, it actually looks quite good for its age!
All in all, great game. I have yet to find anything bad/wrong about the game. 10/10
EDIT:
I've since played throught the campaign, and its really fun. Not necessarily note worthy story telling, and there isn't much of a plot, but I still found it entertaining to play through. It isn't as long as I recalled, being that it took me ~5hrs and I was purposely taking my time.

The concept of the game itself is brilliant. You crash land into an island inhabited by cannibals, and you(along with anyone else you are playing Co-Op with) are the only survivors. You need to forage the land, gather resources so that you can build up a base and craft tools, while avoiding the cannibals. The cannibals themselves are superhuman mutants capable of finishing you off very fast, and they usually travel in groups, so its best to avoid them until you are well equipped. The atmosphere in this game is brilliant, the forest itself looks gorgeous, and the sound effects are spot on. It is a game where you can marvel at the beauty of a particular spot at daytime, and be terrified at the exact same spot at night when its pitch dark and you can hear cannibals nearby.
My only complain is the lighting effects get a bit too dark during night which makes it almost impossible to see, whereas realistically the moonlight should be sufficient to be able to see to some extent. After a point you venture into caves to find even better loot, and unravel the story further. Overall it is a pretty well done survival experience, and I would recommend you give it a try.

If I'm being honest I'm not sure it has one, or it was hidden, or deliberately ambiguous, or I'm an idiot. I believe you play a small boy who has died in real life and wake up in this world that is not quite alive but not quite dead. Much of the game is about using your brain to traverse the environment around you.
My hypothesis is that the boy is neither entirely dead or entirely alive, which is supported by the fact that no matter what you do in the game, the boy dying inside this world just resets you to where you were. The very dark tone of the game and monochrome palette give the world a feeling that everything here is stuck with you, that the gray is the in between you must traverse.
As I've said, it's about traversing the environment, often through leaps of faith, and deliberate death by trial and error. The game is a test, and like all tests of skill and will, it gets harder as you go, and this game is no exception. Often I found myself frustrated, but only three times did I need a break after too much failure.
This is not a game you can play through one time without dying, I'm not saying its impossible, but highly improbable considering the timing, and luck required in many parts of the game. And although this game is about puzzles, often timing is more crucial a skill than simply solving what is in front of you. As someone who does well with puzzles, adding the function of timing into it, made a few parts quite difficult, but in the end, I passed the test around the 4 hours and 30-minute mark.
I believe honestly, if you do not like puzzles or timing skill checks, this game is not for you, it will anger and frustrate you. But then there is the fact that it's a beautifully crafted look into simple mechanics, and an idea, and the ability to make that successful, because for all intents and purposes this game delivers, where others do not.
The game is meant to be played with a controller, and it feels both natural and simplistic. This could have easily been a game that existed in a time when most games had only a few buttons because there are only two things here you can do. You can jump, and you can do an action, thus only two buttons are required. However, it's important to realize that you can achieve a lot with only two buttons, and despite the infuriating necessity for most modern games to support a full keyboard of buttons, this is how games should be.
There were no issues with the use of the two available button options, although timing being necessary, often you could, for example, jump off something, and miss something else and think your button press missed, but more likely was your brain and your fingers need to communicate better, it's not an issue with the game.
Thanks either to its simplicity, or design, I encountered no issues whatsoever, it ran perfectly for me.
I had this game in my library for a while, in my backlog of games, but recently purchased Inside by the same company, and so I wanted to try this game out first. I had no idea what to expect going in, and thus found myself pleasantly surprised by what I played. Everything about this game I loved, even when I found myself frustrated--and that is truly the test of what makes a good game, because I paused it, and went back at it until I got it--it was a marvelous perplexing spark of genius in a deliberately, dull, monochromatic world, thriving despite its subject matter.
In the end, that final moment of triumph gave way to a sad and cryptic, ambiguous end to my journey. Despite wanting more, and feeling like I may have missed something, I feel full, like after a thanksgiving dinner with family, I want to rest.
This game was fantastic, and truly a lot of fun, despite some frustrating situations, the triumph felt in salvation upon defeating a terribly difficult section made it all worth it. It's puzzling, it's cold monochromatic palette, its gorgeous soundtrack, and the simple look and feel of this game all make it a successful endeavor.
For people that enjoy puzzle games, this is easily a 10/10. However, if you are someone easily frustrated to the point of anger, skip this entirely. If you are somewhere in between, I think you will still enjoy it, around an 8/10 for you.

I originally played these games on the PS2, so I knew what I was getting in terms of story and gameplay from this title. My biggest concern when buying this was the PC port. It being a PS2 Era, it should not be that hard to update it and make it run better. But at the same time, the port could be handled poorly and run like crap.
I am here to report that the port of the game is functional, smooth, and feels amazing to play. That is Mainly what I based my recommend on. Of course, if you haven’t played a .hack game or even know the .hack series, I’ll fill you in on this extensive review.
.hack takes place in a pretty unique setting in a faux MMORPG game ‘The World’ which has been affected by internet phenomena out of bounds of the current game. The story of this game takes place after the events of an anime called .hack Roots. There a references to characters from that anime that appear in this game that you would have no context for if you didn’t watch the anime. This may bug some people. The game does a good enough job of explaining the events prior to the game through cutscenes referencing the main characters. There are also some tidbits and references through forum posts. There should be enough here to get the story without watching Roots, but the presence of some unexplained relationships can be off putting.
You follow a character by the name of Haseo, who is essentially your rpg edgelord. You start the story with essentially the very beginning of the.hack Roots anime. Two characters approach you with the pretense of teaching you the game. Then essentially comes the Tutorial, then the beginning of a big cutscene reel. The two characters that invited you are Player Killers (PKers) and do what they do best to you. While bullying you, the two get owned by the BEST character in the game. After that and the whole cutscene spiel, you essentially start again, and follow Haseo on his misadventure of gaining power, learning of the special characters called Epitath Users, and battling a virus hitting the world called AIDA.
The story doesn’t really start taking off until Volume 2. But there is still enough in Volume 1, if maybe with not as many big plot points and crazy happenings that follow the world. The Characters you encounter along the way are all pretty likable, with perhaps the exception of the main character at least through most of Volume 1. Point is, the story is good, but there are little rivets here and there that can make it a little bit slow or cringy. Stick with it though, because Volume 2 on gets considerably better.
The loop of gameplay here is essentially, go read email, go do task in email, and then log out, and read email again. The loop is broken up often through world building like reading forum posts, doing optional quests, and playing special campaigns through the game that are offered. You may also break up the loop by going to grind. This is a pretty level driven game, equipment and levels can really make or break you sometimes.
Speaking of that, the game can either be easy if you use all the systems the game has in place or challenging if you do not. It is not impossible to beat the game without using everything, but being well prepared will always lend an easier time. Upgrading your and your party members equipment will show favorable results. Not doing that you may find yourself lacking some firepower. That said, there are a ton of party members in this game, so keeping them all updated is a bit hard. Pick your favorites and keep them fleshed out while the rest kinda just are there.
Combat in this game is simple but very fun. You have a basic combo, with a finisher depending on the weapon equipped. You have a charge attack. You have 4 skill slots you can easily activate, and you can also cast some magic skills if you want. You have access to more weapons the further you go in, with one per volume. There is also the Avatar Battles, which are nice break from the normal combat. You have a shot, a slash, and a dash and the battles all have some unique attacks and patterns to watch for. Really, this is probably the strongest part of the game for me.
60FPS smooth through most of the game, with some slowdowns with particularly particle heavy things, like awakenings, and some scenes. Though they also are a bit to conveniently placed and it almost feels like cinematic effect. Outside of that, it's silky smooth and fast to play. It feels really good.
Looks can be spotty, Textures and models are updated, but textures still look a little icky up close. Not only that, but there is an awful lot of texture clipping, especially with character models and different floor looks. I’ll often seen little jittery black likes of pixels in scenes as someone's foot clips through their cape or their hand through their armor. It doesn’t look ‘bad’ but it is a place that could have been improved to look even better.
All the little extras and improvements that come with this game are nice. Ability to use items consecutively outside of combat. Faster leveling and weapon leveling. Faster paced battles with your higher damage output. It just makes the game all the better with all these little improvements. They did this in game, where in Volume 2 there were lots of changes that just made the game better present from the very get go.
All these little things make the game worth buying, it is 4 games in 1, with good improvements and additions that just polish it up a little. There are certainly some things I would have liked changed (like the requirements for the campaigns and book of 1000 are still really high) but it is overall a nice touch here and there.
To wrap it up
This game is fairly priced for what it is. If you played these games and want to relive them, this is the best way to do it now. If you are new to .Hack, you may be lost, but I think the game stands well enough on its own. If you are not a fan of RPGS driven by story, avoid this. This hits a very small niche of people, and this is a very japanese game. But my final verdict is Recommend.

That's going to be the general gist of my review of Metin2. I know it's going to bring cries that I'm just shilling for Game Forge or that I'm some rabid fanboy on the defensive, clutching desperately at straws in an attempt to excuse otherwise inexcusable faults in Metin2... but really? Mostly Negative? If you're interested in Metin2, I urge you to take a few moments to read this before deciding to avoid the game yourself because of the negative reviews.
I don't think it really needs repeating, but I'll give a brief overview on the points that I think have been covered well in other reviews already left here on Steam:
Gamplay is incredibly fun, the combat system mixing the simplicity of spectacle fighters with the complexity of traditional fighting games. The spacebar attack is an awesome idea that every game should adopt, much better than jumping.
At launch, some characters (Warrior, Sura, Ninja) were rather lacking and difficult to contend against while others (Shaman, Lykan) had some insane balance issues that made them outright broken and frustrating to fight against. While several of those issues have been taken care of, there are still some balance concerns in the game.

I absolutely loved and played the .Hack GU trilogy to death. I played it tons on my PS2. I'd already played it so much that I could recite entire scenes without paying attention to it. I no longer had a PS2 and had one of the early PS3s that actually had backwards compatibility, but mine was one of those that needed updates first before a new PS2 game could be played, so when Redemption came out I actually had to wait a while before I could play it. I could list many faults with these games, but even despite those flaws, I would still rate them really highly, at least a 9/10.
But I can't really say the same about the remaster. It's still the fun game series, and the games themselves havn't changed much, but while the remaster has introduced some great changes, it also introduces some negatives as well. There are more than enough reviews that gush about the remaster, but I want to note it's downsides. Even with the things I dislike about this master in mind, I still recommend this game though, especially if you were already a fan.
Also, I have not reached Vol. 4 yet. Just to let you guys know, but it should be irrelevant as my issues are with general changes to all of these games, and not really the story as that was left unchanged. Basically this review is not about the game itself, but the remaster.
I'm not one to garner interest by saving my most important point for last, it's going to be my first point, and that is the difficulty. In this remaster, they made it easier by giving you more EXP, and having you deal more damage, along with a bit of a faster combat speed. When I initially heard of these changes, I already didn't like them, but thought they were just tiny details I could just shrug off, not realizing how big they actually change things. It's much easier, even with the original game's lax difficulty in mind. You'll already feel like you're overleveled by just doing the main quests, but if you decide to go do some side quests, or even just some random field hopping, you're going to make the game way too easy. In the old games it was either too difficult because you were underleveled, or too easy because you grinded, but here you are not given that choice, it's just too easy. This leads to battles not being nearly as satisfying, and that's my biggest problem with this.
With the enhanced EXP and enhanced damage comes another issue, and that is GP, the game's currency. Unlike EXP, the amount you get was untouched. If you want to get some GP by fighting some battles, you're going to become easily overleveled, meaning to get GP you're forced to use methods that don't involve gaining EXP. This is less of an important note as the easiest and best ways to gain GP were not by battles, but it's still enough for me to consider it a negative.
The graphics are definitely improved, but it to me is both a negative and a positive. It definitely looks nicer, that's a good thing, the problem is the animation. In just normal cutscenes, the characters mouths don't move. It's not really anyone's fault, this was a PS2 game, but having graphics that are far more than the PS2's graphics actually really makes you notice this small nitpick of a detail to the point where it's actually kind of jarring.
Many remasters try to just bring an old series up to today's standards with enhanced graphics and quality of life upgrades while trying it's best to keep the original game's experience as close as possible, but this remaster is less like those remasters. It isn't really here to preserve the experience you had with the original trilogy, but is more here to just introduce new players into the series, while also giving old and new players alike a new 4th game. There's nothing inherently wrong with this at all, it's just something worth noting to temper expectations for those that wanted to experience Vol. 1 through 3 like they did from the PS2 era while getting some updates to bring it up to more modern standards.
These are the issues I found with the remaster. Not to say there are no positives, in fact if the remasters were actually bad, I wouldn't actually put this as a recommended title. There are far more than enough forum posts and reviews talking about why this game is worth it, while I felt like there weren't enough talking about the issues with this.
I know some of you are going to be baffled at this, a review that basically talks about all the negatives and skips all the positives of a game, while at the same time telling you that I do in fact recommend this game, and that's completely rational, in fact it'd be weirder if you weren't wondering why. This review isn't here to deter anyone from buying the game, in fact it isn't even here to convince people to buy it, the reason why I made this was because I want people to temper expectations when it comes to this remaster.
TL;DR original Trilogy's difficulty changes affect more than you initially think it will. If you want a pristine, but slightly updated experience with Volumes 1 through 3 before you move on to the new Volume 4, then you might be a tiny bit disappointed. Also, this review was merely me wanting to note some negatives, I still recommend the game if you're a fan, please don't hate me, I'm really sensitive

What a haunting, melancholy experience...
To me, this is the type of game that helps define video games as art.
In the simplest of terms, Limbo is a platforming puzzle game. Moving ever forward, the player is confronted with puzzle after puzzle, some requiring pure reflex and careful jumping, others requiring a more thoughtful approach. Regardless of whether the player is manipulating objects in the environment or simply dodging lethal terrain, the difficulty in Limbo feels organic and fair. There are moments that are more challenging than others, but having just finished it, I can say that all of the puzzles have a simple solution.
But it's so much more than just the puzzles that Limbo has to offer. It's in its very name: Limbo. A space between reality and dream. A stasis between life and death. In its hazy monochromatic fog, Limbo leads the player through surreal and nightmarish landscapes. Why? Piecing together and creating the story for ones self is what makes Limbo so enthralling, at least to me. Very little is given, and for a generation of games that spoon-feed their players and hold them by the hand, the stark ambiguity of Limbo is absolutely refreshing.
I won't share my interpretations of the story/ending. In some ways, I feel that it's all very obvious, as long as you're observant.
In the end, do I recommend Limbo? Yes. If your taste is bombastic colors and sound, however, you'll find yourself disappointed. For anyone else interested in a title that encourages you to think: this is your game.

I've played Ragnarok Online 2 for over two hundred hours.
That probably says something about my lack of a social life more than the game, but whatever.
It's not a terrible game. I won't say it's the worst one out there. I enjoyed it - to a point. Overall, I'd give it a passing grade of 6/10, but if there was a 50/50 recommend option I'd definitely select it.
The pros:
Free. That's the biggy. You can easily play it and wipe it off your hardrive without regrets if necessary.
Had a great time as an assassin. DPS is the way to go; tank and healer classes have much less fun in RO2.
Lots of class diversity, something inherited from RO1.
Lots of dungeons if you actually have friends or manage to join a guild.
The cons:
Hah! Like you can join a guild! Hardly anyone plays, so you end up waiting for randoms half the time or, if you're not masochistic, skipping the dungeons altogether. Without dungeons there are massive holes in both the plot and your equipment list.
Class diversity is cool to a point. RO2 isn't forgiving when it comes to min/maxing mistakes; you often have to buy reset scrolls. This leads to cookie cutter characters and people afraid to go off the path.
The grind is real! Good god I had a terrible time of it, and I was DPS! For example, a quest in Izlude. This was to kill 25 mermen soldiers, then 25 mermen warriors. Immediately afterwards, you get a quest to kill 25 slightly different mermen soldiers and 25 slightly different mermen warriors. After that, you get an optional quest to kill fifty more mermen, except these are merwoman! My loathing for this scenario led me to come back with a fire magician. I nuked the whole fishy place. If you don't do it with friends, you're stuck slowly killing entire hordes alone. Hopefully you brought potions, or every three enemies you'll be stopping to eat.
Premium items. Premium mounts. Ugh. I see people walk by with their five dollar peco peco and I want to facepalm.
The walking is worse than the grinding. At least with the grinding we can watch the flashy animations. The mounts help slightly, but the flying outposts are few and far between, plus they aren't marked very well. As an assassin, I could actually outrace most normal mounts by quaffing a speed potion, which was sad. To go any faster? Buy premium mounts.
Interface is odd. Auction house is the most egregious example. You can't even use the search bar, leaving you to slowly search through pages upon pages of items before you find something you want.
All in all, I feel like I have to recommend trying it, just because I have the founder's title and I spent so long playing. It was entertaining for a while, but ultimately I set it down when I reached the end. Not much replayability once you get to max level - you'll never want to go through certain sections again, which makes making a new character a serious pain.

Ahhh Chroma Squad, where to begin... I know!
TL;DR
Chroma squad is a fantastic action startegy game with an in depth, self aware story. With a well written set of dialogue, and a surprisingly deep combat system Chroma Squad is sure to please strategy fans... even if you haven't seen power rangers!
Chroma Squad, in an depth action strategy game that never ceases to amaze me! With large a (and albeit, very obvious) inspiration from Sabans Power Ranger. Chroma Squad is a game that will make you want to relive your childhood... and at the same time want to destroy it. You see Chroma Squad's difficulty system can be changed on the fly for those of you who don't want to think... If you do enjoy a challenge however, play the game on hard mode (warning! PLAN ABOUT THREE STEPS AHEAD ON HARD). This game can, and will kick you in the rear so hard you won't remember what you planned to do afterwards.
Chroma Squad has a very (from what I have played) unique system called teamwork. This system allows your teamates to perform double, tiple, even quadruple attacks (similar fire emblem fates), but there is a catch... teamwork is the only way to use your finisher (a vital tool later on) , and can allow your team to move further on the set! Now you may be wondering what can make this game so difficult, IMO I believe Chroma Squad is one of the few games that got difficulty right. It doesn't just swarm you with hundreds of cheap, or extremely powerful enemies, atleast not in the beginning. Chroma Squad has a real sense of growth meaning that as you get stronger the game can and WILL adapt.
Mecha battles, this feature surprised me. when I had my first mecha battle I was pleasently surprised. Though simple the mecha battle can really make you question your "startegic genius" and really mke you pull your hair out if not careful.
To sum it up, this game seems very simple, and easy on your first run. That fact can be a lie, the game can be very challenging to the extreme on the harder difficulties, and the AI can be very ruthless and capitalize on every mistake you make. The premise is great, and the game has this atmosphere that I find hard to explain, but enjoy. The mecha battles are a nice break from the normal gameplay. Worth a buy. if you watched Power Rangers for sure!
My score: 5/5 (6/5 if you enjoyed Power Rangers as a child)

I'm going to own up to my bias here, I played this as a teenager but never finished it back on the ps2 days. I never knew all that happened but I got far enough that I was captivated by the world. Art design, atmosphere, world building, and the feel of it all is so sublime that I have trouble properly wording it.
While the design can get ludicrous at times, it's such a varied and unique style that I've never encountered another game that has produced this weird combination of celtic/germanic fantasy and japanese style. The music hits you the best with this combination as you'll be quick to notice that it loves the german language to induce a very nice mysterious atmosphere at key moments. The cinematics also show off how this is when CyberConnect2 really started to embrace their insane animation style. It is a an absolute joy to watch and it sucks there aren't more hand animated cutscenes. Finally, the changes they made really fized the pacing of these games. Each game back in the day took 20+ hours and now the whole series has been condensed with each part being a nice 10-15 hour experience. It really is the first series (dot hack in general not G.U.) that popularized the idea of making a story take place in a real game, and G.U. is the best the series has to offer.
It's not a perfect game, but I am begging you to give it a chance, If you don't like it, that is completely fine, but I see so much potential for this series and I hope more people can see why I love it.

Coming from a newcomer's perspective into the .Hack series, .Hack//G.U. last recode is the first game I’ve played in the series so from this perspective I would like to say if you are a newcomer .Hack//G.U. last recode is a great introduction to the PS2 underrated game series that hopefully can be reborn into today's market. That said this game comes with all 3 volume's for the .Hack//G.U. trilogy with an extended volume 4 that adds a liner 3 hour or so expansion onto the story of the trilogy that overall helped finalise and gave a satisfying conclusion to this 100 hour or so story of a MMORPG that is a single player game..... Huh.
Some great things that this game does is that the overall story and characters are all interesting with some that you will love while some you will hate (won't say any names) that will make you keep coming back to see what happens in this game. Speaking of game the gameplay itself seems to improve as you go through the volumes with new battle techniques  being introduced as the volumes go on and for the most part the combat is fun and has a very 'tales of' action feel to it but just not as refined.
However some things must be made apparent when dealing with .Hack//G.U. Last Recode as there are some cons I personally found with the game, the first thing is the keyboard control scheme seriously F.......k this default setup it is absolutely horrible and it doesn't help that the game's tutorial has only the Xbox controller prompts in the game so good luck finding out what A, X, B, Y, LB, LT ext. are because the game won't tell you that. But to be fair you can change the assigned key's in the options so that's a minor complaint I’m just warning anyone that plays this with a keyboard to find your own set-up like I had to.

Finally 100% completed this game, a lot because the awesome looking letter/pattern achievements that you can display in your showcase on your profile. Yes, I admit that was one of the reasons why I got the game in its first place. But behind all the letters and showcasing there is actually a nice little game, if not 100% when it comes to enjoyment. I will still reccomend it, though, it is a really good game that is not too expensive even when it's not on sale.
So what's the good things besides the achievements? The simple concept of connecting shapes, or dots if you want over all the letters in the alphabet  plus extra levels that changes every day (Daily), and a nice bonus that you can change the colour pallette of the background and the shapes. 25 levels per letter set will keep you entertained(or frustrated) throughout the hours, days, week... depending on how fast you complete. There are excellent guides however should you get stuck somewhere. Also, a huge plus for the silence; no annoying music, just the occasional sounds when you connect lines and makes it to the next level.
The only downside is the later letter sets when you get the same colour and shapes on every level, sometimes it gets a bit monotonous to do a lot at once. It's getting better once you are closer to the end, though.
Looking at both sides of the games, it is a really good one and well worth its price so get it whether it's on sale or not. Not much bad aside from above, either and if those would have had a bit more variety I would probably make huge shoutouts about getting it. Do get it however.

I want to love this game, for its quirkiness and unique setting (something reminding me of 1980s / 90s children's shows, Where the Wild Things Are, and a Spongebob-ish universe...) but beyond Lovely Weather We're Having providing for a few laughs at its strange settings, funny character designs (the dog that follows you around inparticular, with his goofy smile...) and some amusing dialog (including a character lamenting / loving being kicked in the face and asking you to do so again as it's the only thing he has in life, more or less..) the game does little to provide any direction where you are to go, which fits the game's somewhat nitrous oxide/innocuous feeling atmosphere, but doesn't make for a very engaging game experience overall.
This game's retail price of 7.99 is very high, once you realize that there isn't anything to the gameplay beyond wandering through the forests, fields, and neighborhoods and occassionally exchanging a few lines of dialog with one of a handful of NPCs. In the game's description it mentions the weather in the game reflecting your actual location, which I never saw much variety in, whether as a result of it being clear days here, having some kind of location service/recognition switched off (??) or just having not tried to "play" the game enough. All of that aside, as a feature, if that doesn't affect the gameplay beyond only an aesthetic change, I don't see it adding much value to the title overall, beyond a kind of cool visual 'app'/technology.
If the game at least made an effort to conveying some kind of narrative or sense of progression and wasn't quite so experimental / abstract of an experience (and had a lower price point in lieu of that..) then I might recommend it, but as-is, on sale, all-in-all it amounted to what I expected of it: Some funny / nice / weird settings, without much to do.

@Whimsicalrogue Check out my review of @BeholdStudio's Chroma Squad -- Five out of five stars.
But seriously, this is one of my favourite tactics RPGs of all time. It's more streamlined and casual-friendly, since there are fewer elements -- no experience points (just upgrades and equipment), no world map (just a main hub) and so on -- but it is still quite difficult on the highest difficulty setting.

Having played the demo of this game before, I honestly don't see a huge improvement.
One of my gripes with this game is how difficult it is to see what's going on around you.  Since bullets keep moving very quickly even if you're not moving, you don't really have time to glance around.  This leads to you getting shot in the back constantly, which is not helped by the level design.
Another source of frustration is how difficult it is to predict if a bullet will hit you.  I never understood exactly what my hitbox was, I was pretty much just praying whenever a bullet whizzed by.
These two issues combine to make the last level especially frustrating, as you restart over and over again and try to complete the level with the incomplete information you have.  I eventually cheesed it by hiding in a corner.  I have no shame.
I would add that making bullet trails the same colour as the enemies makes them hard to see.
The story is cute at first but quickly gets in the way, offering no real original idea.  The game seems to really revel in throwing its "mysteries" in your face.  I get it game developper, you think your story is really amazing and deep.  I don't really care, I just want to play.  This is compounded by the fact that the game never tells you when it's saving, so you might end up replaying levels and sitting through those boring story bits again if you press ESC at the wrong time.
Seriously devs, the whole "meta commentary on how game devs really control the players" was done well 10 years ago in Bioshock, and has been beaten to death since then.  It's not clever, original or interesting.  Just let it go.  It's come to the piont where games like the Stanley Parable are parodying the concept.  When parodies start popping up like that, you might want to reconsider playing it straight. It's a good sign the trope is well known and no longer that interesting on its own.
Anyway, after you manage to make it through this torture, the game finally unlocks levels and endless mode, which is what it should have started with.  Unfotunately, by this point it has destroyed any good will it had.
Play the demo and skip this.

Το SUPERHOT είναι ένας ιδιαίτερος first-person shooter indie τίτλος της αυτοαποκαλούμενης SUPERHOT Team.Τι το κάνει να ξεχωρίζει από τα υπόλοιπα shooter?Ο χρόνος κυλάει μόνο όταν εσείς κινείστε.Κάθε παύση ισοδυναμεί με μια παύση στο χρόνο.Κάθε παύση ακινητοποιεί κάθε αντίπαλο και σου δίνει τη δυνατότητα να καταστρώσετε ένα πλάνο εξόντωσης για τον καθένα ξεχωριστά,πολλαπλές φορές ανάλογα με τις κινήσεις τους.
Η ιστορία ξεκινάει με τον πρωταγωνιστή σερφάροντας στον υπολογιστή μέχρι που ένας φίλος  προτείνει ένα παιχνίδι εικονικής πραγματικότητας(VR). Εντυπωσιασμένος από την κριτική του,ο παίκτης αποφασίζει να ρίξει μια ματιά στο περιεχόμενο του παιχνιδιού.
Το παιχνίδι χωρίζεται σε διάφορα levels,μέσα από τα οποία ο παίκτης χάνεται όλο και περισσότερο στον κόσμο του Superhot.Όσο περισσότερο εθίζεται,τόσο μεγαλύτερα ερωτήματα δημιουργούνται.
Το Gameplay είναι σχετικά απλό,ο παίκτης μπορεί να πάρει αντικείμενα και όπλα τα οποία θα τον βοηθήσουν να εξοντώσει τους εχθρούς του.Με την παύση του χρόνου,κάθε επίπεδο μπορεί να ολοκληρωθεί διαφορετικά κάθε φορά.
Δυστυχώς,το campaign διαρκεί το πολύ δύο ώρες.Όμως,μετά την ολοκλήρωση του παιχνιδιού ξεκλειδώνονται δύο νέα modes,το endless και το challenges.
Το endless είναι ένα σύνολο επιπέδων στα οποία  ο παίκτης μπορεί να ολοκληρώσει κάποιες προκλήσεις ή να παίζει ασταμάτητα επιτυγχάνοντας συνεχώς μεγαλύτερο high score.
Αντίθετα,το challenges είναι η επανάληψη όλων των campaign levels με διάφορους περιορισμούς.Ωστόσο,το γεγονός ότι οι περιορισμοί είναι πάνω στα ίδια levels του campaign θυμίζει περισσότερο new game+ παρά κάτι ξεχωριστό.
Παράλληλα όλοι οι παίκτες μπορούν να ανεβάσουν τα πιο τρελά  replays τους στο site της SUPERHOT team, έρχοντας έτσι σε επαφή με τα υπόλοιπα μέλη του SUPERHOT.
Ο κόσμος του Superhot είναι μινιμαλιστικά σχεδιασμένος για να ταιριάζει με το ψηφιακό concept.Η παλέτα χρωμάτων περιέχει αποχρώσεις του λευκού και του μαύρου, καθώς και του κόκκινου το οποίο χαρακτηρίζει τους αντιπάλους.Ο αλλόκοτος κόσμος σε συνδιασμό με την έλλειψη soundtracks κάνει την ατμόσφαιρα τόσο ψυχρή όσο και ανατριχιαστική.
Σε γενικές γραμμές το SUPERHOT είναι μια έξυπνη ιδέα που εκτελέστηκε πολύ βιαστικά.Οι δημιουργοί θα μπορούσαν κάλλιστα να εμπλουτίσουν όχι μόνο την ιστορία αλλά και τα επιπλέον modes.Παρόλα αυτά προτείνεται σε όλους  όσους θέλουν ένα γρήγορο παιχνιδάκι,σε περίοδο μεγάλων εκπτώσεων.

No Time to Explain Remastered is a platformer by tinyBuild games, and for their first game it's pretty damn good.
Level design is excellent, challenging but still fun. Stages often have their own gimmicks, this keeps the gameplay varied and interesting. The soundtrack is brilliant, and compliments the levels very well. The changes made from the original, particularly those regarding optimisation and controls, are definitely good ones; I run a rairly low-end computer and had lag issues in some sections of the original, all fixed this version. Controls are simple and intuitive, and while different characters will have different methods of getting around, the game does a good job of teaching you how to use them. I found the story to be highly amusing; I won't spoil it here but everything that happens is just so unexpected and ridiculous, it had me laughing out loud more than once.
Overall, No Time to Explain sets out to be a funny, original platformer, and it succeeded.

**A bit of a mixed review but altogether I do recommend**
While making this review I had 7hrs played on The Long Dark. This time was enough to experience the first map fully. Exploring was great in the game and I give a big plus for that. The survival had a nice feeling as well. It took me a few hours of gameplay to even find the next map (which I have not explored fully yet). Overall for an early access game I was content with what I got and enjoyed it. It comes with a wide variety of playstyles so if you don't like as much of a challenge don't worry! Plus for only $20 you can get a lot of hours on this game which makes it very worth it in my opinion. All together If you like survival games, especially ones that challenge you, you're bound to like this game.
Now my complaints/suggestions
Because this game is early access I don't exactly know what they have planned for the game so some of these things they may be trying to fix or add.
-All around a bit more content. Even though it is sandbox mode there should be small objectives that people want to get to help their survival. It would be really interesting to see a way to get power for the main shelters. A way to move slightly faster by crafting snowshoes. Crafting in general just seems a bit bland. Although they want the game to be challenging, you should also be able to craft things to make living a bit easier as you play.
-Because of the lack of crafting new things I feel like it makes survival tedious. You don't really have new ways to get food or make a shelters better so you're stuck doing the same things.
-Lastly the biggest complaint would have to be how long we have waited for story mode. If you are looking for the story mode I'd say wait until it leaves early access (which could be a long time from now.) Otherwise you only have sandbox mode and some challenge modes.

Limbo is a beautifully stylistic and well-made puzzle platformer. The silent and bleak atmosphere is expressed very well and the movement feels natural. It’s a very relaxing and ambient game, and However, I did have my problems with the game.
Gameplay
Limbo is a puzzle platformer, but neither part was exceptional. The platforming is mostly bland, and, even with the introduction of new and interesting features, still seemed lacking for the most part. The main character is slow and cannot sprint, making getting from point to point tedious and boring, especially with the music-less bleak scenery and atmosphere. The puzzles themselves aren't that difficult, but they are tedious and require a lot of waiting usually. Waiting for the bolder to roll, waiting for the light to swing back, waiting for the platform to move, etc. Everything just moves so slow in this game.
In addition, you die a lot. This isn't bad considering the theme and mood of the game, but its irritating in relation to the puzzles.  Although the respawn points are very generous with their frequency, the puzzles are slow and repeating the same puzzle multiple times can be frustrating. There’s a lot of auto scroll or waiting on things out of your control, and often can be failed in a simple mistake, making repeating the puzzle multiple times feel boring and unnecessary when you already know what to do.
Story
There’s not much of a story to this game, which is okay since the game is about Limbo, but for most of the game there isn't much drive to continue moving forward outside of finishing the game. The highlight of the game is the first third, where a giant spider is pursuing the character. This spider is threatening, brutal, and scary. It gives a lot of tension to the game, and really pushes the player forward to escape from it, but it is only present in the first third, and the rest of the game you are just wandering forward any real overarching threat or goal, and it just makes it less interesting.
By no means is this a bad game. It’s a cheap, short, interesting game that does its unique aspects well, and I don’t regret taking the time to play through it, but at the same time I didn’t find anything really special about it that makes it stand out as a game other than its cool atmosphere and style. Is it worth the price, yeah? Did I find it that enjoyable, not really.
